knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-stage conditional risk mapping with coherent axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage specialization from \(\mathcal Z_2\) to \(\mathcal Z_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(\rho:\mathcal Z_2\to\mathcal Z_1\) is a conditional risk mapping if, for every \(Z,Z'\in\mathcal Z_2\), it satisfies \[\rho(\alpha Z+(1-\alpha)Z')\preccurlyeq\alpha\rho(Z)+(1-\alpha)\rho(Z')\quad\forall\alpha\in[0,1],\] \[Z\succcurlyeq Z'\Longrightarrow\rho(Z)\succcurlyeq\rho(Z'),\] \[\rho(Z+Y)=\rho(Z)+Y\quad\forall Y\in\mathcal Z_1,\] and \[\rho(\alpha Z)=\alpha\rho(Z)\quad\forall\alpha\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-stage conditional risk mapping is convex, monotone, translation equivariant for first-stage quantities, and positively homogeneous.
assumptions_latex: \rho:\mathcal Z_2\to\mathcal Z_1
Z,Z'\in\mathcal Z_2
Y\in\mathcal Z_1
\alpha\in[0,1]\text{ for convexity}
\alpha\geq0\text{ for positive homogeneity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\text{ satisfies convexity, monotonicity, translation equivariance, and positive homogeneity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional risk mapping with coherent axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General stage-to-stage formulation; the four extracted axioms are the coherent-risk axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(\rho_{t+1}:\mathcal Z_{t+1}\to\mathcal Z_t\) is a conditional risk mapping if, for every \(Z,Z'\in\mathcal Z_{t+1}\), it satisfies \[\rho_{t+1}(\alpha Z+(1-\alpha)Z')\preccurlyeq\alpha\rho_{t+1}(Z)+(1-\alpha)\rho_{t+1}(Z')\quad\forall\alpha\in[0,1],\] \[Z\succcurlyeq Z'\Longrightarrow\rho_{t+1}(Z)\succcurlyeq\rho_{t+1}(Z'),\] \[\rho_{t+1}(Z+Y)=\rho_{t+1}(Z)+Y\quad\forall Y\in\mathcal Z_t,\] and \[\rho_{t+1}(\alpha Z)=\alpha\rho_{t+1}(Z)\quad\forall\alpha\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stagewise conditional risk mapping is convex, monotone, translation equivariant for current-stage quantities, and positively homogeneous.
assumptions_latex: \rho_{t+1}:\mathcal Z_{t+1}\to\mathcal Z_t
Z,Z'\in\mathcal Z_{t+1}
Y\in\mathcal Z_t
\alpha\in[0,1]\text{ for convexity}
\alpha\geq0\text{ for positive homogeneity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_{t+1}\text{ satisfies convexity, monotonicity, translation equivariance, and positive homogeneity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness of measurable randomized relaxation under a monotone risk measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that measurable randomization does not improve the risk value beyond applying the risk measure to the pointwise infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal Z=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F,P) and \mathfrak M=L_{p'}(\Omega,\mathcal F,P;\mathbb R^n), where p,p'\in[1,+\infty], and let \mathfrak M_X be the admissible measurable decisions. Let \rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R} be a proper risk measure satisfying monotonicity (R2), and suppose \Psi:=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\in\mathcal Z. If \rho is continuous at \Psi, then \inf_{\chi\in\mathfrak M_X}\rho(F_\chi)=\rho\!\left(\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For admissible measurable decision rules, a proper monotone risk measure that is continuous at the pointwise best outcome assigns the randomized relaxation the same infimum as the risk of that pointwise infimum.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal Z=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F,P),\quad \mathfrak M=L_{p'}(\Omega,\mathcal F,P;\mathbb R^n)
p,p'\in[1,+\infty]
\rho:\mathcal Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper and satisfies monotonicity (R2)}
\Psi:=\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\in\mathcal Z
\rho\text{ is continuous at }\Psi
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{\chi\in\mathfrak M_X}\rho(F_\chi)=\rho\!\left(\inf_{x\in X}F(x)\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional-expectation representation of a conditional risk mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation under a countably atomic conditioning sigma-algebra; the defining construction of the associated family \(\mathfrak C\) is outside this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z_i=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F_i,P)\), \(i=1,2\), with \(\mathcal F_1\subset\mathcal F_2\), and let \(\rho:\mathcal Z_2\to\mathcal Z_1\) be a conditional risk mapping. If \(\mathcal F_1\) has countably many elementary events, then, for the associated family \(\mathfrak C\) of probability measures on \((\Omega,\mathcal F_2)\) corresponding to a probability distribution \(v\) on \((\Omega,\mathcal F_1)\), \[\rho(Z)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathfrak C}\mathbb E_\mu[Z\mid\mathcal F_1]\qquad\forall Z\in\mathcal Z_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the conditioning sigma-algebra has countably many elementary events, the conditional risk mapping is the supremum of conditional expectations over its associated family of probability measures.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal Z_i=L_p(\Omega,\mathcal F_i,P),\quad i=1,2
\mathcal F_1\subset\mathcal F_2
\rho:\mathcal Z_2\to\mathcal Z_1\text{ is a conditional risk mapping}
\mathcal F_1\text{ has countably many elementary events}
\mathfrak C\text{ is the associated family described by the preceding source construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(Z)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathfrak C}\mathbb E_\mu[Z\mid\mathcal F_1]\quad\forall Z\in\mathcal Z_2.

children.title: Conditional Monetary Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: The monetary conditional class underlying scalar dynamic risk evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Monetary Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost convention for one-step conditional monetary risk evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, let \(\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F\), and let \(\mathcal X\subseteq L^0(\mathcal F)\) contain \(L^0(\mathcal G)\) and be closed under their addition. A conditional monetary risk mapping is a map \(\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal X\to L^0(\mathcal G)\) satisfying monotonicity and conditional cash invariance: \[X\leq Y\ \text{a.s.}\Longrightarrow\rho_{\mathcal G}(X)\leq\rho_{\mathcal G}(Y)\ \text{a.s.},\qquad \rho_{\mathcal G}(X+m)=\rho_{\mathcal G}(X)+m\] for every \(X,Y\in\mathcal X\) and \(m\in L^0(\mathcal G)\) for which \(X+m\in\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional monetary risk mapping is monotone in losses and shifts exactly by any currently measurable cash amount.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F\) is a sub-\(\sigma\)-algebra.
\(\mathcal X\) is stable under admissible additions from \(L^0(\mathcal G)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathcal G}\) is monotone and conditionally cash invariant.

notation.meaning: Almost-sure equivalence classes of finite, real-valued, \(\mathcal G\)-measurable random variables.
Conditional risk mapping under information \(\mathcal G\), using the loss convention.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard loss-convention definition of a conditional monetary risk mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The loss-convention definition is mathematically standard and fits the definition container, but no inspectable citation supports the convention or domain formulation.

children.title: Conditional Convex Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Nonhomogeneous conditional risk mappings with convex dual representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Convex Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convexity with random, currently measurable mixing weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conditional monetary risk mapping \(\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal X\to L^0(\mathcal G)\) is conditionally convex if, whenever \(X,Y\in\mathcal X\) and \(\lambda\in L^0(\mathcal G)\) satisfies \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\) almost surely with \(\lambda X+(1-\lambda)Y\in\mathcal X\), \[\rho_{\mathcal G}\bigl(\lambda X+(1-\lambda)Y\bigr)\leq \lambda\rho_{\mathcal G}(X)+(1-\lambda)\rho_{\mathcal G}(Y)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Thus diversification selected using information \(\mathcal G\) cannot have greater assessed risk than the corresponding conditional mixture of assessed risks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional convexity permits random mixing weights known at the evaluation time and rewards diversification under each information state.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_{\mathcal G}\) is a conditional monetary risk mapping.
\(\mathcal X\) is closed under the displayed conditional mixtures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathcal G}(\lambda X+(1-\lambda)Y)\leq\lambda\rho_{\mathcal G}(X)+(1-\lambda)\rho_{\mathcal G}(Y)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: A \(\mathcal G\)-measurable mixing weight taking values in \([0,1]\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition using conditional random convex combinations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-convexity definition and content kind fit the leaf, but the random-weight formulation has no cited authoritative source or locator.

children.title: Conditional Coherent Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Positively homogeneous conditional mappings with risk-envelope representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Coherent Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional coherence in the loss convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conditional monetary risk mapping \(\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal X\to L^0(\mathcal G)\) is conditionally coherent if it is conditionally convex and conditionally positively homogeneous: for every \(X\in\mathcal X\) and every nonnegative \(a\in L^0(\mathcal G)\) with \(aX\in\mathcal X\), \[\rho_{\mathcal G}(aX)=a\rho_{\mathcal G}(X)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Equivalently, conditional convexity and positive homogeneity imply conditional subadditivity, \(\rho_{\mathcal G}(X+Y)\leq\rho_{\mathcal G}(X)+\rho_{\mathcal G}(Y)\), whenever all terms belong to the domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional coherent mapping is monetary, conditionally convex, and homogeneous under nonnegative scales observable at the evaluation time.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_{\mathcal G}\) is conditionally monetary and convex.
\(\mathcal X\) is stable under the displayed scaling and addition operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathcal G}\) is conditionally positively homogeneous and subadditive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated conditional coherence axioms are standard and appropriately classified as a definition, but the equivalence with conditional subadditivity and its domain conditions require an inspectable source.

children.title: Conditional Tail-Risk Mapping Families
children.top_down_role: Conditional tail-sensitive families and their compatibility with recursive evaluation.

children.title: Conditional Quantile Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Conditional quantile-based evaluations across information stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Quantile Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower conditional quantile of a loss at level \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in L^0(\mathcal F)\), let \(\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F\), and fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). The conditional quantile risk mapping is the conditional value-at-risk \[\operatorname{VaR}_{\alpha}(X\mid\mathcal G):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}\left\{m\in L^0(\mathcal G):\mathbb P(X\leq m\mid\mathcal G)\geq\alpha\ \text{a.s.}\right\}.\] It is a \(\mathcal G\)-measurable version of the lower conditional \(\alpha\)-quantile. The essential infimum convention fixes the value when the conditional distribution has atoms or a nonunique quantile interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional value-at-risk is the smallest currently measurable threshold exceeded by the loss with conditional probability at most one minus alpha.
assumptions_latex: A regular conditional distribution, or equivalently the displayed conditional-probability predicates, is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{VaR}_{\alpha}(X\mid\mathcal G)\) is the lower conditional \(\alpha\)-quantile of \(X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard essential-infimum definition of conditional value-at-risk

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits a definition container, but the essential-infimum convention, existence of a measurable conditional quantile, and treatment of atoms require a specific authoritative citation. Conditional-probability predicates do not themselves require a regular conditional distribution, so that claimed equivalence also needs confirmation or correction.

children.title: Conditional Spectral Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Conditional weighted-tail evaluations across information stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Spectral Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional quantile mixture for integrable losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F)\), let \(q_u(X\mid\mathcal G)\) denote its lower conditional \(u\)-quantile, and let \(\phi:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)\) be measurable, nondecreasing, and satisfy \(\int_0^1\phi(u)\,du=1\). Provided the integral is finite, the conditional spectral risk mapping generated by \(\phi\) is \[\rho_{\phi,\mathcal G}(X):=\int_0^1 q_u(X\mid\mathcal G)\phi(u)\,du.\] The integral is evaluated pointwise up to almost-sure equality and produces a \(\mathcal G\)-measurable random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional spectral risk mapping averages conditional loss quantiles using normalized weights that increase toward worse outcomes.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F)\) and the displayed integral is finite almost surely.
\(\phi\geq0\) is nondecreasing and has unit integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\phi,\mathcal G}(X)\in L^0(\mathcal G)\) is the \(\phi\)-weighted conditional quantile average.

notation.meaning: Lower conditional quantile of the loss at level \(u\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard loss-oriented conditional spectral-risk formula

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral formula fits the leaf and definition role, but pointwise conditional quantiles must admit a jointly measurable version in the quantile level and outcome before the integral is justified. The necessary measurability and integrability regime needs authoritative support.

children.title: Recursive Compatibility of Tail-Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries for composing tail-sensitive mappings over time.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Compatibility of Tail-Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong recursive compatibility for terminal-loss mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) be a filtration and let \(\rho_t:\mathcal X_T\to L^0(\mathcal F_t)\) be conditional tail-risk mappings in the loss convention. The family is recursively compatible if, for every \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\) and \(X\in\mathcal X_T\), \[\rho_s(X)=\rho_s\bigl(\rho_t(X)\bigr)\quad\text{a.s.}\] whenever the composition is defined. Equivalently, an intermediate risk assessment may replace the terminal loss without changing any earlier assessment. Conditional quantile or spectral formulas applied independently at each date need not satisfy this identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursive compatibility means replacing a terminal loss by any later risk assessment leaves every earlier assessment unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) is a filtration.
The domains are stable under the displayed compositions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_s=\rho_s\circ\rho_t\) on \(\mathcal X_T\) for every \(s\leq t\).

notation.meaning: Admissible terminal losses measurable at time \(T\).
Risk assessment conditional on information \(\mathcal F_t\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard strong time-consistency recursion under the loss convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind condition fits recursive compatibility, but the sign-dependent recursion convention and the claim that independently applied conditional quantile or spectral mappings may fail it require a specific source and locator.

children.title: Preference-Induced Conditional Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Conditional nonlinear evaluations induced by exponential or utility-based preferences.

children.title: Conditional Entropic Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Conditional exponential-preference evaluations in dynamic settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Entropic Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential certainty equivalent for losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F\), let \(\gamma>0\), and let \(X\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[\exp(\gamma X)\mid\mathcal G]<\infty\) almost surely. The conditional entropic risk mapping with risk-aversion parameter \(\gamma\) is \[\rho_{\gamma,\mathcal G}(X):=\frac{1}{\gamma}\log\mathbb E\!\left[\exp(\gamma X)\mid\mathcal G\right].\] It is \(\mathcal G\)-measurable, monotone, conditionally cash invariant, and conditionally convex. For \(m\in L^0(\mathcal G)\) with finite expressions, \(\rho_{\gamma,\mathcal G}(X+m)=\rho_{\gamma,\mathcal G}(X)+m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional entropic risk is the logarithmic conditional exponential moment of loss, scaled by inverse risk aversion.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[e^{\gamma X}\mid\mathcal G]\) is finite almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\gamma,\mathcal G}(X)=\gamma^{-1}\log\mathbb E[e^{\gamma X}\mid\mathcal G]\) defines a conditional convex monetary risk mapping.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conditional entropic-risk definition and elementary properties

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entropic formula and stated monetary-convex properties are standard under the loss convention and fit a definition container, but no inspectable citation supports them or the operative domain.

children.title: Conditional Utility-Based Risk Mappings
children.top_down_role: Conditional evaluations induced by general utility preferences.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Utility-Based Risk Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional certainty equivalent generated by a loss preference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u:I\to\mathbb R\) be continuous and strictly increasing on an interval \(I\), and suppose \(X\) is \(I\)-valued with \(\mathbb E[|u(X)|\mid\mathcal G]<\infty\). If \(\mathbb E[u(X)\mid\mathcal G]\in u(I)\) almost surely, the conditional utility-based certainty-equivalent mapping is \[C_{u,\mathcal G}(X):=u^{-1}\!\left(\mathbb E[u(X)\mid\mathcal G]\right).\] It is \(\mathcal G\)-measurable and monotone. Interpreted for losses, convex \(u\) expresses aversion to dispersion; conditional cash invariance generally requires additional structure on \(u\), notably exponential or affine form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional utility-based mapping converts conditional expected transformed loss back through the inverse preference transform.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \(I\).
The conditional expectation is finite and lies in \(u(I)\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{u,\mathcal G}(X)=u^{-1}(\mathbb E[u(X)\mid\mathcal G])\) is a monotone conditional certainty equivalent.

notation.meaning: Strictly increasing preference transform on the loss domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certainty-equivalent construction fits the leaf, but its interpretation as a loss preference, the convex-transform dispersion claim, and the exponential-or-affine cash-invariance characterization require authoritative sourcing and precise domain qualifications.

children.title: Preference-Induced Recursion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Temporal regimes in which preference-induced mappings support recursive evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Preference-Induced Recursion Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tower recursion for a fixed preference transform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) be a filtration and let a single continuous strictly increasing transform \(u:I\to\mathbb R\) define \(C_t(X):=u^{-1}(\mathbb E[u(X)\mid\mathcal F_t])\). Whenever all expressions are finite and remain in their domains, the tower property yields \[C_s(C_t(X))=C_s(X)\quad\text{a.s. for every }0\leq s\leq t\leq T.\] Thus a common transform across dates generates recursive certainty equivalents. Date-dependent transforms do not generally retain this recursion unless their conditional certainty-equivalent operators satisfy the same composition identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using one preference transform at every date makes conditional certainty equivalents recursive; changing transforms can destroy that compatibility.
assumptions_latex: The same continuous strictly increasing transform \(u\) is used at every date.
All conditional expectations and inverse transforms are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_s\circ C_t=C_s\) for every \(s\leq t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: recursion follows from the conditional-expectation tower identity for a common transform

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The common-transform recursion is mathematically consistent with the tower property and property is an appropriate content kind. A source is still required for this recursion regime and especially for the stated failure boundary with date-dependent transforms.

children.title: Dynamic Risk-Evaluation Domains
children.top_down_role: Objects on which dynamic risk evaluation is defined.

children.title: Terminal-Position Risk Systems
children.top_down_role: Dynamic evaluation of a terminal random position through intermediate information.

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal-Position Risk Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic assessment of one terminal loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) be a filtered probability space and let \(\mathcal X_T\subseteq L^0(\mathcal F_T)\) be a class of terminal losses. A terminal-position risk system is a family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) with \[\rho_t:\mathcal X_T\longrightarrow L^0(\mathcal F_t),\qquad t=0,\ldots,T.\] For each terminal loss \(X\), the random variable \(\rho_t(X)\) is its assessment using information available at time \(t\). If each \(\rho_t\) is monetary, convex, or coherent, the system inherits that corresponding pointwise classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal-position system assigns an information-adapted risk assessment at every date to the same terminal loss.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) is a filtration.
\(\mathcal X_T\subseteq L^0(\mathcal F_T)\) is the common terminal-loss domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\rho_t(X))_{t=0}^T\) is adapted for every \(X\in\mathcal X_T\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard domain-and-codomain definition of a dynamic terminal-position risk system

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The family-of-maps formulation fits the terminal-position definition container, but no cited source establishes this terminology, domain convention, or inherited classification.

children.title: Adapted Cost-Stream Risk Systems
children.top_down_role: Dynamic evaluation of adapted streams across multiple stages.

children.title: Cash-Flow Risk Systems
children.top_down_role: Dynamic risk evaluation of adapted payment streams.

knowledge_statements.title: Cash-Flow Risk Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic risk evaluation of remaining adapted cash flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) be a filtration and let \(\mathcal C\) be a class of adapted real-valued cash-flow streams \(C=(C_0,\ldots,C_T)\). A cash-flow risk system is a family \((R_t)_{t=0}^T\) with \[R_t:\mathcal C\longrightarrow L^0(\mathcal F_t),\] such that \(R_t(C)\) depends only on the remaining stream \((C_t,\ldots,C_T)\). Under the loss convention, current cash invariance is \[R_t(C+m e_t)=R_t(C)+m\] for every admissible \(m\in L^0(\mathcal F_t)\), where \(e_t\) places its argument only at date \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cash-flow risk system evaluates each remaining adapted payment stream and shifts by any currently known payment added today.
assumptions_latex: \(C=(C_0,\ldots,C_T)\) is adapted.
The stream domain is stable under admissible additions \(m e_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_t(C)\in L^0(\mathcal F_t)\), depends only on \((C_t,\ldots,C_T)\), and is current-cash invariant.

notation.meaning: Unit cash-flow stream concentrated at date \(t\).
Time-\(t\) risk of the remaining cash flow.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard process-domain extension of conditional monetary risk

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record is appropriately a definition, but whether tail locality and current-cash invariance are defining requirements, and the sign used for a payment added at time t, depend on the selected cash-flow convention and require a domain-specific source.

children.title: Cost-Process Risk Systems
children.top_down_role: Dynamic risk evaluation of stagewise cost processes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Process Risk Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapted risk process generated from an adapted cost process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=(Z_0,\ldots,Z_T)\) be an adapted cost process in a domain \(\mathcal Z\). A cost-process risk system is an operator \(\mathfrak R\) assigning to each \(Z\in\mathcal Z\) an adapted assessment process \[\mathfrak R(Z)=\bigl(\mathfrak R_0(Z),\ldots,\mathfrak R_T(Z)\bigr),\qquad \mathfrak R_t(Z)\in L^0(\mathcal F_t),\] where \(\mathfrak R_t(Z)\) depends only on costs from date \(t\) onward. It is normalized if \(\mathfrak R_t(0)=0\), and monotone if \(Z_s\leq Z'_s\) almost surely for every \(s\geq t\) implies \(\mathfrak R_t(Z)\leq\mathfrak R_t(Z')\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cost-process system converts each adapted future cost process into an adapted process of date-by-date risk assessments.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is an adapted cost process.
Each component uses only the cost tail beginning at its evaluation date.

children.title: Stream Aggregation Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Stream Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines recursive aggregation of an adapted finite-horizon cost stream.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a filtered probability space with horizon \(T\), a stream aggregation regime is a family of maps \(A_t:\prod_{s=t}^T L^p(\mathcal F_s)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\). It is recursive when there are conditional one-step aggregators \(\varphi_t:L^p(\mathcal F_t)\times L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) such that \(A_T(C_T)=C_T\) and \(A_t(C_t,\ldots,C_T)=\varphi_t(C_t,A_{t+1}(C_{t+1},\ldots,C_T))\) for \(t<T\). A monotone regime additionally satisfies \(C_s\le D_s\) for every \(s\ge t\) only if \(A_t(C_t,\ldots,C_T)\le A_t(D_t,\ldots,D_T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stream regime recursively converts future adapted costs into a current measurable value, with monotonicity preserving componentwise cost order.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) is a filtered probability space.
\(1\le p\le\infty\), and every stream component belongs to the indicated \(L^p\) space.

children.title: Policy-Dependent Risk Evaluation

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Dependent Risk Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluates controlled costs under the filtration and probability law induced by a policy.

The policy-dependent risk evaluation at time \(t\) is \(J_t(\pi)=\rho_t^\pi(C_t^\pi,\ldots,C_T^\pi)\in L^p(\mathcal F_t^\pi)\). Both the cost stream and the conditional law used by \(\rho_t^\pi\) may depend on \(\pi\). Policies are compared at time \(t\) by the almost-sure order of \(J_t(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is evaluated by applying conditional risk to the costs, information, and probability law generated by that policy.

\(C_s^\pi\in L^p(\mathcal F_s^\pi)\) for \(s=t,\ldots,T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Scenario-Tree Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nodewise form of conditional dynamic risk on a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N_t\) be the nodes at depth \(t\) of a finite scenario tree, and let \(\operatorname{ch}(n)\) denote the children of \(n\in\mathcal N_t\). Every \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable value is constant on each node, so a one-step conditional risk map is represented by node maps \(r_n:\mathbb R^{\operatorname{ch}(n)}\to\mathbb R\) through \((\rho_t Z)(\omega)=r_n((Z_m)_{m\in\operatorname{ch}(n)})\) for \(\omega\in n\). A recursive cost evaluation satisfies \(V_n=C_n+r_n((V_m)_{m\in\operatorname{ch}(n)})\) at nonterminal nodes and \(V_n=C_n\) at terminal nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite scenario tree, conditional risk is a nodewise function of child values, yielding a backward recursion.

children.title: General Filtered Probability Regime

knowledge_statements.title: General Filtered Probability Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines dynamic monetary risk on a general discrete-time filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a filtered probability space, a general filtered dynamic monetary risk regime is a family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) with \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) such that, for all terminal positions \(X,Y\) and all \(m\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), \(X\le Y\) implies \(\rho_t(X)\ge\rho_t(Y)\), and \(\rho_t(X+m)=\rho_t(X)-m\). It is normalized when \(\rho_t(0)=0\), and local when \(\rho_t(1_A X)=1_A\rho_t(X)\) for every \(A\in\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filtered dynamic monetary risk measure maps terminal positions to current measurable capital requirements and obeys monotonicity and conditional cash invariance.

children.title: Markov Risk Regime

knowledge_statements.title: Markov Risk Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines conditional risk recursion depending only on the current Markov state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X_t)_{t=0}^T\) be a controlled Markov process with action \(U_t\), transition kernel \(P_t(\cdot\mid x,u)\), and stage cost \(c_t(x,u)\). A Markov risk regime consists of transition risk mappings \(\sigma_t(v,x,u)\) whose value depends on the future function \(v\) only through its distribution under \(P_t(\cdot\mid x,u)\). For a fixed Markov policy \(\mu\), its value functions satisfy \(V_T^\mu(x)=c_T(x)\) and \(V_t^\mu(x)=c_t(x,\mu_t(x))+\sigma_t(V_{t+1}^\mu,x,\mu_t(x))\). Thus no pre-\(t\) history enters the recursion beyond \(X_t=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Markov risk recursion evaluates future value using only the current state, selected action, and corresponding transition law.
assumptions_latex: \((X_t)\) is a controlled Markov process with measurable transition kernels.
The displayed costs and value functions lie in the domains of the transition risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t^\mu(x)=c_t(x,\mu_t(x))+\sigma_t(V_{t+1}^\mu,x,\mu_t(x))\).

children.title: History-Dependent Risk Regime

knowledge_statements.title: History-Dependent Risk Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines dynamic risk evaluation on full observable histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t=0,\ldots,T\), let \(H_t=(X_0,U_0,\ldots,U_{t-1},X_t)\) be the observable history. A history-dependent risk regime is a family of measurable transition risk mappings \(\sigma_t(\cdot,H_t,U_t)\) for which a policy \(\pi\) has recursion \(V_T^\pi(H_T)=c_T(H_T)\) and \(V_t^\pi(H_t)=c_t(H_t,\pi_t(H_t))+\sigma_t(V_{t+1}^\pi,H_t,\pi_t(H_t))\). The regime is genuinely history-dependent when no measurable function of the nominal state \(X_t\) alone represents \(V_t^\pi(H_t)\) for all admissible histories and policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History-dependent risk uses the observable path when the nominal current state is not sufficient for conditional evaluation.
assumptions_latex: Policies are nonanticipative measurable functions of observable histories.
Costs and transition risk mappings are measurable on their history spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Acceptance-Set Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents conditional monetary risk by its time-indexed acceptance set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to\overline L^0(\mathcal F_t)\) be monotone and conditionally cash invariant, and define \(\mathcal A_t=\{X\in L^p(\mathcal F_T):\rho_t(X)\le0\}\). Then the conditional acceptance-set representation is \[\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}\{m\in L^p(\mathcal F_t):X+m\in\mathcal A_t\}.\] Conversely, if \(\mathcal A_t\) is monotone and the displayed essential infimum is well defined, this formula defines a monotone, conditionally cash-invariant risk functional. For \(t<s\), stepped acceptance sets restrict acceptable positions to \(L^p(\mathcal F_s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional risk equals the least current measurable capital addition that makes a terminal position acceptable.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t\) is monotone and satisfies \(\rho_t(X+m)=\rho_t(X)-m\).
The essential infimum is well defined in \(\overline L^0(\mathcal F_t)\).

children.title: Conditional Penalty-Function Representation

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Penalty-Function Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust dual representation of a conditionally convex monetary risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_t:L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\to L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\) be normalized, conditionally convex, monotone, cash invariant, and continuous from above. Then \[\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_t}\left(E_Q[-X\mid\mathcal F_t]-\alpha_t^{\min}(Q)\right),\] where \(\mathcal Q_t=\{Q\ll P:Q=P\text{ on }\mathcal F_t\}\) and \[\alpha_t^{\min}(Q)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{X\in\mathcal A_t}E_Q[-X\mid\mathcal F_t].\] The minimal penalty is time-\(t\) measurable and assigns each conditional model the least penalty compatible with \(\rho_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional convex risk is the worst penalized conditional expected loss over models agreeing with the reference law on current information.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t:L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\to L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\) is normalized, conditionally convex, monotone, and cash invariant.
\(\rho_t\) is continuous from above.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional envelope representation of a coherent monetary risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_t:L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\to L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\) be a conditionally coherent monetary risk functional with the Fatou property. Its conditional risk envelope is a set \(\mathcal Z_t\) of nonnegative densities satisfying \(E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]=1\). The envelope representation is \[\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Z\in\mathcal Z_t}E[-ZX\mid\mathcal F_t].\] Conversely, any nonempty conditionally convex set \(\mathcal Z_t\) with these density properties defines through the displayed formula a monotone, cash-invariant, conditionally sublinear risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional coherent risk is the worst conditional expected loss over an envelope of normalized nonnegative densities.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Prior Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_t:L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\to L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\) be conditionally coherent and have the Fatou property. knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Pasting Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability condition allowing conditional models to be pasted at an information time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\mathcal Q\) of measures absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\) is stable under conditional pasting at time \(t\) if, for every \(Q_1,Q_2\in\mathcal Q\), the measure \(Q_1\otimes_t Q_2\) defined by \[E_{Q_1\otimes_t Q_2}[X\mid\mathcal F_t]=E_{Q_1}[E_{Q_2}[X\mid\mathcal F_t]\mid\mathcal F_t]\] for bounded \(X\), equivalently by the density \[Z^{Q_1\otimes_t Q_2}=Z_t^{Q_1}\frac{Z_T^{Q_2}}{Z_t^{Q_2}},\] belongs to \(\mathcal Q\), whenever the density ratio is defined. Conditional-pasting compatibility requires this property at every evaluation time.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Process Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents successive evaluations of a terminal position as an adapted risk process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a dynamic monetary risk family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) and a terminal position \(X\in L^p(\mathcal F_T)\), its risk process is the adapted process \(R^X=(R_t^X)_{t=0}^T\) defined by \[R_t^X=\rho_t(X),\qquad t=0,\ldots,T.\] For an adapted cost stream \(C=(C_s)_{s=0}^T\), the remaining-cost risk process is \[R_t^C=\rho_t\!\left(-\sum_{s=t}^T C_s\right).\] Each \(R_t^X\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable; if \(\rho_T(X)=-X\), then \(R_T^X=-X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk process records at every time the conditional risk of a terminal position or of the remaining cost stream.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) is defined for every \(t\).
The terminal position or cumulative remaining cost belongs to \(L^p(\mathcal F_T)\).

children.title: Supermartingale Representation

knowledge_statements.title: Supermartingale Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time Doob representation of a dynamic risk process under a fixed probability measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,Q)\) be a filtered probability space, and let \(R_t^X:=\rho_t(X)\) be integrable for every \(t\). The risk process has a \(Q\)-supermartingale representation precisely when \(R_s^X\geq E_Q[R_t^X\mid\mathcal F_s]\) for \(s\leq t\). Equivalently, there exist an integrable \(Q\)-martingale \(M^X\) and a predictable integrable increasing process \(A^X\), with \(A_0^X=0\), such that \[\rho_t(X)=M_t^X-A_t^X,\qquad 0\leq t\leq T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk process is a supermartingale exactly when it decomposes into a martingale minus a predictable increasing process.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\) and \(R_t^X\in L^1(Q)\) for every \(t\).
\((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) satisfies the usual discrete-time filtration conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^X\text{ is a }Q\text{-supermartingale}\iff R_t^X=M_t^X-A_t^X\).

notation.meaning: risk assigned at time t to terminal position X

children.title: Temporal Process Linkages

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Process Linkages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Links adjacent-date risk inequalities, arbitrary-date inequalities, and compensator increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integrable adapted risk process \(R_t^X:=\rho_t(X)\), the adjacent-date inequalities \[R_t^X\geq E_Q[R_{t+1}^X\mid\mathcal F_t],\qquad t<T,\] imply \(R_s^X\geq E_Q[R_t^X\mid\mathcal F_s]\) for every \(s\leq t\), by iterated conditional expectation. If \(R^X=M^X-A^X\) is its Doob decomposition, then \[R_s^X-E_Q[R_t^X\mid\mathcal F_s]=E_Q[A_t^X-A_s^X\mid\mathcal F_s]\geq0.\] Thus temporal risk deterioration is represented by expected compensator growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-step supermartingale inequalities propagate to every pair of dates, with each temporal gap equal to expected compensator growth.
assumptions_latex: \(R_t^X\in L^1(Q)\) for \(0\leq t\leq T\).
\(R^X=M^X-A^X\), where \(M^X\) is a \(Q\)-martingale and \(A^X\) is increasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_s^X-E_Q[R_t^X\mid\mathcal F_s]=E_Q[A_t^X-A_s^X\mid\mathcal F_s]\geq0\).
review_flags: source needed for intended risk-process correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adjacent-to-arbitrary-date implication and compensator identity are plausible, and property fits the leaf, but no cited source establishes this as the intended temporal risk-process linkage.

children.title: Time-Consistency Notions
children.top_down_role: Consistency concepts distinguished by the comparisons, acceptability judgments, or decisions they preserve.

children.title: Strong Time Consistency
children.top_down_role: The recursive order-preservation regime associated with dynamic programming.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Time Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive strong consistency for normalized conditional monetary risk measures on terminal losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) be normalized conditional monetary risk measures, interpreted on terminal net positions. The family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) is strongly time consistent if, for every \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\) and \(X\in L^p(\mathcal F_T)\), \[\rho_s(X)=\rho_s\!\left(-\rho_t(X)\right).\] Equivalently, replacing a position at time \(t\) by the \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable position whose value equals its assessed capital requirement does not change its earlier assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong time consistency requires every earlier risk assessment to equal the assessment obtained by recursively inserting the later capital requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(1\leq p\leq\infty\) and \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\).
\(\rho_t\) is normalized, monotone, and conditionally cash invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_s(X)=\rho_s(-\rho_t(X))\) for all \(X\) and \(s\leq t\).

notation.meaning: conditional monetary risk measure at time t

review_flags: authoritative locator for sign convention and equivalence needed

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive formula is a standard strong-time-consistency form under a loss/capital-requirement sign convention, and definition is appropriate, but an authoritative locator is required to verify that convention and the stated domain assumptions.

children.title: Weak Order-Based Consistency Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Weaker temporal compatibility based on selected order comparisons.

children.title: Weak Time Consistency
children.top_down_role: Restricted temporal compatibility weaker than full recursive consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Time Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-preservation form of weak temporal consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic assessment family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\), with \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), is weakly time consistent in the equality-preservation sense if, for all \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\) and \(X,Y\in L^p(\mathcal F_T)\), \[\rho_t(X)=\rho_t(Y)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\rho_s(X)=\rho_s(Y).\] Hence positions indistinguishable under a later assessment remain indistinguishable under every earlier assessment, without requiring preservation of strict or non-strict order between unequal assessments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two positions receive equal risk assessments at a later date, weak consistency requires equal assessments at every earlier date.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t(X)\) and \(\rho_t(Y)\) are compared almost surely.
\(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(X)=\rho_t(Y)\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)=\rho_s(Y)\).
review_flags: source needed to confirm equality-preservation interpretation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Equality preservation is a coherent definition, but the term weak time consistency is used for inequivalent notions in the literature. No source identifies this exact meaning for the terminal container.

children.title: Order-Based Time Consistency
children.top_down_role: Temporal preservation of selected risk comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Based Time Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure order preservation from later assessments to earlier assessments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic assessment family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) is order-based time consistent if, for every \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\) and all terminal positions \(X,Y\), \[\rho_t(X)\leq\rho_t(Y)\quad Q\text{-a.s.}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\rho_s(X)\leq\rho_s(Y)\quad Q\text{-a.s.}\] The comparison is made between the complete conditional assessments at time \(t\), and the resulting order must be preserved at every earlier date. Applying the condition in both directions yields equality preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any almost-sure ordering of two later risk assessments must persist at all earlier dates; equality preservation follows as a special case.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) belong to the common domain of every \(\rho_t\).
\(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(X)\leq\rho_t(Y)\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)\leq\rho_s(Y)\).

notation.meaning: conditional risk assessment at time t

review_flags: source needed to distinguish this notion from strong time consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order-preservation statement is internally consistent and definition fits the leaf, but a source is needed to distinguish this notion from strong time consistency and other order-based variants.

children.title: Comparison-Scope Regimes
children.top_down_role: Classes of comparisons retained across conditioning dates.

knowledge_statements.title: Comparison-Scope Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized temporal consistency obtained by restricting which position pairs may be compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(s\leq t\), let \(\mathcal C_{s,t}\subseteq L^p(\mathcal F_T)\times L^p(\mathcal F_T)\) be an admissible comparison scope. A dynamic assessment is \(\mathcal C\)-order consistent when \[ (X,Y)\in\mathcal C_{s,t},\quad \rho_t(X)\leq\rho_t(Y)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\rho_s(X)\leq\rho_s(Y). \] If two regimes satisfy \(\mathcal C_{s,t}^{(1)}\subseteq\mathcal C_{s,t}^{(2)}\) for every \(s\leq t\), then consistency under \(\mathcal C^{(2)}\) implies consistency under \(\mathcal C^{(1)}\). Full pairwise comparison is therefore the strongest scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-consistency strength depends on the admissible pairs compared; consistency for a larger comparison scope implies consistency for every smaller scope.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C_{s,t}\) is specified for every \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\).
All inequalities are interpreted almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C^{(1)}_{s,t}\subseteq\mathcal C^{(2)}_{s,t}\Rightarrow[\mathcal C^{(2)}\text{-consistency}\Rightarrow\mathcal C^{(1)}\text{-consistency}]\).

notation.meaning: admissible position-pair comparisons between dates s and t

review_flags: taxonomy-specific comparison regimes require a supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity with respect to nested comparison scopes is logically correct and condition fits the container, but the parameterized regime appears taxonomy-specific and has no supporting citation.

children.title: Acceptance-Rejection Consistency Duality
children.top_down_role: One-sided propagation of acceptability and rejection judgments.

children.title: Acceptance Consistency
children.top_down_role: Forward or backward propagation of acceptable positions.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward propagation of acceptability through a dynamic risk-measure family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) be normalized conditional risk measures, where a position \(X\) is acceptable at time \(t\) when \(\rho_t(X)\leq0\). The family is acceptance consistent if, for every \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\), \[\rho_t(X)\leq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\rho_s(X)\leq0.\] Equivalently, for the acceptance sets \(\mathcal A_t:=\{X:\rho_t(X)\leq0\}\), acceptance consistency requires \(\mathcal A_t\subseteq\mathcal A_s\) whenever \(s\leq t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A position acceptable at a later date must also be acceptable at every earlier date.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t(0)=0\) for every \(t\).
Inequalities are interpreted almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(X)\leq0\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)\leq0\), equivalently \(\mathcal A_t\subseteq\mathcal A_s\).

notation.meaning: conditional risk measure at time t

review_flags: source needed to confirm temporal direction and sign convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement consistently describes backward propagation of nonpositive assessments, but acceptance-consistency conventions vary. A source must verify the temporal direction, threshold convention, and acceptance-set inclusion.

children.title: Rejection Consistency
children.top_down_role: Forward or backward propagation of rejected positions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rejection Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward propagation of rejection through a dynamic risk-measure family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) be normalized conditional risk measures, where a position \(X\) is rejected at time \(t\) when \(\rho_t(X)\geq0\). The family is rejection consistent if, for every \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\), \[\rho_t(X)\geq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\rho_s(X)\geq0.\] Equivalently, for the rejection sets \(\mathcal R_t:=\{X:\rho_t(X)\geq0\}\), rejection consistency requires \(\mathcal R_t\subseteq\mathcal R_s\) whenever \(s\leq t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A position rejected at a later date must also be rejected at every earlier date.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t(0)=0\) for every \(t\).
Inequalities are interpreted almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(X)\geq0\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)\geq0\), equivalently \(\mathcal R_t\subseteq\mathcal R_s\).

notation.meaning: conditional risk measure at time t

review_flags: source needed to confirm temporal direction and boundary convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement consistently describes backward propagation of nonnegative assessments, but rejection-consistency and zero-boundary conventions vary. The exact definition requires an authoritative locator.

children.title: One-Sided Propagation Asymmetry
children.top_down_role: Structural differences between acceptability propagation and rejection propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Propagation Asymmetry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical distinction between propagation of nonpositive and nonnegative risk assessments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s\leq t\), acceptance consistency constrains only the event \(\{\rho_t(X)\leq0\}\), whereas rejection consistency constrains only \(\{\rho_t(X)\geq0\}\). Their conjunction gives the two-sided sign implications \[\rho_t(X)\leq0\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)\leq0,\qquad \rho_t(X)\geq0\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)\geq0.\] Consequently, if \(\rho_t(X)=0\), both properties together force \(\rho_s(X)=0\). Either one-sided condition alone supplies no implication for assessments having the opposite strict sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceptance and rejection consistency propagate opposite signs; together they preserve a zero assessment, while either condition alone controls only one side.
assumptions_latex: \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\).
Acceptance and rejection use the thresholds \(\rho_t(X)\leq0\) and \(\rho_t(X)\geq0\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(X)=0\Rightarrow\rho_s(X)=0\) when both one-sided consistencies hold.
review_flags: source needed for the intended acceptance-rejection duality framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Given the preceding one-sided definitions, the zero-preservation conclusion is logically correct and property is appropriate. No source confirms that these are the intended acceptance–rejection consistency notions.

children.title: Update-Rule Consistency
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency organized by update rules for future assessments.

knowledge_statements.title: Update-Rule Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal consistency expressed through operators that update later assessments to earlier information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\), let \(U_{s,t}:L^p(\mathcal F_t)\to L^p(\mathcal F_s)\) be an update rule. A dynamic assessment family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) is consistent with \(U\) if \[\rho_s(X)=U_{s,t}(\rho_t(X))\] for every terminal position \(X\) and every \(s\leq t\). The update rules are temporally coherent when \(U_{r,s}\circ U_{s,t}=U_{r,t}\) for all \(r\leq s\leq t\), so updating through an intermediate date gives the same earlier assessment as direct updating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Earlier assessments must be obtained by applying a coherent update operator to later assessments, independently of whether updating is direct or staged.
assumptions_latex: \(U_{s,t}\) maps \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable assessments to \(\mathcal F_s\)-measurable assessments.
\(U_{t,t}\) is the identity map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_s=U_{s,t}\circ\rho_t\) and \(U_{r,s}\circ U_{s,t}=U_{r,t}\).

notation.meaning: update rule from time t to time s

review_flags: update-rule consistency has multiple inequivalent formulations
source needed to confirm equality-based version

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An equality-based coherent update system is mathematically well formed and definition fits the topic, but update-rule consistency has several inequivalent formulations. No citation supports this exact factorization and composition requirement.

children.title: Decision-Policy Time-Consistency Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Agreement between initially planned and subsequently reoptimized decisions.

children.title: Decision Time Consistency
children.top_down_role: Temporal agreement for decisions selected at different evaluation dates.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision Time Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stagewise persistence of prescribed decisions under conditional reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi^*=(a_0^*,\ldots,a_{T-1}^*)\) be a feasible adapted policy, and let \(J_t(\pi;h_t)\) be the conditional objective after history \(h_t\). The policy is decision-time consistent if, at every history \(h_t\) reached by \(\pi^*\), its prescribed action satisfies \[a_t^*(h_t)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{a\in\mathcal A_t(h_t)}\;\inf_{\pi_{t+1:T-1}}J_t((a,\pi_{t+1:T-1});h_t).\] Thus reoptimization at a reached history never recommends replacing the current decision selected by the original policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every reached history, reoptimization must retain the current action prescribed by the original policy.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi^*\) is feasible and adapted.
The displayed infimum and action argmin are well-defined at each reached history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_t^*(h_t)\) remains conditionally optimal at every reached \(h_t\).

notation.meaning: information history available at time t

review_flags: source needed for the intended decision-policy distinction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulation captures persistence of the current action at reached histories, but no source verifies the intended decision-level notion, and the feasible continuation set conditional on the candidate action is not explicitly introduced.

children.title: Policy Time Consistency
children.top_down_role: Temporal stability of contingent policy plans.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy Time Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality of the entire prescribed continuation policy under conditional reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi^*=(a_0^*,\ldots,a_{T-1}^*)\) be a feasible adapted policy, and write \(\pi^*_{t:T-1}\) for its continuation after time \(t\). The policy is policy-time consistent if, for every history \(h_t\) reached by \(\pi^*\), \[\pi^*_{t:T-1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\pi_{t:T-1}\in\Pi_t(h_t)}J_t(\pi_{t:T-1};h_t).\] Hence conditional reoptimization preserves the complete continuation plan, not merely its current action. Policy time consistency therefore implies decision time consistency whenever the first action of every optimal continuation solves the corresponding stagewise minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every reached history, the whole continuation of the original policy must remain optimal under conditional reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi_t(h_t)\) is the set of feasible adapted continuation policies.
A minimizing continuation exists at each reached history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi^*_{t:T-1}\) is conditionally optimal for every reached \(h_t\).

notation.meaning: continuation of the original policy from time t

review_flags: source needed for the intended policy-level formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement coherently requires optimality of the complete continuation policy and definition fits the leaf, but an authoritative source is needed for this policy-level notion and its asserted relation to decision time consistency.

children.title: Reoptimization Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Agreement boundaries between initial plans and later reoptimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of an optimal policy with conditional reoptimization at almost every reachable decision history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi^*\) minimize a nested dynamic-risk objective over admissible policies, let \(\pi^*_{t:}|_{h_t}\) denote its continuation after history \(h_t\), and let \(P_{H_t}^{\pi^*}\) be the distribution of the time-\(t\) history induced by \(\pi^*\). Reoptimization compatibility holds when, for every \(t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\) and for \(P_{H_t}^{\pi^*}\)-almost every \(h_t\), \[\pi^*_{t:}|_{h_t}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\pi_{t:}\in\Pi_t(h_t)}\rho_t^{h_t}\!\left(C_{t:T}^{\pi_{t:}}\right),\] where \(\rho_t^{h_t}\) is the conditional tail-risk evaluation after \(h_t\). Thus conditional reoptimization preserves the prescribed continuation at almost every history reachable under \(\pi^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is reoptimization-compatible when its continuation remains optimal for the conditional tail problem at every time and at almost every history induced by that policy.
assumptions_latex: Regular conditional tail-risk evaluations \(\rho_t^{h_t}\) exist for \(P_{H_t}^{\pi^*}\)-almost every \(h_t\).
The conditional tail problems attain their minima over \(\Pi_t(h_t)\) for \(P_{H_t}^{\pi^*}\)-almost every \(h_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(t\), the continuation \(\pi^*_{t:}|_{h_t}\) is conditionally optimal for \(P_{H_t}^{\pi^*}\)-almost every \(h_t\).

notation.meaning: information history available at time t
history distribution induced by policy π* at time t
conditional tail-risk evaluation after history h_t
remaining cumulative cost under policy π
admissible continuation policies after history h_t
