children.title: Recursive Composition Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency viewed through adjacent conditional compositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Composition Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong time consistency for normalized conditional monetary risk measures under the loss convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) be normalized conditional monetary risk measures \(\rho_t:L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\to L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\), with cash invariance \(\rho_t(X+m)=\rho_t(X)-m\) for \(m\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\). The family is strongly time-consistent, meaning that \(\rho_t(X)\leq\rho_t(Y)\) implies \(\rho_s(X)\leq\rho_s(Y)\) for every \(s\leq t\), if and only if \[\rho_s(X)=\rho_s\!\left(-\rho_t(X)\right)\] for every \(X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\) and \(s\leq t\). It suffices to verify this identity at adjacent times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong time consistency is equivalent to evaluating every future position by first applying the later conditional risk measure and then the earlier one.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) is a finite discrete-time filtration.
Each \(\rho_t\) is normalized, monotone, local, and conditionally cash-invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_s=\rho_s\circ(-\rho_t)\) for all \(s\leq t\), equivalently for all adjacent pairs.

notation.meaning: essentially bounded, time-t measurable random variables
conditional risk measure at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive identity is a standard strong-time-consistency characterization under the stated monetary convention, but the cited generic recursive-method section does not demonstrably support this conditional-risk theorem or its hypotheses.

children.title: Acceptance-Set Decomposition Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency viewed through decomposable acceptance sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Set Decomposition Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance-set form of strong time consistency for conditional convex monetary risk measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(s\leq t\), define \(A_s=\{X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T):\rho_s(X)\leq0\}\), \(A_t=\{X:\rho_t(X)\leq0\}\), and \(A_{s,t}=A_s\cap L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\). A normalized local conditional convex monetary risk family is strongly time-consistent if and only if its acceptance sets satisfy \[A_s=A_{s,t}+A_t:=\{Y+Z:Y\in A_{s,t},\ Z\in A_t\}\] for every \(s\leq t\). Consequently, acceptability at time \(s\) decomposes into an acceptable time-\(t\) component and a residual position acceptable from time \(t\) onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong time consistency is equivalent to decomposing each earlier acceptance set into an intermediate-time acceptance set plus the later acceptance set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_t:L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\to L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\) is normalized, local, convex, monotone, and cash-invariant.
Acceptance sets use the loss convention \(\rho_t(X)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\rho_t)\) is strongly time-consistent if and only if \(A_s=A_{s,t}+A_t\) for every \(s\leq t\).

notation.meaning: time-t measurable positions acceptable at time s

review_flags: authoritative dynamic-risk theorem and closure conventions needed

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The acceptance-set decomposition is plausible and fits the characterization leaf, but no source is supplied to confirm the exact function spaces, normalization, and whether any closure qualification is required.

children.title: Penalty Cocycle Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency viewed through intertemporal compatibility of penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Cocycle Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal-penalty form of strong time consistency for robust conditional convex risk measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\rho_t\) has the robust representation \(\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_t}(E_Q[-X\mid\mathcal F_t]-\alpha_t(Q))\), with minimal penalty \(\alpha_t\). For \(s\leq t\), let \(\alpha_{s,t}\) be the minimal penalty obtained by restricting the dual supremum to \(L^\infty(\mathcal F_t)\). Under the Fatou property and the usual compatibility of the dual domains, strong time consistency is equivalent to the cocycle identity \[\alpha_s(Q)=\alpha_{s,t}(Q)+E_Q[\alpha_t(Q)\mid\mathcal F_s]\] for every admissible \(Q\) and every \(s\leq t\), with equality interpreted almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong time consistency is equivalent to splitting every minimal penalty into an earlier-step penalty plus the conditional expectation of the later penalty.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_t\) is a normalized conditional convex monetary risk measure with the Fatou property.
The dual measure domains are stable under restriction and conditional concatenation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong time consistency holds if and only if the minimal penalties satisfy the displayed cocycle identity.

notation.meaning: minimal penalty of dual measure Q at time t
minimal penalty for the restricted s-to-t risk mapping
admissible dual probability measures at time t

review_flags: exact dual-domain hypotheses and authoritative theorem locator needed

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimal-penalty cocycle has the expected form, but “usual compatibility” is not an explicit theorem hypothesis. An authoritative theorem must fix the admissible measures, restricted penalties, equivalence classes, and stability conditions.

children.title: Rectangularity-Stability Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency viewed through stability of model families under conditional pasting.

children.title: Rectangular Model Families
children.top_down_role: Conditional model families organized by rectangular temporal structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Model Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangularity of probability models on a finite filtered scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a finite filtered scenario tree, let \(K_t(h_t)\) be a nonempty set of admissible one-step conditional distributions after history \(h_t\). The induced model family \(\mathcal Q\) is rectangular when \[\mathcal Q=\left\{Q:Q(d\omega)=q_0(d\omega_1)q_1(d\omega_2\mid h_1)\cdots q_{T-1}(d\omega_T\mid h_{T-1}),\ q_t(\cdot\mid h_t)\in K_t(h_t)\right\}.\] Thus each admissible conditional kernel may be selected independently at every time and history, and every such concatenation remains in \(\mathcal Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model family is rectangular when admissible one-step conditional laws can be chosen independently at every node and concatenated into another admissible model.
assumptions_latex: The horizon and scenario tree are finite.
Every kernel set \(K_t(h_t)\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q\) contains exactly all nodewise concatenations of its admissible one-step kernels.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the finite-tree rectangular-model leaf, but it lacks a source specifying how nodewise kernel sets are derived and how zero-probability histories are treated.

children.title: Stability Under Conditional Pasting
children.top_down_role: Closure of model families under history-dependent pasting.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability Under Conditional Pasting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Density-process formulation of stability under history-dependent pasting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_t^Q=E_P[dQ/dP\mid\mathcal F_t]\) for \(Q\in\mathcal Q\), and assume the relevant densities are positive. The family \(\mathcal Q\) is stable under conditional pasting when, for every \(t\), \(Q,Q^1,Q^2\in\mathcal Q\), and \(A\in\mathcal F_t\), the probability measure \(\bar Q\) defined by \[Z_T^{\bar Q}=Z_t^Q\left(\mathbf1_A\frac{Z_T^{Q^1}}{Z_t^{Q^1}}+\mathbf1_{A^c}\frac{Z_T^{Q^2}}{Z_t^{Q^2}}\right)\] also belongs to \(\mathcal Q\). The pasted model follows \(Q\) through time \(t\) and then selects the conditional evolution of \(Q^1\) or \(Q^2\) according to \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional-pasting stability means that combining one model’s past with event-dependent conditional futures from admissible models produces another admissible model.
assumptions_latex: Every \(Q\in\mathcal Q\) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\).
The density ratios in the pasting formula are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Q\in\mathcal Q\) for every admissible time, event, and triple of models.

notation.meaning: time-t density process of Q relative to P
event known at the pasting time

review_flags: pasting convention and zero-density treatment need authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The density formula is meaningful under strict positivity, but no source confirms that this event-dependent three-measure operation is the intended conditional-pasting notion or supplies the required zero-density convention.

children.title: Rectangularity–Stability Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Regimes linking rectangular geometry to temporal stability.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangularity–Stability Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence on finite filtered trees between kernel rectangularity and conditional-pasting stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q\) be a nonempty family of probability measures on a finite filtered scenario tree, all absolutely continuous with respect to a reference measure \(P\). Then \(\mathcal Q\) is rectangular—its admissible one-step conditional kernels may be selected independently at every node—if and only if \(\mathcal Q\) is stable under conditional pasting at every time and every event in the current sigma-field. When \(\mathcal Q\) is also closed, the coherent risk family \[\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q}E_Q[-X\mid\mathcal F_t]\] consequently admits recursive evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite scenario tree, rectangularity of conditional model choices is equivalent to closure of the model family under conditional pasting.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and horizon are finite.
\(\mathcal Q\) is nonempty and dominated by a reference measure \(P\).
Closure is imposed when asserting the robust risk representation consequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q\) is rectangular if and only if it is stable under conditional pasting.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-tree correspondence is plausible, but absolute continuity alone permits null histories where kernels and density ratios are undefined. A source is needed to establish the exact positivity, closure, and pasting hypotheses and the recursive-risk consequence.

children.title: Risk-Penalty Process Characterization Pair
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency viewed through dynamic process properties.

children.title: Risk-Process Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal-consistency criteria expressed through risk-process behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Process Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Process-level form of strong time consistency under the monetary loss convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each terminal position \(X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\), define its risk process by \(R_t^X=\rho_t(X)\). A normalized local conditional monetary risk family is strongly time-consistent precisely when, for all \(0\leq s\leq t\leq T\), \[R_s^X=\rho_s(-R_t^X).\] Equivalently, the earlier risk assessment depends on \(X\) only through its later risk assessment, and the full risk process is generated by successive adjacent-time risk mappings. In particular, the terminal convention \(\rho_T(X)=-X\) makes the recursion valid through the horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic risk family is strongly time-consistent exactly when each position’s risk process is generated recursively from its later values.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\rho_t\) is normalized, local, monotone, and conditionally cash-invariant.
The terminal convention is \(\rho_T(X)=-X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_s^X=\rho_s(-R_t^X)\) for every position \(X\) and every \(s\leq t\).

notation.meaning: time-t risk assigned to terminal position X
conditional monetary risk measure at time t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula restates the recursive characterization correctly, but the asserted “precisely when” equivalence is a theorem rather than a generic property. An authoritative process-level characterization source is also absent.

children.title: Penalty-Process Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal-consistency criteria expressed through penalty-process behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Process Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Process-level cocycle characterization for minimal robust-representation penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an admissible dual measure \(Q\), and write \(A_t^Q=\alpha_t(Q)\) for its minimal-penalty process. For a normalized conditional convex risk family with the Fatou property and compatible dual domains, strong time consistency is equivalent to \[A_s^Q=\alpha_{s,t}(Q)+E_Q[A_t^Q\mid\mathcal F_s],\qquad 0\leq s\leq t\leq T.\] Hence the accumulated penalty from time \(s\) decomposes into the penalty incurred between \(s\) and \(t\) and the conditional value of the remaining penalty process. It is enough to impose this decomposition for adjacent times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalty process characterizes time consistency when each earlier penalty equals its one-period increment plus the conditional expected later penalty.
assumptions_latex: The risk measures are normalized, conditionally convex, monetary, and have the Fatou property.
Minimal penalties and restricted penalties share compatible dual domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty process satisfies the cocycle decomposition for every admissible \(Q\) and every \(s\leq t\).

notation.meaning: penalty accumulated between times s and t

review_flags: minimal-penalty process theorem and domain hypotheses need source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an if-and-only-if characterization and should be typed as a theorem, not a generic property. Its minimal-penalty domains, restricted penalties, and adjacent-time sufficiency require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Cross-Process Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Consistency relationships between risk-process and penalty-process representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Process Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between recursive risk processes and cocyclic minimal-penalty processes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_t^X=\rho_t(X)\) and \(A_t^Q=\alpha_t(Q)\), where \[R_t^X=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_t}\left(E_Q[-X\mid\mathcal F_t]-A_t^Q\right).\] The risk and penalty processes are cross-compatible when the dual domains are stable under conditional pasting and, for every \(s\leq t\), \[A_s^Q=\alpha_{s,t}(Q)+E_Q[A_t^Q\mid\mathcal F_s].\] Under attainment or the standard essential-supremum approximation property, this penalty cocycle yields \(R_s^X=\rho_s(-R_t^X)\); conversely, strong recursion of the risk process yields the cocycle for minimal penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable dual domains and a penalty cocycle make the robust risk process recursive; with minimal penalties, risk recursion also recovers the cocycle.
assumptions_latex: The conditional convex risk measures have robust representations with minimal penalties.
Dual domains are stable under conditional pasting.
Dual suprema are attained or admit directed essential-supremum approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Penalty-process cocycles and risk-process recursion are equivalent compatible descriptions of strong time consistency.
review_flags: equivalence requires an authoritative theorem fixing dual-domain and closure assumptions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The terminal container concerns compatibility, but the record asserts a bidirectional primal-dual characterization rather than merely giving a representation. A source must establish the exact attainment or approximation, closure, minimality, and domain-stability hypotheses; theorem or duality would be the appropriate kind.

children.title: Bellman-Policy Compatibility Characterization
children.top_down_role: Temporal consistency viewed through recursive optimality and policy stability.

children.title: Bellman Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of dynamic risk evaluation with recursive value decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Bellman Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bellman recursion for controlled systems evaluated by one-step conditional risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a controlled state process with feasible actions \(U_t(x)\), transition \(X_{t+1}=F_t(x,u,W_{t+1})\), stage cost \(c_t(x,u,W_{t+1})\), terminal cost \(g\), and one-step conditional risk mapping \(\sigma_t\), Bellman compatibility means that \[V_T(x)=g(x),\qquad V_t(x)=\inf_{u\in U_t(x)}\sigma_t\!\left(c_t(x,u,W_{t+1})+V_{t+1}(F_t(x,u,W_{t+1}))\right).\] The nested dynamic-risk objective from any time and state must equal \(V_t(x)\); otherwise the dynamic risk evaluation and Bellman decomposition are incompatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bellman compatibility requires the nested risk objective to equal a backward recursion using the same one-step conditional risk mappings.
assumptions_latex: The controlled state is Markov with respect to the chosen information state.
Each one-step risk mapping is monotone and local.
The displayed infima are measurable and well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value functions satisfy the displayed risk-sensitive Bellman recursion.

notation.meaning: optimal value function at time t
feasible actions at state x and time t

source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

source_witnesses.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bellman formula fits the leaf, but the cited Gosavi locator concerns an ordinary average-reward Bellman policy equation, while the Pflug locator is generic recursion. Neither inspectably supports the stated finite-horizon nested conditional-risk recursion.

children.title: Policy Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of temporal risk evaluation with stable policy choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of Bellman minimizers with conditionally optimal continuation policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the risk-sensitive Bellman recursion holds and that each infimum admits a measurable selector \(\mu_t^*(x)\). Define the Markov policy \(\pi^*=(\mu_0^*,\ldots,\mu_{T-1}^*)\). Policy compatibility holds when, for every time \(t\) and every reachable state \(x\), \[\mu_t^*(x)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{u\in U_t(x)}\sigma_t\!\left(c_t(x,u,W_{t+1})+V_{t+1}(F_t(x,u,W_{t+1}))\right),\] and the continuation \((\mu_t^*,\ldots,\mu_{T-1}^*)\) attains the nested conditional value \(V_t(x)\). Consequently, truncating and reoptimizing the policy at a reachable state preserves its prescribed continuation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is compatible when measurable Bellman minimizers form continuations that attain every conditional tail value and remain optimal after reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: The Bellman recursion is valid for the nested dynamic-risk objective.
Measurable minimizing selectors exist at every time.
The state summarizes all information relevant to conditional costs and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy assembled from Bellman selectors is conditionally optimal from every reachable time-state pair.

notation.meaning: optimal measurable decision rule at time t
policy formed from the decision rules

children.title: Recursive Optimality Linkage
children.top_down_role: Connections between recursive values, reoptimization, and policy stability.

assumptions_latex: A finite horizon \(T\), filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\), and admissible continuation-policy sets \(\Pi_t(h_t)\) are fixed.
Conditional risk mappings \(\rho_t:L^0(\mathcal F_T)\to L^0(\mathcal F_t)\) are monotone and recursively decomposable.
Conditional essential infima are attained by measurable policy selectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A policy is optimal after every history exactly when its continuation attains the corresponding Bellman recursion at every date.

notation.meaning: value at time t and history h_t

review_flags: specialized_dynamic-risk formulation needs direct source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon Bellman characterization for recursively decomposable conditional risk criteria.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 The recursive method p. 13; 1.2.4 Recursive versus non-recursive methods p. 16

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each history \(h_t\), define \(V_T(h_T)=Z_T(h_T)\) and, backward for \(t<T\), \[V_t(h_t)=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{a\in A_t(h_t)}\varrho_t\!\left(c_t(h_t,a)+V_{t+1}(H_{t+1})\right).\] A policy \(\pi^*\) is recursively optimal, meaning that every continuation \(\pi^*_{t:}\) minimizes the conditional criterion over \(\Pi_t(h_t)\), if and only if, for every reachable \(h_t\), its action attains the displayed essential infimum and its subsequent continuation is recursively optimal. Consequently, recursive optimality is equivalent to simultaneous Bellman and continuation-policy compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under recursive conditional risk evaluation and attainment, a policy remains optimal after every history exactly when its actions attain every Bellman minimum and its continuations remain optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Optimality Linkage

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 The recursive method p. 13; 1.2.4 Recursive versus non-recursive methods p. 16

The record also switches from \(\rho_t\) to \(\varrho_t\) and leaves the controlled transition, costs, and reachability convention insufficiently specified.

children.title: Time-Consistency Construction-Repair Calculus
children.top_down_role: Families for constructing recursive systems or repairing nonrecursive criteria.

children.title: Backward Nested Composition
children.top_down_role: Construction from a sequence of one-step conditional mappings.

assumptions_latex: A finite filtered probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) is fixed.
Each \(\varrho_t:L^0(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^0(\mathcal F_t)\) is monotone and maps admissible random variables to finite values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backward nesting defines a recursive, strongly time-consistent dynamic evaluation.

notation.meaning: one-step conditional evaluation from t+1 to t
evaluation at time t of a terminal payoff Z

review_flags: locator supports recursion generally but not the full conditional-risk formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a terminal-payoff evaluation by nesting one-step conditional mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(\rho_{T,T}(Z)=Z\) for every admissible \(Z\in L^0(\mathcal F_T)\), and recursively define \[\rho_{t,T}(Z)=\varrho_t\bigl(\rho_{t+1,T}(Z)\bigr),\qquad t=T-1,\ldots,0.\] Equivalently, \(\rho_{t,T}=\varrho_t\circ\varrho_{t+1}\circ\cdots\circ\varrho_{T-1}\). If \(\rho_{t+1,T}(X)\leq\rho_{t+1,T}(Y)\), monotonicity of \(\varrho_t\) gives \(\rho_{t,T}(X)\leq\rho_{t,T}(Y)\). Thus the nested family is strongly time consistent under the convention that larger values are worse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compose monotone one-step conditional evaluations backward from the terminal date. The resulting nested dynamic evaluation preserves every future conditional ordering at all earlier dates.
knowledge_statements.title: Backward Nested Composition

children.title: Rectangular Risk-Envelope Construction
children.top_down_role: Construction from conditionally stable families of probability models.

assumptions_latex: The probability space is finite, with filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) and reference law \(\mathbb P\).
For each \(t<T\), \(\mathcal Q_t(\omega)\) is a nonempty set of conditional transition laws measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pasting the one-step kernels produces a rectangular model family whose robust conditional expectations satisfy backward recursion.

notation.meaning: admissible conditional laws at time t
rectangular family obtained by kernel pasting

review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports rectangular risk envelopes
exact measurable-space generality requires a dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-space rectangularization by independent historywise selection of one-step probability kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{rect}}\) contain exactly the probability laws \(Q\) whose regular conditional transition at every date \(t\) and history belongs to \(\mathcal Q_t\); equivalently, its elements are formed by pasting arbitrary admissible one-step kernels along the filtration. For terminal loss \(Z\), set \[\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{rect}}}E_Q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t].\] Then \[\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{q\in\mathcal Q_t}E_q[\rho_{t+1}(Z)\mid\mathcal F_t],\qquad \rho_T(Z)=Z.\] Hence rectangularity converts the robust envelope into a backward-nested, time-consistent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allow every admissible one-step model to be pasted independently at each history. Worst-case conditional expectations over the resulting rectangular family then obey backward recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Risk-Envelope Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A dedicated source is required for the kernel-pasting construction, the conditional essential-supremum recursion, and the exact rectangularity assumptions.

children.title: Time-Consistent Hull-Envelope Pair
children.top_down_role: Recursive modifications of initially time-inconsistent criteria.

children.title: Time-Consistent Hulls
children.top_down_role: Hull-based recursive modifications of time-inconsistent criteria.

assumptions_latex: Dynamic risk families are ordered pointwise: \(\sigma\preceq\rho\) means \(\sigma_t(Z)\leq\rho_t(Z)\) for every \(t\) and admissible \(Z\).
The chosen class \(\mathfrak T\) of strongly time-consistent risk families contains at least one majorant of \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the pointwise infimum remains in \(\mathfrak T\), it is the least time-consistent majorant of \(\rho\).
review_flags: terminology and order convention are not supported by supplied locators
a source is needed to distinguish upper hull from alternative hull conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-theoretic upper hull under the loss convention that larger risk values are more conservative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The time-consistent upper hull of a dynamic risk family \(\rho=(\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) is a family \(H^+(\rho)\in\mathfrak T\) satisfying \(\rho\preceq H^+(\rho)\) and \[H^+(\rho)\preceq\sigma\quad\text{for every }\sigma\in\mathfrak T\text{ with }\rho\preceq\sigma.\] If the pointwise infimum belongs to \(\mathfrak T\), it is represented by \[H^+(\rho)=\inf\{\sigma\in\mathfrak T:\rho\preceq\sigma\},\] where the infimum is taken componentwise over dates and admissible losses. Existence is not automatic because a pointwise infimum of time-consistent families need not be time consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-consistent upper hull is the least time-consistent dynamic risk family dominating the original family. Its existence requires closure of the admissible class under the relevant infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Consistent Hulls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order-theoretic definition is plausible and its kind fits the leaf, but no source establishes that this upper-majorant convention is the intended meaning of a time-consistent hull or supplies the required closure conditions.

children.title: Time-Consistent Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Envelope-based recursive modifications of time-inconsistent criteria.

assumptions_latex: Each coherent conditional risk mapping has a dual representation by a nonempty family of probability laws absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mathbb P\).
Conditional essential suprema are well defined on the selected loss space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A rectangular dual envelope generates a strongly time-consistent coherent dynamic risk family.

notation.meaning: rectangular closure of the dual family

review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports time-consistent dual envelopes
minimal rectangular closure and dual-space assumptions need source confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-envelope construction for coherent risk under finite-horizon rectangularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a dual family \(\mathcal Q\), let \(\operatorname{rect}(\mathcal Q)\) be the smallest family containing \(\mathcal Q\) that is stable under admissible pasting at every date, when such a smallest family exists. Its time-consistent risk envelope is the dynamic family \[\rho_t^{\mathrm{env}}(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\operatorname{rect}(\mathcal Q)}E_Q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t],\qquad t=0,\ldots,T.\] The terminal mapping is \(\rho_T^{\mathrm{env}}(Z)=Z\), and pasting stability yields the one-step recursive decomposition. Thus rectangular closure on the dual side defines a coherent, strongly time-consistent envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rectangularly close a coherent risk measure's dual probability family and take worst-case conditional expectations. The resulting dual envelope is a strongly time-consistent dynamic risk family.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Consistent Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rectangular dual-envelope construction needs a source specifying the loss space, pasting operation, existence of the minimal rectangular closure, and the resulting strong time consistency.

children.title: Hull–Envelope Comparison
children.top_down_role: Coverage, minimality, and conservatism differences between repair constructions.

assumptions_latex: A coherent dynamic risk family \(\rho\) has dual family \(\mathcal Q\) on a finite filtered probability space.
The upper hull exists, and \(\operatorname{rect}(\mathcal Q)\) is the minimal pasting-stable dual enlargement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under exact duality, the primal time-consistent upper hull equals the risk family represented by the rectangular dual envelope.
review_flags: primal order and dual inclusion conventions require dedicated source verification
closure and dual-attainment hypotheses may need strengthening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual comparison for coherent risk on a finite filtered probability space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the loss convention, enlarging a coherent risk envelope increases its risk value. Hence \(\mathcal Q\subseteq\operatorname{rect}(\mathcal Q)\) implies \(\rho\\preceq\rho^{\mathrm{env}}\), where \[\rho_t^{\mathrm{env}}(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\operatorname{rect}(\mathcal Q)}E_Q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t].\] If every strongly time-consistent coherent majorant of \(\rho\) corresponds exactly to a rectangular dual family containing \(\mathcal Q\), then minimality on both sides gives \[H^+(\rho)=\rho^{\mathrm{env}}.\] Thus the primal least time-consistent majorant and the dual minimal rectangular enlargement are two representations of the same repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For coherent risk, the least time-consistent majorant agrees with worst-case expectation over the smallest rectangular enlargement of the original dual probability family, provided exact duality and existence hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Hull–Envelope Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hull–envelope identity depends on nontrivial exact-duality, closure, and attainment hypotheses for which no source is supplied. The expression intended as \(\rho\preceq\rho^{\mathrm{env}}\) also contains an erroneous doubled backslash before `preceq`.

children.title: State Augmentation for Consistency
children.top_down_role: Recovery of recursion by retaining risk-relevant history in the state.

assumptions_latex: The controlled process has finite horizon and history \(H_t=(X_0,A_0,\ldots,X_t)\).
A measurable statistic \(S_t=\Phi_t(H_t)\) retains all information needed for transitions, admissibility, and the conditional risk criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented state \((X_t,S_t)\) is sufficient for a Bellman recursion representing the original history-dependent problem.
review_flags: risk-sufficient augmentation criterion needs a specialized source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Markovization of a history-dependent risk criterion by a sufficient statistic.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Markov Processes with Arbitrary State Space p. 101

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that whenever two histories have the same \(Y_t=(X_t,S_t)\), they induce the same feasible actions, conditional law of \(Y_{t+1}\) under each action, current cost, and one-step conditional risk mapping. Then the continuation value depends on history only through \(Y_t\). Writing \(V_T(y)=g(y)\), one may define \[V_t(y)=\inf_{a\in A_t(y)}\varrho_t^{y,a}\!\left(c_t(y,a)+V_{t+1}(Y_{t+1})\right).\] Any measurable minimizing selector yields a policy equivalent, in value and induced decisions, to the corresponding history-dependent policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an added statistic preserves every transition, feasibility, cost, and risk-relevant feature of history, the augmented state supports a Bellman recursion equivalent to the original problem.
knowledge_statements.title: State Augmentation for Consistency

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Markov Processes with Arbitrary State Space p. 101

children.title: Precommitment Regime
children.top_down_role: Optimization under the initial criterion without requiring later agreement.

knowledge_statements.title: Precommitment Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Date-zero optimization without subgame or continuation optimality requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) denote the history available at date \(t\), let \(\Pi_t(H_t)\) be the feasible continuation-policy set, and let \(J_t(\eta_{t:}\mid H_t)\) be the date-\(t\) conditional criterion for \(\eta_{t:}\in\Pi_t(H_t)\). A precommitment policy is any policy satisfying \[\pi^{\mathrm{pc}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\pi\in\Pi}J_0(\pi).\] Its continuation is implemented as part of the date-zero plan; the definition does not require \[J_t(\pi^{\mathrm{pc}}_{t:}\mid H_t)=\inf_{\eta_{t:}\in\Pi_t(H_t)}J_t(\eta_{t:}\mid H_t)\] at any date \(t>0\) or history \(H_t\). Such equality may hold in a particular problem, but it is not imposed by the precommitment regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A precommitment policy minimizes the date-zero objective. Its later continuations are components of that initial plan and need not minimize the criteria used upon later reevaluation.
assumptions_latex: A finite-horizon history process \((H_t)_{t=0}^T\), an admissible policy class \(\Pi\), and feasible continuation-policy sets \(\Pi_t(H_t)\) are fixed.
For each date \(t\), the conditional continuation criterion \(J_t(\eta_{t:}\mid H_t)\) is defined for every \(\eta_{t:}\in\Pi_t(H_t)\).
The date-zero minimization \(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}J_0(\pi)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A precommitment solution minimizes the date-zero objective and is not required to remain optimal under later conditional criteria.

notation.meaning: feasible continuation-policy set after history H_t
date-t conditional criterion for a continuation policy

children.title: Equilibrium Reoptimization Regime
children.top_down_role: Sequential decisions that anticipate future preference revisions.

assumptions_latex: At each date \(t\), a conditional continuation criterion \(J_t\) and feasible one-step deviations are specified.
Future decision makers are assumed to follow the same candidate policy after the current deviation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An equilibrium policy admits no profitable one-step deviation at any reachable history.

notation.meaning: policy using action a now and pi^e thereafter

review_flags: no supplied locator supports intrapersonal equilibrium reoptimization
deviation and off-path conventions require a specialized source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time subgame-perfect intrapersonal equilibrium under one-step deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A policy \(\pi^e\) is an equilibrium reoptimization policy if, for every date \(t<T\) and every relevant history \(h_t\), \[J_t(\pi^e_{t:}\mid h_t)\leq J_t((a,\pi^e_{t+1:})\mid h_t)\quad\text{for every }a\in A_t(h_t).\] The current decision maker chooses optimally while treating future selves' equilibrium continuation as fixed. This condition is imposed sequentially, including off-path histories when subgame perfection is required, and does not assert global minimization of the original date-zero criterion over complete policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each current decision minimizes its own conditional criterion while anticipating that future decisions follow the same equilibrium policy. No admissible one-step deviation may improve the current objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Equilibrium Reoptimization Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A specialized source is required to support the one-step-deviation characterization and to fix whether equilibrium is imposed only on reachable histories or at all histories for subgame perfection.

children.title: Verification-Improvement Coupling
children.top_down_role: Verification and improvement architecture for nonrecursive multistage criteria.

children.title: Martingale Verification
children.top_down_role: Martingale-based certification architecture for candidate solutions.

assumptions_latex: For a candidate policy \(\pi^e\), an adapted integrable verification process \((M_t^{\pi})_{t=0}^T\) is defined for every one-step deviation policy \(\pi\).
Costs are minimized, and all relevant conditional expectations exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Martingale equality for \(\pi^e\) and submartingale inequalities for deviations certify one-step equilibrium optimality.

notation.meaning: adapted verification process under policy pi

review_flags: no supplied source supports this verification orientation
the construction of the verification process is model dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract discrete-time martingale certificate for a minimizing equilibrium policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(M_T^{\pi}\) equals the realized terminal objective associated with \(\pi\), and its initial value equals the candidate value. If, for every \(t<T\), \[E^{\pi^e}[M_{t+1}^{\pi^e}\mid\mathcal F_t]=M_t^{\pi^e}\] and, for every admissible policy \(\pi\) differing from \(\pi^e\) only at date \(t\), \[E^{\pi}[M_{t+1}^{\pi}\mid\mathcal F_t]\geq M_t^{\pi^e},\] then no such one-step deviation lowers the time-\(t\) conditional objective. Thus \(M^{\pi^e}\) is a verifiable certificate of equilibrium reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is verified when its value process is a martingale, while every one-step deviation produces the inequality unfavorable to a minimizing decision maker.
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale Verification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The terminal-value and one-step conditional relations alone do not establish how the verification process represents each date's conditional objective. A model-specific verification theorem is needed before the inequalities can certify equilibrium.

children.title: Sequential Improvement
children.top_down_role: Stagewise refinement architecture for nonrecursive multistage criteria.

assumptions_latex: A current policy \(\pi^k\) and well-defined conditional one-step deviation values \(Q_t^{\pi^k}(h_t,a)\) are available.
Measurable minimizing actions exist at every updated history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backward one-step minimization produces a policy with no larger local continuation values and stops only at a one-step equilibrium.

notation.meaning: value of deviating now and following pi^k thereafter

review_flags: no supplied source supports this equilibrium policy-improvement algorithm
global convergence is deliberately not asserted
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward one-step policy improvement for a time-inconsistent minimizing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an admissible policy \(\pi^k\). For \(t=T-1,T-2,\ldots,0\), evaluate \(Q_t^{\pi^k}(h_t,a)\), the time-\(t\) criterion obtained by choosing \(a\) at \(h_t\) and using the already selected continuation thereafter, and set \[\pi_{t}^{k+1}(h_t)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{a\in A_t(h_t)}Q_t^{\pi^k}(h_t,a).\] Retain \(\pi_t^k(h_t)\) when it is already minimizing. Stop when a full backward sweep makes no changes; otherwise repeat. A fixed point satisfies every one-step equilibrium inequality, although finite termination or global improvement requires additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sweep backward, replacing each action by a best current response to the selected future continuation. Stop when a complete sweep changes nothing; the result satisfies one-step equilibrium conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Improvement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed improvement algorithm. The definition of \(Q_t^{\pi^k}\) is also ambiguous because the sweep refers to an already updated future continuation rather than consistently using \(\pi^k\); termination and fixed-point claims require a precise hybrid-policy update rule.

children.title: Verification–Improvement Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between candidate certification and subsequent refinement.

assumptions_latex: Verification and improvement use the same conditional deviation functional \(Q_t^{\pi}(h_t,a)\).
A candidate policy \(\pi\) and its associated adapted value process are integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The verification residual is simultaneously the local improvement signal; all residuals vanish exactly at an equilibrium fixed point.
review_flags: no supplied source supports the stated coupling
martingale-residual identity depends on the model-specific verification process
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual identity connecting one-step verification inequalities to policy improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimizing problem, define the local residual by \[R_t^{\pi}(h_t)=V_t^{\pi}(h_t)-\inf_{a\in A_t(h_t)}Q_t^{\pi}(h_t,a).\] Then \(R_t^{\pi}(h_t)\geq0\). A strictly positive residual identifies an action replacement that lowers the current conditional criterion, while \(R_t^{\pi}(h_t)=0\) is precisely the one-step verification condition at \((t,h_t)\). When the verification process is chosen so that its conditional drift equals this residual, martingale verification and sequential improvement use the same computable quantity. Consequently, \(\pi\) is an equilibrium fixed point exactly when every residual vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gap between a policy's continuation value and its best one-step deviation is both a verification residual and an improvement signal. All such gaps vanish exactly at equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.title: Verification–Improvement Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary best-deviation gap is plausible, but identifying it with the conditional drift of a martingale verification process is model dependent and unsupported. A source must establish the common deviation functional and drift identity.

children.title: Time-Consistency Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Principal mechanisms preventing recursive evaluation or policy stability.

children.title: Non-Nested Static-Risk Failure
children.top_down_role: Failure associated with applying one static risk functional to a full future path.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Nested Static-Risk Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A continuation-equivalence test exposing failure of a static pathwise risk objective to admit dynamic recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_0:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to\mathbb R\) be a static loss-risk functional and let \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) be a proposed continuation mapping. If there exist terminal losses \(X,Y\) such that \(\rho_t(X)=\rho_t(Y)\) almost surely but \(\rho_0(X)\ne\rho_0(Y)\), then no mapping \(R_{0,t}:L^p(\mathcal F_t)\to\mathbb R\) can satisfy \(\rho_0(Z)=R_{0,t}(\rho_t(Z))\) for every \(Z\). Thus optimizing the single static quantity \(\rho_0\) over complete future paths cannot, with this continuation statistic, obey a Bellman recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two continuations have identical conditional risk but different initial static risk, that conditional statistic cannot support a Bellman recursion for the static objective.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le p\le\infty\) and \(\mathcal F_t\subseteq\mathcal F_T\).
\(\rho_t(X)\) is the continuation statistic proposed for decisions at time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(X)=\rho_t(Y)\) and \(\rho_0(X)\ne\rho_0(Y)\) imply that \(\rho_0\) does not factor through \(\rho_t\).

notation.meaning: static risk functional applied at the initial time

children.title: Nonrectangular Model-Family Failure
children.top_down_role: Failure of local recursion under dynamically coupled model choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrectangular Model-Family Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust conditional expectations fail to recurse when admissible probability models cannot be pasted across histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q\) be a family of probability measures and define \(\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q}E_Q[X\mid\mathcal F_t]\). Rectangularity requires that, after any time-\(t\) history, the conditional continuation of one member of \(\mathcal Q\) may be pasted to the pre-\(t\) part of another while remaining admissible. If \(\mathcal Q\) is not rectangular, the tower identity may fail: for some bounded loss \(X\), \(\rho_s(X)\ne\rho_s(\rho_t(X))\) for \(s<t\). Such an \(X\) certifies failure of local robust recursion because the stagewise maximizers need not correspond to any single measure in \(\mathcal Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without stability under conditional pasting, stagewise worst-case choices may not form an admissible global model, and the robust tower identity can fail.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) is a filtration and \(X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\).
Every \(Q\in\mathcal Q\) admits the displayed conditional expectations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A witness \(X\) with \(\rho_s(X)\ne\rho_s(\rho_t(X))\) demonstrates failure of recursive worst-case evaluation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: robust-control rectangularity is the standard pasting condition underlying the robust tower property
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed implication from nonrectangularity to a bounded witness for tower-identity failure requires precise pasting, domination, and conditional essential-supremum hypotheses. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Law Invariance versus Strong Consistency
children.top_down_role: Restrictions arising from simultaneously imposing law invariance and strong temporal consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Law Invariance versus Strong Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous law invariance and strong temporal consistency impose both distributional and conditional-order restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic loss-risk family \((\rho_t)_{t=0}^T\) is law invariant at time zero when \(X\stackrel{d}{=}Y\) implies \(\rho_0(X)=\rho_0(Y)\). It is strongly time consistent when, for every \(s<t\), \(\rho_t(X)\le\rho_t(Y)\) almost surely implies \(\rho_s(X)\le\rho_s(Y)\). Consequently, any family satisfying both properties must preserve every conditional continuation ordering under all earlier evaluations while assigning the same initial value to identically distributed terminal losses. A law-invariant static functional lacking a conditional extension with this order-preservation property cannot generate a strongly consistent dynamic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible family must ignore distribution-preserving changes initially while preserving every conditional risk ordering at all earlier times; many static law-invariant risks lack such an extension.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) evaluates terminal losses.
\(\rho_0(X)\) is finite for the compared losses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Law invariance and strong consistency jointly require distributional invariance at time zero and backward preservation of conditional risk order.

notation.meaning: X and Y have the same probability law
conditional loss-risk evaluation at time t

review_flags: classification theorem intentionally not asserted because its exact hypotheses depend on atomlessness, coherence, and filtration structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definitions are plausible, but the exact meaning of strong time consistency and the extension claim depend on the dynamic-risk framework and filtration assumptions. An authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Dynamic Value-at-Risk Failure Regime
children.top_down_role: Temporal and optimization failures associated with nonnested quantile risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Value-at-Risk Failure Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-stage finite-tree example where unnested terminal VaR disagrees with recursive conditional VaR.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the lower quantile convention \(\operatorname{VaR}_{\alpha}(X)=\inf\{x:P(X\le x)\ge\alpha\}\) for losses. Let four terminal outcomes be equiprobable and let \(\mathcal F_1\) distinguish two equally probable branches. On the first branch let \(X\) take values \(0,100\); on the second let it take values \(1,2\), conditionally equiprobably. At \(\alpha=3/4\), \(\operatorname{VaR}_{3/4}(X)=2\). Conditional stage-one VaR equals \(100\) on the first branch and \(2\) on the second, so \(\operatorname{VaR}_{3/4}(\operatorname{VaR}_{3/4}(X\mid\mathcal F_1))=100\). Hence unnested VaR violates the recursive identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a four-leaf tree, static 75% VaR equals 2 while nested conditional 75% VaR equals 100, directly disproving temporal recursion.
assumptions_latex: All four terminal leaves have probability \(1/4\).
Quantiles use the lower-quantile convention displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{VaR}_{3/4}(X)\ne\operatorname{VaR}_{3/4}(\operatorname{VaR}_{3/4}(X\mid\mathcal F_1))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the finite counterexample is completely checkable from the displayed quantile definition and leaf probabilities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-tree counterexample and both quantile calculations are correct, and counterexample is the proper content kind. The record nevertheless has no cited source.

children.title: Information-Filtration Mismatch Interface
children.top_down_role: Failure caused by incompatible conditioning, policy, or scenario-tree information.

children.title: Information Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by inconsistent information available to evaluations or policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Information Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A state description is inadequate when it merges histories having different conditional risk evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_t\) be the information state used by a dynamic program and let \(\mathcal F_t\) contain the full observed history. Information mismatch occurs if there exist histories \(h,h'\) with \(S_t(h)=S_t(h')\), an admissible action \(u\), and a continuation loss \(X^u\) such that \(\rho_t(X^u)(h)\ne\rho_t(X^u)(h')\). Then no function \(v_t\) of \(S_t\) alone can represent that continuation evaluation at both histories. A Bellman recursion based only on \(S_t\) is therefore invalid unless the state is augmented or the conditional risk model is changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If identical dynamic-programming states conceal histories with different conditional continuation risks, no value function of that state alone can support the recursion.
assumptions_latex: \(S_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
\(\rho_t(X^u)\) is defined for every considered continuation loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed witness prevents a representation \(\rho_t(X^u)=v_t(S_t,u)\) valid on both histories.

notation.meaning: information state retained by the dynamic program

source_refs.locator: 2.4 A Simple Modeling Framework for Dynamic Programs p. 50

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 A Simple Modeling Framework for Dynamic Programs p. 50

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The obstruction is valid on a finite scenario tree, but pointwise values at histories are not generally well defined for almost-sure equivalence classes. The cited dynamic-programming section does not yet establish the risk-specific formulation.

children.title: Filtration Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by incompatible conditioning structures across stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Filtration Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurability condition linking the policy filtration to the filtration used by conditional risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let controls be adapted to a policy filtration \((\mathcal G_t)\), while \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) conditions on a model filtration \((\mathcal F_t)\). A filtration mismatch relevant to recursion exists when, for some admissible continuation loss \(X\), either \(X\notin L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\) or \(\rho_t(X)\notin L^p(\mathcal G_t)\). In the latter case the risk-adjusted continuation value uses information unavailable to a \(\mathcal G_t\)-adapted decision. The Bellman minimization is not implementable under the stated policy information unless measurability is restored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk conditioning and policy information are mismatched when a continuation is outside the risk domain or its evaluated value is not observable to the policy.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)\) and \((\mathcal G_t)\) are filtrations on one probability space.
Admissible controls at time \(t\) are \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility requires \(X\in L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\) and \(\rho_t(X)\in L^p(\mathcal G_t)\) for every admissible continuation.

notation.meaning: information used by the conditional risk model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: domain and measurability compatibility are necessary for an adapted Bellman decision
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The domain and policy-measurability requirements are plausible necessary conditions, but their precise formulation requires a source specifying the relationship between the two filtrations and the conditional-risk domain.

children.title: Policy–Conditioning Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Boundary between admissible policy information and risk-evaluation conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy–Conditioning Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient adaptation, domain, measurability, and locality requirements for risk-aware policy recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a policy filtration \((\mathcal G_t)\), a one-step risk mapping \(\rho_t\), and admissible controls \(u_t\), policy–conditioning compatibility requires: \(u_t\) is \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable; every induced one-step loss plus continuation value \(Z_{t+1}^{u_t}\) lies in the domain of \(\rho_t\); and \(\rho_t(Z_{t+1}^{u_t})\) is \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable. In addition, locality requires \(\mathbf1_A\rho_t(X)=\mathbf1_A\rho_t(\mathbf1_AX)\) for every \(A\in\mathcal G_t\). Under these conditions, the risk-adjusted quantities compared by the time-\(t\) policy depend only on information available when the action is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible recursion uses adapted controls, admissible continuation losses, observable conditional risk values, and a risk mapping local to currently observable events.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal G_t)\) is the policy information filtration.
\(Z_{t+1}^{u_t}\) denotes the loss and continuation generated by action \(u_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All time-\(t\) risk comparisons are \(\mathcal G_t\)-measurable and local to \(\mathcal G_t\).

notation.meaning: next-step loss plus continuation under the action

review_flags: exact locality convention and filtration hypotheses require an authoritative dynamic-risk source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed locality identity requires normalization such as rho_t(0)=0; the framework-independent locality condition is normally stated through equality on observable events. The mapping domain, codomain, and supporting source are absent.

children.title: Nested Worst-Case Models
children.top_down_role: Recursive worst-case evaluation across future branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Worst-Case Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive robust evaluation formed by nesting conditional worst-case expectations at successive stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For terminal loss \(X\), let \(\mathcal Q_t(\omega)\) be a conditionally admissible set of one-step probability kernels and define \(\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{q\in\mathcal Q_t}E_q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]\). Set \(V_T=X\) and recursively define \(V_t=ho_t(V_{t+1})\) for \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\). The nested worst-case value is \(V_0=(\rho_0\circ\rho_1\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T-1})(X)\). When the induced global model family is rectangular, this value also equals the supremum of \(E_Q[X]\) over all path measures obtained by selecting an admissible kernel from each \(\mathcal Q_t\) after every history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested worst-case model repeatedly takes the largest conditional expectation; under rectangularity, this equals worst-case expectation over all admissible pasted path models.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\).
Each conditional kernel set \(\mathcal Q_t\) is nonempty and yields well-defined conditional expectations.
The global kernel family is rectangular for the final equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_0=(\rho_0\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T-1})(X)=\sup_Q E_Q[X]\) over admissible pasted path measures.

notation.meaning: conditional set of admissible one-step kernels

review_flags: rectangular kernel representation requires source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested representation fits the container, but equivalence with a supremum over pasted path measures is a nontrivial rectangularity result not supported by the cited generic recursion locator.

children.title: Nested Spectral Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Recursive conditional spectral and quantile-weighted risk families.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Spectral Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive dynamic risk obtained by mixing conditional CVaR levels at each stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(t<T\), let \(\mu_t\) be a probability measure on \([0,1)\) and define the conditional spectral mapping \(\rho_t(Z)=\int_{[0,1)}\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\,\mu_t(d\alpha)\) for losses \(Z\) for which the integral is finite. Given terminal loss \(X\), set \(V_T=X\) and \(V_t=ho_t(V_{t+1})\). The resulting nested spectral risk is \(V_0=(\rho_0\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T-1})(X)\). Concentrating \(\mu_t\) at one level produces nested conditional CVaR, while concentrating it at \(0\) produces conditional expectation at that stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested spectral risk recursively applies mixtures of conditional CVaR levels; point-mass weights recover nested CVaR or conditional expectation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F_T)\) and every displayed spectral integral is finite.
Each \(\mu_t\) is a probability measure supported on \([0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_0=(\rho_0\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T-1})(X)\) is the nested spectral evaluation.

notation.meaning: stage-t mixing distribution over tail-probability levels

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral coherent risks are standard mixtures of CVaR, and dynamic nesting is defined by composition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and correctly recovers conditional CVaR and expectation through point masses, but no authoritative source is supplied for the conditional spectral representation and convention.

children.title: Polyhedral Dynamic Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Dynamic coherent models with finite-dimensional polyhedral risk envelopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Dynamic Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario conditional coherent risk represented by a polyhedral envelope of probability weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with \(m_t\) successor scenarios, let \(z\in\mathbb R^{m_t}\) be the vector of successor losses and let \(\mathcal U_t=\{q\in\mathbb R^{m_t}:q\ge0,\ \mathbf1^\top q=1,\ A_tq\le b_t\}\) be a nonempty polytope. The stage mapping \(\rho_t(z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal U_t}q^\top z\) is a finite-valued coherent risk functional. With \(V_T=X\) and \(V_t=\rho_t((V_{t+1,j})_{j=1}^{m_t})\), the dynamic model is a nested polyhedral risk model. Every stage evaluation is a linear program and attains its maximum at an extreme point of \(\mathcal U_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral dynamic risk model maximizes successor loss over a polytope of probability weights at every node and nests these linear programs backward.
assumptions_latex: Each node has finitely many successor scenarios.
\(\mathcal U_t\) is a nonempty polytope contained in the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal U_t}q^\top z\), and the maximum is attained at an extreme point of \(\mathcal U_t\).

notation.meaning: nested risk-adjusted value at stage t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: support functions of probability polytopes give coherent finite-scenario risks, and linear objectives attain maxima at polytope extreme points
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-scenario polyhedral-envelope representation, coherence claim, and extreme-point attainment are mathematically standard and fit the representation container, but the record lacks a citation.

children.title: Conditional CVaR Stage Mappings
children.top_down_role: One-step conditional tail-risk components used in the nested model.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional CVaR Stage Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step conditional tail-loss mapping used as a component of a nested multistage risk model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le\alpha<1\), a sub-sigma-algebra \(\mathcal F_t\), and an integrable loss \(Z\), define the conditional CVaR stage mapping by \[\rho_t^{\alpha}(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{\eta\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)}\left\{\eta+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}E[(Z-\eta)_+\mid\mathcal F_t]\right\}.\] Its value is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable. For \(\alpha=0\), \(\rho_t^0(Z)=E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]\). Applying mappings of this form successively to future losses defines a nested conditional-CVaR evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional CVaR minimizes an observable threshold plus scaled conditional expected excess loss; nesting these one-step mappings produces a dynamically recursive tail-risk model.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in L^1(\mathcal F_{t+1})\).
\(0\le\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t^{\alpha}(Z)\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\) is the conditional CVaR stage value, with \(\rho_t^0(Z)=E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]\).

notation.meaning: conditional CVaR mapping at stage t and level alpha

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed conditional Rockafellar–Uryasev formula is the standard one-step conditional CVaR representation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
