children.title: Risk-Placement Location Duality
children.top_down_role: Alternative locations of conditional CVaR within multistage aggregation.

children.title: Stage-Cost Risk Placement
children.top_down_role: Conditional risk applied to current-stage cost components.

knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Cost Risk Placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bellman representation placing the one-step stage loss inside the current conditional risk mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_t(x_t,u_t,\xi_{t+1})\) be the loss incurred between times \(t\) and \(t+1\), and let \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) be a conditional risk mapping. Stage-cost risk placement uses the recursion \[V_t(x_t)=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{u_t\in U_t(x_t)}\rho_t\!\left(c_t(x_t,u_t,\xi_{t+1})+V_{t+1}(x_{t+1})\right),\qquad V_T=c_T.\] Thus both the newly realized stage loss and the downstream value are inside the same one-step risk evaluation. This placement differs from adding an already known stage cost outside \(\rho_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stage-cost placement applies the current conditional risk mapping jointly to the next realized stage loss and the downstream value before minimizing over actions.
assumptions_latex: Admissible \(u_t\) are \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
The quantity inside \(\rho_t\) belongs to \(L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\).
The essential infimum is well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{u_t}\rho_t(c_t+V_{t+1})\) places the uncertain stage loss inside the time-t risk mapping.

notation.meaning: loss realized from stage t to stage t+1
risk-adjusted value function at time t

review_flags: exact stage-cost placement convention requires source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches stage-cost risk placement, but the state transition defining x_{t+1} is omitted and the cited generic section does not yet support this exact recursion. The comparison with placing a known cost outside rho_t also depends on conditional cash invariance.

children.title: Cost-to-Go Risk Placement
children.top_down_role: Conditional risk applied to continuation-value components.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-to-Go Risk Placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines nested conditional CVaR applied to the entire downstream cost-to-go.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\) be a filtration, let \(C_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\), and let \(\rho_t:L^1(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^1(\mathcal F_t)\) be conditional CVaR mappings. Cost-to-go risk placement is the backward recursion \[V_T=C_T,\qquad V_t=C_t+\rho_t(V_{t+1}),\quad t=T-1,\ldots,0.\] Thus every mapping \(\rho_t\) acts on the complete random continuation value \(V_{t+1}\), rather than only on the next isolated stage cost. The resulting time-zero criterion is \(V_0\), with minimization over admissible nonanticipative policies understood when the costs depend on decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost-to-go placement recursively applies each conditional CVaR mapping to the entire random continuation value, then adds the current known stage cost.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T\).
Each \(\rho_t\) is a well-defined conditional CVaR mapping from \(\mathcal F_{t+1}\) to \(\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t=C_t+\rho_t(V_{t+1})\) for \(t<T\), with \(V_T=C_T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, recursion, notation, and content kind fit the leaf, but no source is supplied for this cost-to-go placement convention or the nested conditional-CVaR recursion.

children.title: Risk-Placement Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interpretive and computational consequences of alternative placement choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Placement Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that moving CVaR across aggregated or separately assessed costs generally changes the criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Risk placement is not generally invariant under decomposition. Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be mutually exclusive losses satisfying \(\mathbb P(X=1,Y=0)=\mathbb P(X=0,Y=1)=1/2\). For upper-tail CVaR at confidence \(\alpha=1/2\), \[\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X)=\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(Y)=1,\qquad \operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X+Y)=1.\] Hence \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X+Y)\ne \operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X)+\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(Y)\). Consequently, applying risk separately to stage costs can differ from applying risk to an aggregated cost-to-go; equivalence requires additional structure, such as deterministic components or another condition yielding additivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CVaR is not additive, so assessing stage costs separately can produce a different value from assessing their aggregated cost-to-go.
assumptions_latex: CVaR uses the upper-tail loss convention.
\(X\) and \(Y\) have the stated two-outcome joint distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X+Y)\ne \operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X)+\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(Y)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the nonadditivity and risk-placement conclusion have no cited source.

children.title: Risk-Parameter Schedule Family
children.top_down_role: Stationary, stage-dependent, and state-dependent parameter regimes.

children.title: Confidence-Level Schedules
children.top_down_role: Stationary, stage-dependent, or state-dependent tail-confidence parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Level Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines stage-dependent confidence levels for a finite-horizon nested CVaR model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a horizon \(T\), a confidence-level schedule is a sequence \(\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{T-1})\in[0,1)^T\). At stage \(t\), the one-step conditional risk mapping is \[\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\] for each integrable \(\mathcal F_{t+1}\)-measurable loss \(Z\). The schedule may be constant, increasing, decreasing, or otherwise stage dependent. Values near zero approach conditional expectation, whereas values near one emphasize progressively smaller upper-tail events. The schedule is deterministic unless its predictability and admissible state dependence are specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A confidence-level schedule assigns each stage its own conditional-CVaR tail level, allowing risk sensitivity to vary over the horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\) and \(\alpha_t\in[0,1)\).
\(Z\in L^1(\mathcal F_{t+1})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\) for every \(t<T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The schedule definition is precise and locally appropriate, including the deterministic-schedule qualification, but no inspectable dynamic-CVaR source is cited.

children.title: Risk-Weight Schedules
children.top_down_role: Stationary, stage-dependent, or state-dependent risk-aversion weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Weight Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines stage-dependent mixtures of conditional expectation and conditional CVaR.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix confidence levels \(\alpha_t\in[0,1)\). A risk-weight schedule is a sequence \(\boldsymbol\lambda=(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_{T-1})\in[0,1]^T\) defining \[\rho_t(Z)=(1-\lambda_t)\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]+\lambda_t\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t),\qquad t<T,\] for integrable \(\mathcal F_{t+1}\)-measurable losses \(Z\). Here \(\lambda_t=0\) gives conditional expectation and \(\lambda_t=1\) gives pure conditional CVaR at stage \(t\); intermediate weights form a convex combination of the two conditional risk assessments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk-weight schedule controls, stage by stage, the mixture between conditional expectation and conditional CVaR.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda_t\in[0,1]\) and \(\alpha_t\in[0,1)\).
\(Z\in L^1(\mathcal F_{t+1})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t=(1-\lambda_t)\mathbb E[\,\cdot\mid\mathcal F_t]+\lambda_t\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal F_t)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mean-CVaR mixture and endpoint weights are correctly stated, and definition fits the leaf, but an authoritative source for this stage-dependent parameterization is missing.

children.title: Joint Schedule Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordinated variation of confidence levels and risk weights across stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Schedule Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterizes nested mean-CVaR models jointly by confidence and risk-weight schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\boldsymbol\alpha\in[0,1)^T\) and \(\boldsymbol\lambda\in[0,1]^T\). Their joint schedule induces one-step mappings \[\rho_t^{\alpha_t,\lambda_t}(Z)=(1-\lambda_t)\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]+\lambda_t\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t).\] Applied recursively as \(V_T=C_T\) and \(V_t=C_t+\rho_t^{\alpha_t,\lambda_t}(V_{t+1})\), the pair \((\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\lambda)\) specifies a joint regime. Risk neutrality occurs if every \(\lambda_t=0\) or every \(\alpha_t=0\); pure nested CVaR occurs if every \(\lambda_t=1\); heterogeneous pairs produce stage-dependent intermediate regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint confidence and weight schedules parameterize the full nested mean-CVaR recursion, including risk-neutral, pure-CVaR, and heterogeneous regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t\) and all recursively generated continuation values are integrable.
\(\alpha_t\in[0,1)\) and \(\lambda_t\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\lambda)\) determines the nested recursion \(V_t=C_t+\rho_t^{\alpha_t,\lambda_t}(V_{t+1})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint parameter representation and stated endpoint regimes are internally consistent, but neither the nested mean-CVaR recursion nor its joint scheduling interpretation is sourced.

children.title: Epigraph-Polyhedral Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional representations supporting scenario-tree and cutting-plane methods.

children.title: Epigraph Representations
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable representations of nested conditional risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the finite-support linear epigraph of a conditional CVaR mapping at one tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a scenario-tree node \(n\), let children \(m\in\mathcal C(n)\) have conditional probabilities \(p_{nm}>0\), losses \(z_m\), and \(\alpha_n\in[0,1)\). The bound \(v_n\ge\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_n}(z\mid n)\) holds exactly when there exist \(\eta_n\in\mathbb R\) and \(u_{nm}\ge0\) such that \[u_{nm}\ge z_m-\eta_n\quad(m\in\mathcal C(n)),\qquad v_n\ge\eta_n+\frac{1}{1-\alpha_n}\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}p_{nm}u_{nm}.\] Minimizing \(v_n\) makes these inequalities attain the conditional CVaR value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite scenario-tree branch, conditional CVaR has an exact linear epigraph using one threshold and nonnegative excess variables.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C(n)\) is finite and \(p_{nm}>0\) with \(\sum_m p_{nm}=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed linear system projects exactly onto \(v_n\ge\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_n}(z\mid n)\).

notation.meaning: conditional probability of child m given node n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-support CVaR epigraph formulation is mathematically standard and representation is the correct content kind, but the exact formula lacks a source with a specific locator.

children.title: Polyhedral Representations
children.top_down_role: Finite-dimensional piecewise-linear representations of nested risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the finite-support risk-envelope dual of conditional CVaR.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(n\), suppose the child losses are \(z_m\), conditional probabilities are \(p_{nm}>0\), and \(\alpha_n\in[0,1)\). Then \[\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_n}(z\mid n)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}q_m z_m,\] where \[\mathcal Q_n=\left\{q:\ \sum_m q_m=1,\quad 0\le q_m\le\frac{p_{nm}}{1-\alpha_n}\ \text{for every }m\right\}.\] Thus conditional CVaR is the worst conditional expectation over a polyhedral set of probability vectors absolutely continuous with respect to the nominal child distribution and having bounded likelihood ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional CVaR equals the largest expected child loss over a polyhedral set of probability distortions with bounded likelihood ratios.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C(n)\) is finite and the nominal conditional probabilities are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_n}(z\mid n)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sum_m q_mz_m\).

notation.meaning: conditional CVaR risk envelope at node n
distorted conditional probability of child m

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-support risk-envelope dual is correctly formulated and duality fits the leaf, but no source or locator supports the exact envelope constraints.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Representation regimes suited to finite scenario-tree formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes nodewise implementation of nested CVaR on a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite scenario tree represent \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\), with every nonleaf node \(n\) carrying conditional child probabilities \(p_{nm}\). A nested conditional-CVaR recursion is scenario-tree compatible when each one-step mapping uses only the values at \(\mathcal C(n)\) and their conditional probabilities. Introducing separate threshold and excess variables at every nonleaf node yields a finite linear extended formulation. Variables shared by scenarios with the same history are indexed by their common node, so nonanticipativity is preserved, and backward evaluation of the nodewise formulations reproduces the nested criterion at the root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested conditional CVaR can be represented nodewise on a finite scenario tree while preserving nonanticipativity and the backward recursion.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite and represents the filtration by node histories.
Each nonleaf node has normalized conditional child probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nodewise CVaR epigraph systems form a finite extended formulation whose root value equals the nested risk criterion.

notation.meaning: conditional transition probability from n to m

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited locator supports scenario-tree structure only; it does not support the nodewise CVaR extended formulation, preservation claim, or equality of its root value with the nested criterion.

children.title: Conditional Risk-Envelope Representation
children.top_down_role: Multiple-prior interpretation of the nested tail-risk model.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Risk-Envelope Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the multiple-prior interpretation of finite-support nested conditional CVaR.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonleaf node \(n\), define \(\mathcal Q_n=\{q:\sum_mq_m=1,\ 0\le q_m\le p_{nm}/(1-\alpha_n)\}\). Conditional CVaR satisfies \[\rho_n(Z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}q_mZ_m.\] Consequently, a nested composition of these mappings equals backward maximization over conditional probability selections \(q^n\in\mathcal Q_n\) at every reached node. Multiplying the selected conditional probabilities along root-to-leaf paths produces a rectangular family of joint scenario probabilities; the nested criterion is the worst expected total loss over this family, subject to the model's timing convention for stage costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested conditional CVaR is worst-case expectation over a rectangular family formed by choosing an admissible distorted conditional distribution at each node.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite with positive nominal conditional probabilities.
Each \(\alpha_n\in[0,1)\), and the nested recursion uses nodewise conditional CVaR.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nested criterion equals worst expected loss over the rectangular product of the nodewise envelopes \(\mathcal Q_n\).

notation.meaning: distorted conditional distribution selected at node n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nodewise envelope and rectangular multiple-prior interpretation match the terminal context, but the nontrivial equivalence between nested composition and worst-case expectation over rectangular product measures needs an authoritative source.

children.title: Risk-Neutral Worst-Case Limit Spectrum
children.top_down_role: Boundary regimes connecting nested CVaR with expectation and worst-case evaluation.

children.title: Risk-Neutral Limit
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes approaching expectation-based evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Neutral Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the expectation endpoint of the nested mean-CVaR parameter family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the one-step mapping \(\rho_t^{\alpha_t,\lambda_t}(Z)=(1-\lambda_t)\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]+\lambda_t\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\), risk neutrality holds whenever \(\lambda_t=0\), or whenever \(\alpha_t=0\) under the upper-tail CVaR convention. If this holds at every stage, then \[V_t=C_t+\mathbb E[V_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t],\qquad V_T=C_T,\] and repeated use of the tower property gives \(V_0=\mathbb E[\sum_{t=0}^TC_t\mid\mathcal F_0]\). Thus the nested model reduces to the ordinary risk-neutral expected-cost criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero CVaR weight or zero confidence at every stage reduces the nested model to ordinary conditional expectations and expected total cost.
assumptions_latex: All stage costs are integrable.
CVaR uses the upper-tail loss convention, for which \(\operatorname{CVaR}_0(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_0=\mathbb E[\sum_{t=0}^TC_t\mid\mathcal F_0]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The risk-neutral endpoints and tower-property reduction are correctly stated under the declared CVaR convention, but no source supports the endpoint identity and nested reduction.

children.title: Worst-Case Limit
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes approaching essential worst-case evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Limit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the essential-supremum endpoint as CVaR confidence tends to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_{t+1})\). Under the upper-tail loss convention, conditional CVaR is nondecreasing in \(\alpha\) and satisfies \[\lim_{\alpha\uparrow1}\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)=\operatorname{ess\,sup}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\quad\text{almost surely}.\] On a finite scenario tree with positive child probabilities, the conditional essential supremum is \(\max_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}Z_m\). Therefore, if every risk weight equals one and every confidence level tends to one, the nested CVaR recursion converges backward to the robust recursion \(V_t=C_t+\operatorname{ess\,sup}(V_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As every confidence level approaches one under pure CVaR weighting, nested CVaR approaches the stagewise worst-case recursion.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_{t+1})\).
For the nested limit, \(\lambda_t=1\) at every stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\to\operatorname{ess\,sup}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\) as \(\alpha\uparrow1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional essential-supremum limit and finite-tree interpretation are plausible and appropriately scoped, but the conditional limit and its propagation through the nested recursion require a cited source.

children.title: Intermediate Tail-Risk Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tail-risk behavior between expectation and worst-case endpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate Tail-Risk Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes parameter values lying strictly between expectation and worst-case assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integrable loss \(Z\), define \(\rho^{\alpha,\lambda}(Z)=(1-\lambda)\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F]+\lambda\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}(Z\mid\mathcal F)\), where \(0<\lambda\le1\) and \(0<\alpha<1\). Then \[\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F]\le\rho^{\alpha,\lambda}(Z)\le\operatorname{ess\,sup}(Z\mid\mathcal F)\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Moreover, \(\rho^{\alpha,\lambda}(Z)\) is nondecreasing in both \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\). Applying such mappings recursively yields intermediate nested tail-risk regimes; strict inequalities require nondegeneracy and that the selected tail parameters distinguish the conditional distribution from its mean and essential supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior confidence levels and positive risk weights produce conditional assessments between expectation and worst case, increasing with either parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in L^1\), with a finite conditional essential supremum for the upper bound.
\(0<\alpha<1\) and \(0<\lambda\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F]\le\rho^{\alpha,\lambda}(Z)\le\operatorname{ess\,sup}(Z\mid\mathcal F)\), monotonically in \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounds and parameter monotonicity are mathematically consistent under the stated finite-essential-supremum condition, but no source supports these properties or their nested-regime interpretation.

children.title: Nesting-Conservatism Boundary
children.top_down_role: Interpretive and computational limits created by repeated tail-risk composition.

children.title: Nesting Depth Effects
children.top_down_role: Risk behavior induced by repeated conditional composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Nesting Depth Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of replacing conditional expectations by conditional CVaR operators in a finite loss recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F_T)\), and let each backward operator be either \(E_t(X)=\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal F_t]\) or \(C_t^\alpha(X)=\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(X\mid\mathcal F_t)\), where \(0\leq\alpha<1\). For two compositions \(R^{(d)}\) and \(R^{(d+1)}\) having the same stage order, suppose the latter replaces one occurrence of \(E_t\) by \(C_t^\alpha\) and leaves all other operators unchanged. Conditional CVaR dominates conditional expectation and every operator is monotone; hence \[R^{(d+1)}(X)\geq R^{(d)}(X)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Repeated replacements therefore produce a nondecreasing sequence of recursively evaluated losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each additional replacement of conditional expectation by conditional CVaR can only increase the recursively evaluated loss; deeper CVaR nesting is therefore weakly more conservative.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F_T)\).
\(0\leq\alpha<1\).
All operators use the loss convention and are composed in temporal order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^{(d+1)}(X)\geq R^{(d)}(X)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Conditional expectation given the stage-t information
Conditional CVaR at confidence level alpha
A temporal composition containing d conditional-CVaR substitutions

review_flags: Exact nested-CVaR monotonicity source and locator are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no citation supports the conditional-CVaR dominance and composition claim.

children.title: Conservatism Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits beyond which nesting produces excessive risk sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Conservatism Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary cases where nested conditional CVaR ceases to exceed risk-neutral conditional expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the loss convention, conditional CVaR satisfies \[\mathbb E[X\mid\mathcal F_t]=\operatorname{CVaR}_0(X\mid\mathcal F_t)\leq\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(X\mid\mathcal F_t),\qquad 0\leq\alpha<1.\] Consequently, a finite nested-CVaR recursion weakly dominates the corresponding recursion of conditional expectations. The conservatism gap vanishes when every confidence level equals zero. It also vanishes at any node whose continuation loss is conditionally constant, because both conditional operators then return that constant. Outside these boundary cases strictness is distribution-dependent: positive conditional tail dispersion may create a strict gap, but nesting alone does not guarantee one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested CVaR reduces to risk-neutral evaluation at level zero and adds no local conservatism for conditionally deterministic continuation losses; otherwise the gap may be strict.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F_T)\).
Conditional CVaR is parameterized by confidence level \(\alpha\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nested conditional CVaR weakly dominates conditional expectation, with equality in the stated boundary cases.
review_flags: A source explicitly covering conditional-CVaR equality and strictness boundaries is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, but the conditional equality and strictness conditions require an authoritative source; the distinction between a local zero gap and equality of the entire recursion should also be confirmed.

children.title: Composition-Induced Distortion
children.top_down_role: Interpretive or computational distortion created by repeated tail-risk evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Composition-Induced Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-stage tree showing that nested CVaR need not equal static CVaR of terminal loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider four equiprobable terminal leaves grouped into two equally likely stage-one branches. In branch \(A\), let terminal losses be \(0\) and \(100\); in branch \(B\), let both losses equal \(50\). At confidence level \(\alpha=1/2\), the conditional CVaRs at stage one are \(100\) and \(50\). Applying root CVaR again gives \[\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}\bigl(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X\mid\mathcal F_1)\bigr)=100.\] The static terminal distribution is uniform on \(\{0,50,50,100\}\), so \[\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X)=75.\] Thus recursive composition changes the tail weighting and strictly exceeds static CVaR.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a four-leaf tree, nested half-level CVaR equals 100 while static half-level CVaR equals 75, demonstrating composition-induced tail distortion.
assumptions_latex: All four terminal leaves have probability \(1/4\).
CVaR uses the average-loss-above-quantile convention, including the required quantile mass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X\mid\mathcal F_1))=100>75=\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(X)\).
review_flags: The explicit counterexample is directly checkable but lacks an external source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally consistent and the content kind fits, but it has no external source or registered evidence locator.

children.title: Expected Conditional Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Multiperiod risk models that aggregate conditional risk evaluations through expectation-based structures.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Risk Aversion in Multistage Stochastic Programming: A Modeling and Algorithmic Perspective

children.title: Stagewise Expected Conditional Risk
children.top_down_role: Expected aggregation of stage-indexed conditional risk contributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Expected Conditional Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive scalar aggregation of stage-indexed conditional risk contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a filtered probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\), let \(Z_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\) be the stage-t loss and let \(\rho_{t-1,t}:L^1(\mathcal F_t)\to L^1(\mathcal F_{t-1})\) be a conditional risk mapping. For deterministic weights \(w_t\geq0\), the stagewise expected conditional-risk functional is \[J_{m EC}(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T)=\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\,\mathbb E\!\left[\rho_{t-1,t}(Z_t)\right].\] It evaluates each stage loss conditionally on prior information and then averages and adds the resulting contributions; it does not recursively insert future risk evaluations into earlier mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate each stage loss by a one-step conditional risk mapping, take its expectation, and sum the weighted scalar contributions without recursive nesting.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
\(\rho_{t-1,t}(Z_t)\in L^1(\mathcal F_{t-1})\).
\(w_t\geq0\) are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_{\rm EC}=\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\mathbb E[\rho_{t-1,t}(Z_t)]\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory does not contain a locator for this specific expected-conditional aggregation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent definition of a nonrecursive stagewise aggregate, but a source is needed to establish that this particular functional and terminology represent the intended model family.

children.title: Expected Conditional CVaR Models
children.top_down_role: Expected conditional-risk models using CVaR as the local risk component.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Conditional CVaR Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational representation of an expected conditional-CVaR stagewise objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For confidence levels \(\alpha_t\in[0,1)\), define the conditional CVaR of \(Z_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\) by \[\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{\eta_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_{t-1})}\left\{\eta_t+\frac{1}{1-\alpha_t}\mathbb E[(Z_t-\eta_t)_+\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\right\}.\] An expected conditional-CVaR model minimizes \[J_{\rm ECC}(Z)=\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\,\mathbb E[\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})].\] Equivalently, it minimizes jointly over adapted thresholds \((\eta_t)\) the expectation of the displayed hinge-loss expressions, summed across stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected conditional CVaR is a weighted sum of expected one-step conditional CVaRs and admits an adapted threshold-plus-hinge variational formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_t\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)\).
\(0\leq\alpha_t<1\) and \(w_t\geq0\).
Each threshold \(\eta_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional-CVaR objective equals the joint adapted-threshold variational problem.
review_flags: A source for the conditional essential-infimum CVaR representation is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the container, but the conditional essential-infimum formula, admissible threshold space, integrability conditions, and interchange with stagewise expectation require a precise source.

children.title: Nested versus Expected-Conditional Modeling Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of recursive consistency, conservatism, and algorithmic coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested versus Expected-Conditional Modeling Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural distinction between recursive and additively aggregated conditional-risk models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one-step conditional risk mappings be \(\rho_{t,t+1}\). The nested evaluation is defined backward by \(V_T=Z_T\) and \(V_t=Z_t+\rho_{t,t+1}(V_{t+1})\); its continuation evaluation is therefore recursively consistent with the same mappings. By contrast, \[J_{\rm EC}=\sum_{t=1}^T w_t\mathbb E[\rho_{t-1,t}(Z_t)]\] is additively separable across stagewise risk terms and introduces no risk-composition coupling. In general these functionals are unequal: composition reweights continuation tails, whereas expected-conditional aggregation evaluates only local stage losses. Equality requires additional structure, such as risk-neutral mappings or conditionally deterministic continuation losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nesting supplies recursive consistency but couples future tail evaluations; expected-conditional aggregation is stage-separable but generally defines a different, nonrecursive objective.
assumptions_latex: All displayed conditional risk evaluations are finite.
The same filtered loss process is used in both constructions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nested and expected-conditional objectives generally differ, coinciding only under additional degeneracy or risk-neutrality conditions.

notation.meaning: Nested continuation loss at stage t

review_flags: The locator supports the recursive/nonrecursive distinction provisionally; exact conditional-risk hypotheses require checking.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section provisionally supports a recursive/nonrecursive distinction, but not the exact conditional-risk formulas or equality claim. Risk-neutral equality additionally depends on aligned weights, treatment of the stage-zero loss, and a scalar initial information state.

children.title: Dynamic Convex Risk Model Family
children.top_down_role: Recursive nonlinear risk systems beyond positive homogeneity.

children.title: Dynamic Entropic Risk
children.top_down_role: Recursive exponential-risk evaluation and its state-based interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Entropic Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon recursive entropic evaluation for an adapted loss stream.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an adapted loss stream \((Z_t)_{t=0}^T\) and risk-aversion parameters \(\gamma_t>0\), define \(V_T=Z_T\) and recursively \[V_t=Z_t+\frac{1}{\gamma_t}\log\mathbb E\!\left[\exp(\gamma_t V_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t\right],\qquad t=T-1,\ldots,0.\] Whenever the conditional exponential moments are finite, \(V_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and gives the dynamic entropic loss from stage \(t\). In a controlled Markov model, if the conditional law of the next state depends only on the current state and action, the conditional logarithmic moment becomes a state-action risk operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic entropic risk recursively adds current loss to the conditional logarithmic exponential moment of the next-stage risk value.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
\(\gamma_t>0\).
\(\mathbb E[\exp(\gamma_tV_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t]<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t=Z_t+\gamma_t^{-1}\log\mathbb E[\exp(\gamma_tV_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t]\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the dynamic entropic recursion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is suitable and internally coherent, but no locator supports the stated finite-horizon recursion or its Markov state-action interpretation.

children.title: Dynamic Optimized Certainty Equivalents
children.top_down_role: Recursive certainty-equivalent models generated by convex loss families.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Optimized Certainty Equivalents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive conditional optimized certainty equivalent generated by stage-dependent convex loss functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell_t:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and nondecreasing, with \(\ell_t(0)=0\) and \(1\in\partial\ell_t(0)\). For \(X\in L^1(\mathcal F_{t+1})\), define the conditional optimized certainty equivalent \[\rho_t^{\ell_t}(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{m\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)}\left\{m+\mathbb E[\ell_t(X-m)\mid\mathcal F_t]\right\}.\] Given losses \((Z_t)_{t=0}^T\), the dynamic OCE is \(V_T=Z_T\) and \(V_t=Z_t+\rho_t^{\ell_t}(V_{t+1})\). Thus each recursion stage optimizes an information-adapted cash offset before applying its convex loss function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic OCE recursively applies a conditional cash-offset minimization generated by a convex nondecreasing loss function.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell_t\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and nondecreasing.
\(\ell_t(0)=0\) and \(1\in\partial\ell_t(0)\).
All conditional expectations and essential infima are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t=Z_t+\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{m\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)}\{m+\mathbb E[\ell_t(V_{t+1}-m)\mid\mathcal F_t]\}\).
review_flags: The precise conditional OCE normalization and domain need an authoritative source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the normalization, conditional domain, admissible cash-offset space, finiteness assumptions, and recursive construction need authoritative support.

children.title: Penalized Multiple-Prior Models
children.top_down_role: Dynamic convex risk represented by model alternatives with intertemporal penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Multiple-Prior Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convex-risk representation by alternative probability models and time-consistent penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\), a conditional convex loss-risk mapping with the Fatou property admits the representation \[\rho_t(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_t}\left\{\mathbb E_Q[X\mid\mathcal F_t]-\alpha_t(Q)\right\},\] where every \(Q\) is absolutely continuous with respect to \(P\), agrees with \(P\) on \(\mathcal F_t\), and \(\alpha_t(Q)\) is an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable penalty. For a time-consistent family, minimal penalties satisfy the cocycle relation \[\alpha_{s,u}(Q)=\alpha_{s,t}(Q)+\mathbb E_Q[\alpha_{t,u}(Q)\mid\mathcal F_s],\qquad s\leq t\leq u.\] The penalty therefore allocates model ambiguity consistently across time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic convex risk is the worst penalized conditional expectation over alternative priors; time consistency corresponds to additive conditional decomposition of minimal penalties.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in L^\infty(\mathcal F_T)\).
Each conditional risk mapping is proper, convex, cash-invariant, monotone, and has the Fatou property.
The prior sets are stable under the pasting operations required for time consistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t\) has the penalized-prior representation, with time consistency encoded by the penalty cocycle.

notation.meaning: Admissible alternative priors agreeing with the reference history through t
Conditional penalty assigned to prior Q

review_flags: An authoritative source for the conditional dual representation and penalty cocycle is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality role is appropriate, but the exact conditional Fatou representation and the hypotheses connecting time consistency, pasting stability, and the minimal-penalty cocycle require a specific source.

children.title: Finite-Horizon Markov Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Stage-indexed Markov risk over finite decision horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Markov Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-sensitive Bellman recursion for a finite-horizon controlled Markov process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given horizon \(T\), state spaces \(S_t\), feasible actions \(A_t(s)\), costs \(c_t(s,a)\), transition kernels \(P_t(\cdot\mid s,a)\), terminal cost \(g_T\), and Markov conditional-risk operators \(\rho_{t,s,a}\), initialize \(V_T(s)=g_T(s)\). For \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\), compute \[V_t(s)=\inf_{a\in A_t(s)}\left\{c_t(s,a)+\rho_{t,s,a}(V_{t+1}(S_{t+1}))\right\}.\] Select a minimizing measurable action \(\pi_t(s)\) when it exists. Output \((V_0,\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{T-1})\); otherwise output infimal values and stagewise minimizing sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward induction replaces conditional expectation in the finite-horizon Bellman equation by a state-action conditional-risk operator and returns a Markov policy.
assumptions_latex: The controlled process is Markov under \(P_t(\cdot\mid s,a)\).
Each displayed risk evaluation is well-defined.
Measurable minimizers exist when an exact policy is claimed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backward recursion returns the finite-horizon Markov risk values and associated minimizing Markov policy.
review_flags: The locators provisionally support finite-horizon dynamic programming; the risk-operator extension requires source verification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the cited general dynamic-programming sections do not establish the risk-operator Bellman recursion or its policy-optimality conditions. A risk-sensitive Markov control source is required.

children.title: Discounted Infinite-Horizon Markov Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Stationary recursive risk under discounted long-horizon evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Discounted Infinite-Horizon Markov Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sup-norm contraction and stationary fixed point for discounted Markov risk recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the state and action sets be finite, let \(0<\beta<1\), and let bounded one-stage costs be \(c(s,a)\). Suppose every Markov risk operator \(\rho_{s,a}\) is monotone and cash-invariant. Define \[(Tv)(s)=\min_{a\in A(s)}\{c(s,a)+\beta\rho_{s,a}(v(S'))\}.\] Then \(T\) is a \(\beta\)-contraction on the bounded value functions under the supremum norm. Hence there is a unique bounded fixed point \(V^*=TV^*\), value iteration \(V_{n+1}=TV_n\) converges to \(V^*\) from every bounded \(V_0\), and any stationary selector attaining the minimum is optimal for the recursive discounted criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discounting makes the stationary Markov risk Bellman operator a contraction, yielding a unique value, convergent value iteration, and an optimal stationary selector.
assumptions_latex: The state and action sets are finite and \(c\) is bounded.
Each \(\rho_{s,a}\) is monotone and cash-invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) has a unique bounded fixed point and \(\lVert T^nv-V^*\rVert_\infty\leq\beta^n\lVert v-V^*\rVert_\infty\).
review_flags: The locator provisionally supports discounted infinite-horizon recursion; explicit risk-operator contraction coverage must be checked.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is mathematically plausible, but the cited generic infinite-horizon section does not specifically support contraction for monotone cash-invariant risk operators or optimality for the recursive risk criterion.

children.title: Transient Markov Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Long-horizon Markov models governed by risk-transience structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Transient Markov Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-transience on nonabsorbing states via summability of iterated Markov risk transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_0\) be the nonabsorbing states of a Markov model with an absorbing zero-cost state, and fix a stationary policy \(\pi\). For a nonnegative function \(v\) extended by zero at the absorbing state, define the coherent risk-transition operator \[(\mathcal R_\pi v)(s)=\rho_{s,\pi(s)}(v(S')),\qquad s\in S_0.\] The policy-induced model is risk-transient if \[\sup_{N\geq1}\left\lVert\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathcal R_\pi^k\mathbf1_{S_0}\right\rVert_\infty<\infty.\] A controlled model is uniformly risk-transient over a policy class if the same bound holds uniformly over all policies in that class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Markov risk model is transient when cumulative iterates of its nonabsorbing-state risk-transition operator remain uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: There is an absorbing state with zero continuation value.
\(\rho_{s,a}\) is a coherent one-step Markov risk mapping on nonnegative continuation values.
Functions on nonabsorbing states are extended by zero at the absorbing state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Risk-transience is the boundedness of \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathcal R_\pi^k\mathbf1_{S_0}\) uniformly in \(N\).

notation.meaning: Unit continuation value on nonabsorbing states

review_flags: The supplied Markov-chain locators do not establish this specialized risk-transience definition.
The exact policy class and functional norm require source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the transient-model leaf, but this specialized nonlinear risk-transience criterion, its operator domain, norm, and uniform policy class require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Undiscounted Markov Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Long-horizon Markov risk models without discount contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Undiscounted Markov Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-horizon, discrete-time Markov model without geometric discounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_t\) be a controlled Markov process, let \(c(s,a)\ge 0\), and let \(\rho_{s,a}\) be a monotone conditional one-step risk map for the next-state cost. For a Markov policy \(\pi\), define \(V_N^\pi=0\) and recursively \(V_t^\pi(s)=c(s,\pi_t(s))+\rho_{s,\pi_t(s)}(V_{t+1}^\pi(S_{t+1}))\) for \(t=N-1,\ldots,0\). The undiscounted infinite-horizon risk value is \(J^\pi(s)=\limsup_{N\to\infty}V_0^\pi(s)\), possibly extended-valued, and the control problem is \(J^*(s)=\inf_\pi J^\pi(s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undiscounted Markov risk model minimizes the limiting nested risk of accumulated nonnegative stage costs, with no geometric attenuation.
assumptions_latex: \(S_t\) is a controlled discrete-time Markov process.
\(c:S\times A\to[0,\infty]\) is measurable.
Each \(\rho_{s,a}\) is a well-defined monotone conditional risk map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J^*(s)=\inf_\pi\limsup_{N\to\infty}V_0^\pi(s)\).

notation.meaning: Finite-horizon nested risk value under policy π

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Markov chains with discrete time p. 58

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Markov chains with discrete time p. 58

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited Markov-chain section does not support the nested risk recursion or its infinite-horizon limit. Monotonicity alone is insufficient to justify interpreting the recursion as accumulated-cost risk, and the finite-horizon values should carry an N index. An authoritative source must determine the intended risk-map assumptions and limit convention.

children.title: Risk-Transience Regime
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions controlling long-run undiscounted risk accumulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Transience Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted transience condition for an undiscounted Markov risk operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a stationary policy \(\pi\), a measurable weight \(w:S\to[1,\infty)\), and the positive Markov risk operator \((\mathcal R^\pi v)(s)=\rho_{s,\pi(s)}(v(S_1))\) for nonnegative measurable \(v\). The policy is risk-transient relative to \(w\) if there exists \(K<\infty\) such that, for every \(N\ge0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{N}(\mathcal R^\pi)^k\mathbf 1(s)\le K w(s)\) for all \(s\in S\). A policy class is uniformly risk-transient when the same \(K\) and \(w\) work for every policy in the class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk transience requires uniformly bounded accumulated iterates of the one-step risk operator in a weighted state norm.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R^\pi\) maps nonnegative measurable functions to nonnegative measurable functions.
\(w(s)\ge1\) for every \(s\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{N\ge0}w(s)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N}(\mathcal R^\pi)^k\mathbf 1(s)\le K\).

notation.meaning: One-step risk transition operator under π

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but this particular transience criterion for iterates of a possibly nonlinear risk operator is not sufficiently standard to accept without an authoritative definition. A source must confirm whether the bound uses the constant function, a weighted operator norm, or another risk-transience formulation.

children.title: Terminal Total-Cost Risk
children.top_down_role: A horizon-wide risk criterion applied to accumulated path cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Total-Cost Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single terminal risk functional applied after aggregating all stage costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a filtered probability space with horizon \(T\), let an admissible policy \(\pi\) generate integrable stage costs \(C_t^\pi\). Given a scalar risk functional \(\rho:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), the terminal total-cost risk criterion is \(J_{\mathrm{term}}(\pi)=\rho(\sum_{t=0}^{T}C_t^\pi)\). The associated optimization problem minimizes \(J_{\mathrm{term}}(\pi)\) over admissible nonanticipative policies. Risk is applied once to the complete path cost rather than recursively during the horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entire accumulated path cost is formed first and then evaluated by one terminal risk functional.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t^\pi\in L^p(\mathcal F_T)\) for every stage.
\(\pi\) is admissible and nonanticipative.
\(\rho\) is defined on the accumulated cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\pi}J_{\mathrm{term}}(\pi)=\inf_{\pi}\rho(\sum_{t=0}^{T}C_t^\pi)\).

notation.meaning: Stage-t cost induced by policy π

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit terminal placement of total-cost risk, but no inspectable citation supports the precise formulation or domain conventions.

children.title: Stagewise Risk Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Separate stage-cost risk evaluations combined across the horizon.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Risk Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive aggregation of separately evaluated stage-cost risks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_t^\pi\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) be the cost at stage \(t\), let \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_t)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a scalar risk functional, and let \(\lambda_t\ge0\). The stagewise risk-aggregation criterion is \(J_{\mathrm{stage}}(\pi)=\sum_{t=0}^{T}\lambda_t\rho_t(C_t^\pi)\). Each cost is evaluated separately before aggregation; consequently this criterion generally differs from applying one risk functional to \(\sum_t C_t^\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each stage cost receives its own risk evaluation, and the resulting scalar risks are combined with nonnegative weights.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t^\pi\) belongs to the domain of \(\rho_t\).
\(\lambda_t\ge0\) for every \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_{\mathrm{stage}}(\pi)=\sum_{t=0}^{T}\lambda_t\rho_t(C_t^\pi)\).

notation.meaning: Risk functional assigned to stage t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches stagewise aggregation and is mathematically coherent, but the record supplies no source for this particular weighted scalar-risk formulation.

children.title: Nested Cost-to-Go Risk
children.top_down_role: Recursive risk evaluation aligned with cost-to-go structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Cost-to-Go Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon recursive composition of conditional one-step risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{T}\) be a filtration, let \(C_t^\pi\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), and let \(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) be conditional risk mappings. Set \(V_T^\pi=C_T^\pi\) and define \(V_t^\pi=C_t^\pi+\rho_t(V_{t+1}^\pi)\) for \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\). The nested cost-to-go risk is \(J_{\mathrm{nest}}(\pi)=V_0^\pi\), equivalently \(C_0^\pi+\rho_0(C_1^\pi+\rho_1(\cdots+\rho_{T-1}(C_T^\pi)))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Future costs are evaluated recursively by conditional risk maps, producing an adapted risk-valued cost-to-go at every stage.
assumptions_latex: \(C_t^\pi\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\).
\(\rho_t:L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) is well defined.
\(\mathcal F_0\) is trivial when a scalar objective is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_{\mathrm{nest}}(\pi)=C_0^\pi+\rho_0(C_1^\pi+\rho_1(\cdots+\rho_{T-1}(C_T^\pi)))\).

notation.meaning: Nested risk cost-to-go at stage t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive definition and selected knowledge kind fit the container, but an authoritative source is required for the conditional-risk recursion and its function-space conventions.

children.title: Multistage Mean–Risk Models
children.top_down_role: Models combining expected performance and a separate multistage risk component.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Mean–Risk Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected total performance combined with a separately weighted multistage risk term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible policy \(\pi\), let \(Z^\pi=\sum_{t=0}^{T}C_t^\pi\) and let \(\mathcal R(C_0^\pi,\ldots,C_T^\pi)\) be a specified scalar multistage risk functional, such as a terminal, stagewise, or nested criterion. For \(\lambda\ge0\), a multistage mean–risk model minimizes \(J_\lambda(\pi)=\mathbb E[Z^\pi]+\lambda\mathcal R(C_0^\pi,\ldots,C_T^\pi)\). The parameter \(\lambda\) controls the tradeoff between expected total cost and the distinct risk component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective adds expected total cost to a nonnegative multiple of a separately specified multistage risk measure.
assumptions_latex: \(Z^\pi\) is integrable for every admissible \(\pi\).
\(\mathcal R\) is defined on the induced cost stream.
\(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_\pi J_\lambda(\pi)=\inf_\pi\{\mathbb E[Z^\pi]+\lambda\mathcal R(C_0^\pi,\ldots,C_T^\pi)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes a plausible mean–risk model, but no source establishes that the broad terminal, stagewise, and nested alternatives are all intended instances of this exact model family.

children.title: Dynamic Risk Constraint-Budget System

children.title: Dynamic Risk Constraints
children.top_down_role: Stagewise or conditional risk restrictions within feasible-policy systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Risk Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapted upper bounds on conditional risks of future accumulated costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t^\pi=\sum_{k=t}^{T}C_k^\pi\) denote the remaining cost and let \(\rho_{t,T}:L^p(\mathcal F_T)\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) be a conditional risk functional. Given an adapted threshold process \(b_t\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), the policy \(\pi\) satisfies the dynamic risk constraints if \(\rho_{t,T}(G_t^\pi)\le b_t\) almost surely for every \(t=0,\ldots,T\). Thus feasibility is checked conditionally at each information state, not solely at the initial stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every stage, the conditional risk of remaining cost must not exceed the currently available adapted threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(G_t^\pi\) belongs to the domain of \(\rho_{t,T}\).
\(b_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
\(\pi\) is nonanticipative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{t,T}(G_t^\pi)\le b_t\ \text{a.s. for all }t=0,\ldots,T\).

notation.meaning: Conditional risk of a terminal-horizon quantity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits dynamic risk constraints, but the precise remaining-cost constraint imposed at every stage is one model variant and requires a source defining its conditional-risk and feasibility conventions.

children.title: Dynamic Risk Budgets
children.top_down_role: Intertemporal limits governing allowable risk exposure.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Risk Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapted resources that bound conditional future risk throughout the horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dynamic risk budget is a nonnegative adapted process \((B_t)_{t=0}^{T}\), with \(B_t\in L^p_+(\mathcal F_t)\), assigned to a policy and conditional risk system. It is feasible for \(\pi\) when \(\rho_{t,T}(\sum_{k=t}^{T}C_k^\pi)\le B_t\) almost surely for every \(t\). If budgets are decision variables, their admissible set must additionally specify an initial cap or an interstage update rule; without such a restriction, arbitrarily large budgets make the constraints vacuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic risk budget is an adapted nonnegative threshold process that bounds remaining conditional risk at every stage.
assumptions_latex: \(B_t\in L^p_+(\mathcal F_t)\).
The conditional risks are defined for all remaining-cost variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{t,T}(\sum_{k=t}^{T}C_k^\pi)\le B_t\ \text{a.s. for every }t\).

notation.meaning: Risk budget available at stage t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold-process definition is plausible, but without an initial cap or interstage update rule it does not fully characterize a dynamic budget system. A source is needed to select the intended budget dynamics.

children.title: Budget Allocation Across Stages
children.top_down_role: Distribution of aggregate risk capacity across stages, states, or policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Budget Allocation Across Stages
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon allocation of a total risk allowance among stage constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\ge0\) be a total risk allowance and let \(r_t(\pi)\ge0\) be the scalar risk charge assigned to stage \(t\). A stage allocation is a vector \(\beta\in\mathbb R_+^{T+1}\) satisfying \(\sum_{t=0}^{T}\beta_t\le B\). The policy-allocation pair \((\pi,\beta)\) is feasible when \(r_t(\pi)\le\beta_t\) for every \(t\). Consequently, feasibility implies \(\sum_{t=0}^{T}r_t(\pi)\le B\); conversely, any nonnegative charges with this aggregate bound admit the allocation \(\beta_t=r_t(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative stage allowances sum to at most the total budget and individually dominate their corresponding risk charges.
assumptions_latex: \(r_t(\pi)\ge0\) for every stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_t(\pi)\le\beta_t\ \forall t\ \text{and}\ \sum_t\beta_t\le B\implies\sum_t r_t(\pi)\le B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic allocation statement is correct, but it is a static scalar allocation model and is not demonstrably the intended dynamic, stage-coupled budget allocation without a supporting source.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Scenario-Tree Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario-tree extensive form for nested coherent conditional risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite rooted scenario tree. For each nonleaf node \(n\), let \(\mathcal C(n)\) be its children and let \(\mathcal Q_n\) be a risk envelope of probability vectors on \(\mathcal C(n)\). With node decisions \(x_n\), costs \(c_n(x_n)\), and leaf values \(V_n=c_n(x_n)\), the nested coherent-risk problem has the extensive representation minimizing \(V_r\) subject to \(V_n\ge c_n(x_n)+\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}q_mV_m\) for every \(q\in\mathcal Q_n\) and every nonleaf \(n\), together with nodewise feasibility and shared decisions at indistinguishable histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite nested coherent-risk problem becomes a nodewise extensive model with one epigraph inequality for every local risk-envelope distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is finite.
Each conditional risk map is coherent with envelope \(\mathcal Q_n\).
Node decisions satisfy nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min V_r\ \text{subject to}\ V_n\ge c_n(x_n)+\sum_{m\in\mathcal C(n)}q_mV_m\ \forall q\in\mathcal Q_n\).

notation.meaning: Conditional risk envelope at node n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but the cited scenario-tree section supports tree structure only, not the coherent-risk envelope epigraph representation. A risk-specific source is required.

children.title: Risk-Averse Bellman Form
