knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Bellman Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon Bellman recursion with a conditional Markov risk operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(t=0,\ldots,T\), let \(S_t\) be a controlled Markov state, let \(A_t(s)\) be the feasible action set, and let \(\rho_{t,s,a}\) evaluate functions of the next state conditionally on \((s,a)\). With terminal cost \(g\), define \(V_T(s)=g(s)\) and \(V_t(s)=\inf_{a\in A_t(s)}\{c_t(s,a)+\rho_{t,s,a}(V_{t+1}(S_{t+1}))\}\). Under Markov sufficiency and time-consistent nested risk evaluation, \(V_0(S_0)\) equals the optimal nested risk, and measurable minimizers define an optimal Markov policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal nested risk is computed backward by minimizing current cost plus conditional risk of the next-stage value.
assumptions_latex: The controlled process is Markov and feasible actions depend on the current state.
The risk criterion is a time-consistent composition of Markov conditional maps.
The displayed infima and required measurable selectors are well defined.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bellman recursion is a suitable representation, but the equality with the optimal nested risk and existence of optimal measurable Markov selectors are theorem-level claims whose stated hypotheses are too generic and uncited.

children.title: Risk-Envelope Minimax Form
children.top_down_role: Adversarial probability-model representation of coherent multistage risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope Minimax Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular adversarial-kernel representation of nested coherent Markov risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every one-step coherent conditional risk map has the dual form \(\rho_{t,s,a}(Z)=\sup_{q\in\mathcal Q_t(s,a)}\mathbb E_q[Z]\), where \(\mathcal Q_t(s,a)\) is a nonempty risk envelope of next-state laws. If these envelopes are rectangular across stages, then for every admissible policy \(\pi\), its nested risk equals \(\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q(\pi)}\mathbb E_Q[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(S_t,A_t)+g(S_T)]\), where \(\mathfrak Q(\pi)\) consists of path laws formed by selecting a kernel from each local envelope. Hence the control problem is the minimax problem \(\inf_\pi\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q(\pi)}\mathbb E_Q[\sum_t c_t+g]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested coherent risk equals worst-case expected total cost over path laws assembled from rectangular local risk envelopes.
assumptions_latex: Each one-step conditional risk map is coherent and admits the stated envelope representation.
Every local envelope is nonempty.
The family of local envelopes is rectangular across stages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_\pi\mathcal R^\pi=\inf_\pi\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q(\pi)}\mathbb E_Q[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}c_t(S_t,A_t)+g(S_T)]\).

notation.meaning: Rectangular family of induced path laws

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind matches the minimax container, but the path-law equivalence requires precise conditional dual-representation, measurability, integrability, and rectangularity hypotheses. No source is supplied for these theorem-level claims.

children.title: Nonanticipativity-Dual Form
children.top_down_role: Scenario-separable representations based on dualized information constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity-Dual Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian dualization of scenario-tree nonanticipativity constraints in a finite convex multistage model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a finite scenario set, let \(X_\omega\) be the feasible policy set for scenario \(\omega\), and let \(A x=0\) collect equalities identifying decisions at nodes with identical observed histories. For \(F(x)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}p_\omega f_\omega(x_\omega)\), strong Lagrangian duality gives
\[
\inf_{x_\omega\in X_\omega,\,Ax=0}F(x)
=
\sup_{\lambda}\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\inf_{x_\omega\in X_\omega}
\bigl(p_\omega f_\omega(x_\omega)+\langle A_\omega^{\mathsf T}\lambda,x_\omega\rangle\bigr).
\]
Thus fixing \(\lambda\) separates the inner problem by scenario, while the dual multipliers price violations of nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing nonanticipativity equalities yields scenario-separable subproblems; maximizing their summed Lagrangian values recovers the convex primal value under strong duality.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) is finite, \(p_\omega>0\), and \(\sum_\omega p_\omega=1\).
Each \(X_\omega\) is nonempty and convex, and each \(f_\omega\) is proper, closed, and convex.
A standard relative-interior constraint qualification holds and the primal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{F(x):x_\omega\in X_\omega,\ Ax=0\}=\sup_\lambda\inf_x\{F(x)+\langle\lambda,Ax\rangle\}\), with a scenario-separable inner infimum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality statement and content kind fit the nonanticipativity-dual container, but no source is supplied for the stated constraint qualification, strong-duality identity, or scenario decomposition.

children.title: Risk-Averse Multistage Geometry
children.top_down_role: Model structures governing convexity, recourse, state sufficiency, and decomposability.

children.title: Linear-Polyhedral Recourse Geometry
children.top_down_role: Piecewise-linear risk-adjusted value-function structure.

children.title: Linear Recourse Geometry
children.top_down_role: Risk-adjusted recourse systems with linear stage structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Recourse Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric linear-programming representation of a one-stage recourse value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed data \(q,W,h,T\), define the extended-real recourse function
\[
Q(x)=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy=h-Tx,\ y\geq0\}.
\]
Its effective domain is the polyhedral projection \(\{x:\exists y\geq0,\ Wy=h-Tx\}\), and its epigraph is the projection of
\[
\{(x,y,\alpha):Wy=h-Tx,\ y\geq0,\ q^{\mathsf T}y\leq\alpha\}.
\]
Consequently, whenever \(Q\) is proper, \(Q\) is a closed polyhedral convex function. Where linear-programming duality applies, \(Q(x)=\sup\{\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx):W^{\mathsf T}\pi\leq q\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear recourse value is a parametric linear-programming value whose domain and epigraph are polyhedral and whose dual gives affine supporting functions.
assumptions_latex: The displayed linear program has no duality gap whenever its value is finite.
\(Q\) is proper on the parameter region under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}Q\) is polyhedral and \(Q(x)=\sup_{W^{\mathsf T}\pi\leq q}\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\).

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier for the recourse equality.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 The Structure of the Dual Feasible Bases p. 158

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7 The Structure of the Dual Feasible Bases p. 158

children.title: Polyhedral Recourse Geometry
children.top_down_role: Risk-adjusted recourse systems with polyhedral feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Recourse Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of finite-scenario polyhedral value functions under polyhedral risk aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose each scenario continuation value \(Q_i:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper polyhedral convex and a coherent polyhedral risk functional has the finite-envelope form \(\rho(z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal E}q^{\mathsf T}z\), where \(\mathcal E\) is a finite set of probability vectors. Then
\[
V(x)=\rho\bigl(Q_1(x),\ldots,Q_m(x)\bigr)
=
\max_{q\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^m q_iQ_i(x)
\]
is polyhedral convex on its effective domain. Hence its epigraph is a polyhedron and it admits finitely many affine supporting pieces on every polyhedral region where it is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-scenario polyhedral continuation values remain polyhedral after aggregation by a coherent risk functional with a finite polyhedral envelope.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many scenarios.
Each \(Q_i\) is proper polyhedral convex.
The risk envelope has finitely many relevant extreme probability vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V=\rho(Q_1,\ldots,Q_m)\) is polyhedral convex.

notation.meaning: Finite set of extreme risk-envelope probabilities.

source_refs.locator: 5.7 The Structure of the Dual Feasible Bases p. 158

source_witnesses.locator: 5.7 The Structure of the Dual Feasible Bases p. 158

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited locator concerns linear-program dual structure but does not specifically support closure under polyhedral risk aggregation. The statement also applies a risk functional on finite vectors to possibly infinite-valued Q_i without specifying a common finite domain or an extended-value convention.

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Value Structure
children.top_down_role: Value-function geometry associated with linear or polyhedral recourse.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Linear Value Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite affine representation of proper polyhedral convex stage values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper closed convex function \(V:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is polyhedral if and only if there exist a polyhedron \(D\), finitely many vectors \(a_j\), and scalars \(b_j\) such that
\[
V(x)=
\begin{cases}
\max_{1\leq j\leq N}\{a_j^{\mathsf T}x+b_j\},&x\in D,\\
+\infty,&x\notin D.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus a finite-valued linear-polyhedral recourse function is convex piecewise affine, and each pair \((a_j,b_j)\) defines a globally valid supporting cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed polyhedral convex value function is exactly a finite maximum of affine functions on a polyhedral domain.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The epigraph of \(V\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V\) has a finite maximum-of-affine-functions representation on \(\operatorname{dom}V\).

notation.meaning: Slope and intercept of affine piece j.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.4 A Piecewise Linear Upper Bound p. 185

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.4 A Piecewise Linear Upper Bound p. 185

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite maximum-of-affine representation is standard and the representation kind fits the leaf, but the cited section is specifically an upper-bound construction and may not support the asserted if-and-only-if characterization or global supporting-piece conclusion.

children.title: Convex Nonlinear Recourse
children.top_down_role: Convex risk-adjusted value functions requiring nonlinear approximation mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Nonlinear Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity preservation under nonlinear recourse minimization and monotone convex risk aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\inf_{y\in Y(\xi)}\{g(x,y,\xi):h_j(x,y,\xi)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,r\}.
\]
If \(Y(\xi)\) is convex and \(g(\cdot,\cdot,\xi)\) and every \(h_j(\cdot,\cdot,\xi)\) are jointly convex, then partial minimization makes \(Q(\cdot,\xi)\) convex. If \(\rho\) is also monotone and convex on the resulting random costs, then \(V(x)=\rho(Q(x,\xi))\) is convex. Unlike finite linear recourse, \(V\) need not be polyhedral or exactly representable by finitely many affine cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly convex nonlinear recourse yields a convex value function, and monotone convex risk aggregation preserves convexity but generally not polyhedrality.
assumptions_latex: For each \(\xi\), the feasible recourse graph is convex.
The recourse objective is jointly convex in the current and recourse decisions.
\(\rho\) is monotone and convex on its domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto \rho(Q(x,\xi))\) is convex, but need not be polyhedral.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex partial-minimization and monotone convex-risk composition claims fit Convex Nonlinear Recourse, but no source is supplied for either claim or for the nonpolyhedral boundary statement.

children.title: Nonconvex Discrete Recourse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes lacking standard convex value-function geometry.

children.title: Integer Recourse
children.top_down_role: Risk-averse multistage recourse containing discrete decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\xi\in\Xi\), \(m,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), and \(1\leq k\leq m\).
For each \(\xi\in\Xi\), \(q(\xi)\in\mathbb R^m\), \(W(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times m}\), \(h(\xi)\in\mathbb R^\ell\), and \(T(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times n}\).
The infimum is interpreted in the extended-real sense, with value \(+\infty\) for infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is a mixed-integer recourse value function and is not guaranteed to be convex or continuous as a function of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recourse whose admissible corrective decisions include at least one integer-valued component.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) be a parameter and let \(\xi\in\Xi\) be an uncertainty realization. Given \(1\leq k\leq m\), an integer-recourse value is an extended-real function of the form
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\inf\bigl\{q(\xi)^{\mathsf T}y:W(\xi)y=h(\xi)-T(\xi)x,\ y\in\mathbb Z^k\times\mathbb R^{m-k},\ y\geq0\bigr\},
\]
where \(Q(x,\xi)=+\infty\) when the constraint system is infeasible. Because the feasible response set changes discretely with \(x\), this value function need not be convex or continuous in \(x\), even though each fixed-parameter problem is mixed-integer linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer recourse requires at least one corrective decision to be integral, producing an extended-real mixed-integer value function that is not generally convex or continuous.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Recourse

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

children.title: Nonconvex Recourse
children.top_down_role: Risk-averse multistage recourse lacking convex stage geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Recourse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recourse value generated by a nonconvex feasible graph or objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a parameter \(x\) and realization \(\xi\), define
\[
Q(x,\xi)=\inf\{g(x,y,\xi):y\in Y(x,\xi)\}.
\]
This is nonconvex recourse when the extended feasible graph \(\{(x,y):y\in Y(x,\xi)\}\) is nonconvex or \(g(\cdot,\cdot,\xi)\) is nonconvex on that graph. In this regime, partial minimization does not generally preserve convexity: \(Q(\cdot,\xi)\) may have disconnected effective domain, jumps, or nonglobal local minima, and affine lower supports need not determine its exact value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex recourse arises from a nonconvex objective or feasible graph, so its marginal value may be discontinuous, nonconvex, or locally misleading.
assumptions_latex: The infimum is interpreted in \(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty,-\infty\}\).
At least one displayed source of nonconvexity is present for some \(\xi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(\cdot,\xi)\) is not guaranteed to be convex or recoverable from affine supporting cuts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition/failure statement fits the nonconvex-recourse leaf and does not claim that every nonconvex formulation produces a nonconvex marginal value. However, no authoritative source or locator is supplied for the definition and listed failure phenomena.

children.title: Convexification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of convex approximations for discrete or nonconvex recourse.

assumptions_latex: In the example, \(x\in[0,1]\) and recourse is a minimization problem.
For the general exactness equivalence, both the original and relaxed minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Q(x)=x<Q(x)=1\) for every \(x\in(0,1)\); more generally, convexification gives a lower bound, and under attainment it is exact exactly when a relaxed optimizer belongs to the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict loss of exactness when discrete recourse is replaced by its continuous relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
Q(x)=\min\{y:y\in\mathbb Z_+,\ y\geq x\},\qquad x\in[0,1].
\]
Then \(Q(0)=0\) and \(Q(x)=1\) for every \(x\in(0,1]\). Replacing \(\mathbb Z_+\) by \(\mathbb R_+\) gives the convex relaxation \(\bar Q(x)=x\), so \(\bar Q(x)<Q(x)\) for \(0<x<1\). More generally, replacing a feasible response set \(C\) by a convex superset such as \(\operatorname{conv}C\) cannot increase a minimization value. Exactness is not automatic; when both minima are attained, equality holds if and only if the relaxed problem has an optimizer belonging to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying discrete recourse gives a lower bound and can create a strict gap. When both optima are attained, the relaxation is exact exactly when it has an optimizer feasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5 Cutting Plane Method for the Solution of the All Integer Variable Linear Programming Problem p. 76

children.title: Stagewise-Independent Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: The classical sampling and decomposition regime for risk-averse SDDP.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise-Independent Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independence regime underlying stagewise sampling and history-invariant continuation distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\xi_t)_{t=1}^T\) be exogenous disturbances and let \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_t)\). The process is stagewise independent when, for every \(t\geq2\) and every measurable set \(B\),
\[
\mathbb P(\xi_t\in B\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=\mathbb P(\xi_t\in B)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Equivalently, the joint law factors as \(P_1\otimes\cdots\otimes P_T\). Hence the distribution used in a stage-\(t\) expectation or conditional risk mapping is independent of the realized earlier disturbance history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise independence means each disturbance has its marginal distribution even after conditioning on all earlier disturbances.
assumptions_latex: \((\xi_t)_{t=1}^T\) are random elements on a common probability space.
All conditional probabilities are understood through regular conditional distributions when needed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=\mathcal L(\xi_t)\) almost surely for every \(t\geq2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-law definition and finite-horizon product-law equivalence are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but the record supplies no source for the definition or its consequence for stagewise risk evaluation.

children.title: Dependent-Process Uncertainty Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dependent-process regimes requiring conditional models or expanded state.

children.title: Markov Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Conditional uncertainty governed by a Markov state.

knowledge_statements.title: Markov Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence summarized by the current exogenous Markov state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An uncertainty state process \((S_t)_{t=1}^T\) is Markov if transition kernels \(K_t\) exist such that, for every measurable set \(B\),
\[
\mathbb P(S_{t+1}\in B\mid S_1,\ldots,S_t)=K_t(S_t,B)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Thus the conditional law of future uncertainty depends on the observed past only through the current state \(S_t\). In a multistage optimization model, continuation values may therefore be indexed by both the endogenous resource state and \(S_t\), rather than by the entire uncertainty history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Markov uncertainty allows temporal dependence, but the current uncertainty state completely determines the conditional law of the next state.
assumptions_latex: Each \(S_t\) takes values in a measurable state space admitting the stated conditional kernels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(S_{t+1}\mid S_1,\ldots,S_t)=K_t(S_t,\cdot)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Exogenous Markov state at stage t.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 Markov chains with discrete time p. 58
2.3 Markov Processes with Arbitrary State Space p. 101

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 Markov chains with discrete time p. 58

children.title: Interstage-Dependent Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Stochastic processes with dependence extending across stage boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Interstage-Dependent Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General temporal dependence beyond history-invariant stagewise sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}=\sigma(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_{t-1})\). The uncertainty process is interstage dependent when, for at least one \(t\geq2\), its conditional transition law
\[
P_t(B\mid\xi_{1:t-1})=\mathbb P(\xi_t\in B\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})
\]
is not almost surely equal to the marginal probability \(\mathbb P(\xi_t\in B)\) for some measurable \(B\). Consequently, continuation distributions and conditional risk evaluations may vary with the observed history; independent stagewise resampling from the marginal law does not preserve the original process.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interstage dependence occurs when some future disturbance distribution changes with observed history, invalidating independent sampling from stagewise marginals.
assumptions_latex: \((\xi_t)_{t=1}^T\) is adapted to its natural filtration.
The required regular conditional laws exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some \(t\) and measurable \(B\), \(P_t(B\mid\xi_{1:t-1})\neq\mathbb P(\xi_t\in B)\) on an event of positive probability.

notation.meaning: Information generated by disturbances through stage t.

source_refs.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications

source_witnesses.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly expresses failure of stagewise independence, but the cited state-dependent-noise section is indirect and does not reliably establish the general definition or the claim about marginal resampling.

children.title: State Expansion for Dependence
children.top_down_role: Expanded state descriptions used to retain relevant dependence information.

knowledge_statements.title: State Expansion for Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Markovization using a recursively updated sufficient statistic of uncertainty history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_t=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_t)\). Suppose a statistic \(S_t=\phi_t(H_t)\) satisfies a recursive update \(S_{t+1}=F_t(S_t,\xi_{t+1})\) and
\[
\mathcal L(\xi_{t+1:T}\mid H_t)=\mathcal L(\xi_{t+1:T}\mid S_t).
\]
If stage costs, feasible actions, and conditional risk mappings depend on \(H_t\) only through the endogenous state and \(S_t\), then adjoining \(S_t\) to the endogenous state yields an exact Markov representation. The Bellman value can be written as \(V_t(z_t,S_t)\), with no loss from discarding the remaining history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursively updated sufficient statistic converts history-dependent uncertainty into an exact augmented-state Markov model when all relevant conditional objects factor through it.
assumptions_latex: \(S_t\) is measurable with respect to \(H_t\).
The displayed conditional-sufficiency identity holds.
Costs, constraints, and conditional risk mappings factor through \((z_t,S_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented process \((z_t,S_t)\) is a sufficient state and admits an exact recursion with value \(V_t(z_t,S_t)\).

notation.meaning: Complete uncertainty history through stage t.

children.title: Information-Risk Feedback Geometry
children.top_down_role: Models in which decisions alter future information or risk structure.

children.title: Endogenous Information
children.top_down_role: Information structures altered by earlier decisions.

assumptions_latex: The policy is \(\pi=(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{T-1})\) on a probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\).
At stage \(t\), observations are generated by a kernel \(K_t(\cdot\mid H_{t-1},\pi_{t-1}(H_{t-1}))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_t^\pi\) is policy-dependent, so admissibility and conditional risk evaluation must use the filtration induced by the same policy.

notation.meaning: Information sigma-field induced by policy pi

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-dependent filtrations generated by decision-dependent observation kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Endogenous information is present when the available filtration depends on the implemented policy. Recursively set \(H_0\) equal to the initial observation and, for \(t\geq 1\), generate \(Y_t\) according to \(K_t(\cdot\mid H_{t-1},\pi_{t-1}(H_{t-1}))\), then define \(H_t=(H_{t-1},\pi_{t-1}(H_{t-1}),Y_t)\) and \(\mathcal F_t^\pi=\sigma(H_t)\). A policy is admissible only if \(\pi_t(H_t)\) is \(\mathcal F_t^\pi\)-measurable. Thus both the feasible decision rules and conditional distributions used downstream are induced by \(\pi\), rather than by a fixed exogenous filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information is endogenous when past decisions alter what is observed, making the filtration, admissible policies, and downstream conditional distributions depend on the implemented policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Endogenous Information

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but no source supports the policy-dependent filtration construction. Observation spaces, kernel measurability, and the precise admissible-policy class are not specified sufficiently to validate the circular policy/filtration dependence.

children.title: Decision-Dependent Risk
children.top_down_role: Risk mappings or distributions altered by policy choices.

assumptions_latex: For each admissible policy \(\pi\), losses lie in \(L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1}^\pi)\).
Each conditional risk mapping has a decision-indexed envelope \(\mathcal Q_t(\pi_t,H_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The continuation value depends on the current action through both future losses and the conditional risk mapping.

notation.meaning: Conditional risk mapping at stage t under the current decision

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional coherent risk whose mapping or envelope changes with the chosen action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Decision-dependent conditional risk is a family of mappings \(\rho_t^a:L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1}^{\pi})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t^{\pi})\), indexed by the current admissible action \(a\). In the coherent finite-support case it may be written as \[\rho_t^a(Z)=\sup_{q\in\mathcal Q_t(a,H_t)}\mathbb E_q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t^\pi],\] where every \(q\) is a conditional probability distortion. Consequently, a Bellman recursion takes the coupled form \[V_t(H_t)=\inf_{a\in A_t(H_t)}\left\{c_t(H_t,a)+\rho_t^a\bigl(V_{t+1}(H_{t+1})\bigr)\right\}.\] The dependence on \(a\) is part of the risk model, not merely dependence of the loss on the decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk is decision-dependent when the selected action changes the conditional risk mapping or its probability-distortion envelope, in addition to changing future losses.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Dependent Risk

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and topic fit, but the decision-indexed conditional risk mapping and envelope representation need a dedicated source. The meaning of q, its reference measure or conditional-probability constraints, and consistency between indexing by a current action and dependence on the full policy are not established.

children.title: Information–Risk Feedback
children.top_down_role: Feedback between information acquisition, decisions, and future risk exposure.

assumptions_latex: The policy \(\pi\) induces both \(\mathcal F_t^\pi\) and conditional mappings \(\rho_t^{\pi_t}\).
The nested risk recursion is well-defined for every admissible policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Policy comparison must evaluate each policy under its own induced information and risk system.

notation.meaning: Total loss generated by policy pi

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling between policy-induced information and policy-dependent nested risk evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a policy \(\pi\), let \(\mathbb F^\pi=(\mathcal F_t^\pi)_{t=0}^T\) be its induced filtration and let \(\mathcal R^\pi=\rho_0^{\pi_0}\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T-1}^{\pi_{T-1}}\) denote its nested risk evaluation, with the usual stagewise insertion of costs. Information-risk feedback means that changing \(\pi_t\) can change both the conditional law revealed through \(\mathcal F_{t+1}^\pi\) and the mapping \(\rho_t^{\pi_t}\). Hence the optimization criterion is \[\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mathbb F^\pi)}\mathcal R^\pi(L^\pi),\] and generally cannot be reduced to minimizing a fixed risk functional over policies adapted to a fixed filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decisions can jointly alter future observations and their risk evaluation; therefore each policy must be assessed using the filtration and nested risk system that it induces.
knowledge_statements.title: Information–Risk Feedback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the leaf, but the policy-dependent feasible set and nested functional are only schematic. A source is needed to justify comparison of policies defined on different induced filtrations and to state the stagewise nesting rigorously.

children.title: Extensive-Form Methods
children.top_down_role: Direct solution families for finite scenario-tree dynamic-risk models.

children.title: Polyhedral-Risk Extensive Forms
children.top_down_role: Direct finite-dimensional formulations for polyhedral conditional risk.

assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite, and every node \(n\) has a finite child set \(C(n)\).
Each conditional coherent risk envelope \(\mathcal Q_n\) is a nonempty polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nested-risk problem has a finite linear extensive form obtained by imposing one epigraph inequality per envelope vertex and tree node.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral conditional risk envelope at node n
Epigraph variable for the continuation risk at node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario-tree representation for coherent conditional risks with polyhedral envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every nonleaf node \(n\), suppose \[\rho_n(z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sum_{m\in C(n)}q_m z_m,\qquad \mathcal Q_n=\operatorname{conv}\{q^{n,1},\ldots,q^{n,K_n}\}.\] Introduce a continuation epigraph variable \(\theta_n\) and child values \(v_m=c_m(x_m)+\theta_m\), with \(\theta_m=0\) at leaves. Then the identity \(\theta_n=\rho_n((v_m)_{m\in C(n)})\) in a minimization model is represented by \[\theta_n\geq\sum_{m\in C(n)}q_m^{n,k}v_m\quad(k=1,\ldots,K_n).\] Together with nodewise feasibility and parent-child linking constraints, these inequalities yield a finite-dimensional linear extensive form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite nested coherent-risk model becomes a linear extensive form by adding continuation variables and one inequality for every vertex of each node’s polyhedral risk envelope.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Risk Extensive Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited scenario-tree section does not specifically support polyhedral conditional-risk extensive forms. Polyhedral risk envelopes alone do not make the complete model linear; linear costs, feasibility, and linking constraints are also required. Exact replacement of equality by epigraph inequalities additionally needs monotone propagation and minimization conditions.

children.title: Nonpolyhedral Extensive-Form Family
children.top_down_role: Direct formulations for nonpolyhedral conditional mappings.

children.title: Conic Extensive Forms
children.top_down_role: Direct multistage formulations using conic risk representations.

assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite.
At each nonleaf node, the epigraph of the conditional risk mapping has a closed conic representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Substituting the local conic epigraphs into the tree recursion produces a finite conic extensive form.

notation.meaning: Closed convex cone defining the nodewise risk epigraph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted conic representation of nonpolyhedral conditional-risk epigraphs on finite trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that for every nonleaf node \(n\), \[(v,\theta)\in\operatorname{epi}\rho_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists y_n:\ A_nv+B_n\theta+C_ny_n-d_n\in K_n,\] where \(K_n\) is a closed convex cone and \(v=(v_m)_{m\in C(n)}\). Introduce node decisions \(x_n\), continuation values \(v_n=c_n(x_n)+\theta_n\), and one lifting vector \(y_n\) per nonleaf node. Imposing \[A_nv_{C(n)}+B_n\theta_n+C_ny_n-d_n\in K_n\] together with nodewise feasibility and parent-child linking constraints gives a conic extensive form whose root objective is \(c_0(x_0)+\theta_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every conditional-risk epigraph is conically representable, local lifting variables and cone constraints convert the nested model into one finite conic extensive form.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Extensive Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the conic-extensive-form leaf, but no source is supplied. Conic representability of the risk epigraphs is insufficient by itself: node costs, feasible sets, and transition/linking constraints must also admit compatible conic representations.

children.title: Smooth-Risk Extensive Forms
children.top_down_role: Direct multistage formulations using smooth conditional risk mappings.

assumptions_latex: The scenario tree is finite with strictly positive conditional probabilities \(p_{m\mid n}\).
Each node uses entropic risk with parameter \(\gamma_n>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nested entropic-risk problem is a smooth convex extensive form with one log-sum-exp epigraph constraint at each nonleaf node.

notation.meaning: Conditional probability from node n to child m

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear extensive form specialized to nested entropic conditional risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonleaf node \(n\), define the conditional entropic risk by \[\rho_n(v)=\frac{1}{\gamma_n}\log\left(\sum_{m\in C(n)}p_{m\mid n}e^{\gamma_n v_m}\right).\] With \(v_m=c_m(x_m)+\theta_m\) and \(\theta_m=0\) at leaves, impose the smooth convex inequalities \[\theta_n\geq\frac{1}{\gamma_n}\log\left(\sum_{m\in C(n)}p_{m\mid n}e^{\gamma_n(c_m(x_m)+\theta_m)}\right).\] Combining these inequalities with nodewise constraints and parent-child state transitions yields a finite smooth extensive form. Because the objective minimizes the root value, every risk epigraph inequality is tight at an optimum whenever downstream values are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested entropic risk yields a smooth convex extensive form by placing a conditional log-sum-exp epigraph constraint at every nonleaf scenario-tree node.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Risk Extensive Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entropic-risk formula is standard and the representation fits the leaf, but no source is supplied. Smooth convexity of the entire extensive form requires suitable assumptions on costs, transitions, and feasible sets. Tightness of every epigraph inequality also requires monotonic propagation to the root and attainment, not merely finite downstream values.

children.title: Nonpolyhedral Solver Geometry
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing structure arising from conic or smooth risk formulations.

assumptions_latex: The extensive form has twice differentiable local functions or conic blocks satisfying an appropriate constraint qualification.
Variables and constraints are ordered by scenario-tree nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The derivative or primal-dual system is tree sparse, while each nonpolyhedral risk mapping contributes a node-local curved or conic block.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative and primal-dual sparsity induced by local nonpolyhedral risk epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_n\) collect the decision, continuation, and risk-lifting variables at node \(n\). If each transition constraint couples only \(w_{a(n)}\) and \(w_n\), and each risk epigraph couples \(w_n\) only to variables of children in \(C(n)\), then the linearized optimality matrix satisfies \[J_{ij}=0\quad\text{whenever nodes }i\text{ and }j\text{ share neither a local constraint nor a tree edge.}\] Smooth risks contribute node-local Hessian blocks; conic risks contribute node-local primal-dual scaling blocks. Eliminating leaf-to-root preserves a tree-based block elimination order, although Schur complements may couple siblings through their common parent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpolyhedral risk adds local curvature or cone-scaling blocks, while the full derivative system retains the block sparsity and elimination order of the scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Solver Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A property is an appropriate kind for this leaf, but no source supports the asserted derivative and elimination geometry. The indexing of J by nodes is not defined for a Jacobian or KKT system, and the claimed fill behavior depends on the precise formulation and elimination ordering.

children.title: Tree-Sparse Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces exploiting scenario-tree block structure.

assumptions_latex: The model is indexed by a finite rooted scenario tree.
Every constraint is node-local or links a node to its parent or children.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extensive form can be communicated to a solver by local blocks plus parent-child adjacency, without assembling unrelated zero blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block interface exposing scenario-tree adjacency and node-local risk structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tree-sparse solver interface represents each nonroot node \(n\) by a local variable block \(x_n\), local constraints \(A_nx_n\in D_n\), and a parent link \[B_nx_{a(n)}+E_nx_n=b_n.\] A conditional-risk epigraph at \(n\) is supplied as a local block involving \(n\) and its children, together with derivatives, cone data, or polyhedral rows appropriate to that block. The global interface is therefore the collection \[\{(A_n,B_n,E_n,b_n,D_n):n\in\mathcal N\}\] plus the parent map \(a\). This representation determines the extensive form while exposing the adjacency required for block factorization and parallel node evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree-sparse interface supplies node-local constraint and risk blocks together with parent links, allowing solvers to exploit scenario-tree adjacency without materializing structural zeros.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Sparse Solver Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the solver-interface leaf, but the cited scenario-tree section does not support the proposed solver API, risk-block interface, factorization claim, or parallel evaluation claim. Several symbols used in the statement, including D_n, E_n, b_n, a(n), and the node set, are not introduced in the notation.

children.title: Risk-Adjusted Nested L-Shaped Methods
children.top_down_role: Nested cutting-plane decomposition with risk-adjusted stage subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and all conditional risk envelopes are finite and polyhedral.
Every stage subproblem is a feasible linear program with bounded value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns the exact root policy after finitely many distinct supporting cuts have been generated.

notation.meaning: Approximation of the continuation value at node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree nested Benders method for linear models with polyhedral conditional risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize lower approximations \(\widehat V_n^0\equiv-\infty\) subject to any valid finite lower bounds. At iteration \(k\), solve forward from the root using the current cuts to obtain trial states \(s_n^k\). In a backward pass, solve each child linear subproblem and maximize its dual value over the node’s polyhedral risk envelope. The resulting risk-weighted dual multipliers define a valid cut \[\widehat V_n^{k+1}(s)\geq\alpha_n^k+(\beta_n^k)^{\mathsf T}s.\] Add violated cuts and repeat. Stop when the root upper and lower bounds differ by at most \(\varepsilon\); output the incumbent policy, with exact finite termination when \(\varepsilon=0\) and only finitely many dual-envelope extreme points exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested L-shaped method alternates forward trial policies and backward risk-weighted dual cuts, stopping when root upper and lower bounds meet the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Adjusted Nested L-Shaped Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the cited classical L-shaped section does not establish the risk-adjusted multistage extension. Finite exact termination and recovery of an exact root policy require substantially more assumptions and a precise upper-bound construction, cut-generation rule, and treatment of all relevant tree nodes.

children.title: Risk-Envelope Decomposition Methods
children.top_down_role: Decomposition based on conditional probability distortions or envelope variables.

assumptions_latex: The nested coherent risk model has rectangular nonempty polyhedral conditional envelopes \(\mathcal Q_n\).
For fixed envelope weights, the decision subproblem is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite constraint generation solves the envelope saddle formulation exactly when every \(\mathcal Q_n\) has finitely many extreme points.

notation.meaning: Conditional risk envelope at node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint generation over rectangular conditional probability-distortion envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite sets \(S_n^0\subseteq\mathcal Q_n\) for all nonleaf nodes. At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted decision master with \[\theta_n\geq\sum_{m\in C(n)}q_m v_m\quad\text{for every }q\in S_n^k.\] For its solution, independently solve each envelope separation problem \[q_n^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sum_{m\in C(n)}q_m v_m.\] If \(\sum_m(q_n^k)_mv_m\leq\theta_n+\varepsilon\) at every node, stop and output the master policy. Otherwise set \(S_n^{k+1}=S_n^k\cup\{q_n^k\}\) at violated nodes and repeat. Rectangularity permits nodewise separation; finite polyhedral envelopes give finite exact termination for \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method solves a restricted risk-envelope master, finds worst conditional probability distortions nodewise, adds violated envelope inequalities, and repeats until none exceed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope Decomposition Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constraint-generation algorithm fits the leaf, but no source is supplied. Exact finite termination requires a fully specified finite master, exact separation, and assumptions ensuring that all relevant nodewise epigraph constraints are generated and solved globally; rectangularity and finite envelope vertices alone do not establish the stated result.

children.title: Scenario-Nonanticipativity Decomposition Coupling
children.top_down_role: Pathwise or bundlewise decomposition coupled through risk and information structures.

children.title: Scenario Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Pathwise or bundlewise partitioning of multistage risk problems.

assumptions_latex: The finite scenario set is \(\Omega\), with one decision copy \(x^\omega\) per scenario.
Cross-scenario nonanticipativity and risk-envelope consistency constraints admit Lagrangian dualization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixing the coordination multipliers separates the relaxation into scenario subproblems, while multiplier updates enforce cross-scenario consistency.

notation.meaning: Decision vector copied for scenario omega

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-copy decomposition with dual coordination of information and risk coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write scenario copies as \(x=(x^\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\) and collect nonanticipativity and any duplicated risk-envelope consistency equations as \(Mx=0\). Initialize \(\lambda^0\). At iteration \(k\), solve in parallel \[x^{\omega,k}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x^\omega\in X^\omega}\left\{F_\omega(x^\omega)+(M_\omega^{\mathsf T}\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}x^\omega\right\}.\] Form the residual \(r^k=\sum_{[1m? no invalid] }\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario decomposition duplicates decisions, dualizes cross-scenario consistency, solves scenario subproblems in parallel, and updates coordination multipliers from the resulting residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical statement terminates with the corrupted placeholder “\sum_{[1m? no invalid] }” and omits the residual formula, multiplier update, step-size rule, and stopping condition described in the plain text. The cited scenario-tree section does not support the decomposition algorithm. This incomplete record cannot be validated or repaired without reconstructing substantive missing content and obtaining an appropriate source.

children.title: Nonanticipativity Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition organized around shared information constraints.

assumptions_latex: Scenarios sharing a history at stage \(t\) form an information bundle \(B\).
After fixing shared risk-envelope variables, the remaining objective is scenario separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consensus or multiplier iterations enforce nonanticipativity while preserving scenario-wise subproblem solves.

notation.meaning: Decision copy for scenario omega at stage t
Consensus decision for information bundle B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus decomposition of scenario copies over common-history information bundles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Impose nonanticipativity as \(x_t^\omega=z_{t,B}\) whenever \(\omega\in B\). Given \(z^k\), multipliers \(u^k\), and penalty \(r>0\), solve the scenario subproblems \[x^{\omega,k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x^\omega\in X^\omega}\left\{F_\omega(x^\omega)+\sum_t(u_t^{\omega,k})^{\mathsf T}x_t^\omega+\frac r2\sum_t\lVert x_t^\omega-z_{t,B(\omega,t)}^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Update each \(z_{t,B}^{k+1}\) by the probability-weighted average of \(x_t^{\omega,k+1}\) over \(\omega\in B\), then set \(u_t^{\omega,k+1}=u_t^{\omega,k}+r(x_t^{\omega,k+1}-z_{t,B}^{k+1})\). Stop when primal and dual consensus residuals meet their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity decomposition uses scenario copies, bundle-level consensus decisions, and multiplier or penalty updates until decisions agree across scenarios with the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a progressive-hedging-style nonanticipativity decomposition and fits the leaf, but the cited scenario-tree section does not support it. Convergence requires explicit convexity, closedness, feasibility, and saddle-point assumptions, while the treatment of shared risk-envelope variables and their effect on separability is not specified.

children.title: Risk-Coupled Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination requirements induced by conditional risk across decomposed components.

assumptions_latex: Each scenario subproblem is convex and has a common nonanticipative decision space \(X\).
The conditional risk measure has a convex risk-envelope representation with nonempty envelope \(\mathcal Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At coordination, \(x_s=z\) for every scenario \(s\), and the risk-weighted stationarity residual vanishes.

notation.meaning: scenario decision and shared consensus decision

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consensus feasibility and risk-weighted stationarity are the canonical optimality conditions for convex scenario decomposition with a risk envelope
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex scenario decomposition with nonanticipativity and risk-envelope coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_s:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be closed convex scenario objectives and let \(\mathcal Q\) be a convex risk envelope. Risk-coupled coordination is attained by \((x_s,z,q,\lambda_s)\) when \[x_s=z\quad\text{for all }s,\qquad q\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\tilde q\in\mathcal Q}\sum_s \tilde q_s Q_s(x_s),\] and there exist \(g_s\in\partial Q_s(x_s)\) such that \[0\in q_s g_s+\lambda_s+N_X(x_s),\qquad \sum_s\lambda_s=0.\] Thus nonanticipativity is enforced through consensus, while the common risk maximizer determines the scenario weights used in stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordination requires scenario decisions to agree, risk weights to maximize the envelope representation, and risk-weighted scenario subgradients to satisfy consensus stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Coupled Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no source supports this specialized risk-coupled KKT system. The underlying consensus optimization problem, scenario index set, envelope normalization, multiplier sign convention, and constraint qualification are not specified sufficiently to justify attainment from the displayed conditions.

children.title: Regularized Risk-Averse Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Stabilized decomposition for risk-adjusted value approximations.

assumptions_latex: Each stage problem is convex and admits valid affine lower cuts for its risk-adjusted continuation value.
The regularization parameter satisfies \(\lambda_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every backward cut remains a valid lower bound, while the proximal term stabilizes only the trial-point computation.

notation.meaning: current lower approximation of the continuation value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of convex risk-averse nested decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a prox-center \(\bar x_t^k\), compute the forward trial decision by \[x_t^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_t(x_{t-1}^k,\xi_t)}\left\{c_t(x,\xi_t)+\underline V_{t+1}^{k-1}(x)+\frac{\lambda_k}{2}\lVert x-\bar x_t^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] In the backward pass, evaluate the unregularized risk-adjusted recourse problem and append a supporting cut \(\ell_t^k(x)=\alpha_t^k+(\beta_t^k)^{\mathsf T}x\) satisfying \(\ell_t^k(x)\le V_t(x)\). Update \(\underline V_t^k=\max\{\underline V_t^{k-1},\ell_t^k\}\), choose the next prox-center by a prescribed incumbent rule, and stop under the decomposition method's statistical or deterministic gap test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward subproblems include a proximal penalty around an incumbent, while backward passes generate unregularized valid risk-adjusted cuts and preserve the lower approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Risk-Averse Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the stabilized-decomposition leaf, but the cited regularized-decomposition section does not establish the stated risk-averse extension, preservation of risk-adjusted cuts, prox-center rule, or stopping rule. A specialized source and locator are required.

children.title: Risk Representations in SDDP
children.top_down_role: Algorithmic interfaces for nested coherent, spectral, and envelope-based risk models.

children.title: Nested CVaR SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP specialization for nested conditional CVaR models.

assumptions_latex: The horizon is finite and each stage has a finite conditional outcome distribution.
The confidence levels satisfy \(0\le\alpha_t<1\), and stage subproblems are convex with strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backward dual solutions generate affine lower cuts for the nested conditional-CVaR value functions.

notation.meaning: conditional value at risk at level alpha

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional CVaR has a convex threshold representation whose linear-program dual supplies SDDP cut coefficients
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon convex SDDP with nested conditional CVaR.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(V_{T+1}=0\) and recursively define \[V_t(x_{t-1})=\inf_{x_t\in X_t(x_{t-1},\xi_t)}\left\{c_t(x_t,\xi_t)+\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}\bigl(V_{t+1}(x_t,\xi_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t\bigr)\right\},\] where \[\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_t}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)=\inf_{\eta\in L^1(\mathcal F_t)}\left\{\eta+\frac{1}{1-\alpha_t}\mathbb E[(Z-\eta)_+\mid\mathcal F_t]\right\}.\] A forward pass uses \(\underline V_{t+1}^{k-1}\) to sample trial states. A backward pass solves the threshold-form child problems at each visited state, extracts dual subgradients, and appends their risk-weighted affine supporting cut to \(\underline V_t^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested-CVaR SDDP uses the conditional CVaR threshold formulation in backward subproblems and forms risk-weighted affine cuts from their dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested CVaR SDDP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Nested CVaR SDDP, but the specialized construction lacks a source. The displayed recursion also mixes a value function depending only on the predecessor state with a current-stage realization and changes the conditioning index between the assumptions and formula; a source is needed to fix the information-state convention reliably.

children.title: Spectral-Risk SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP specialization for convex combinations of spectral risk measures.

assumptions_latex: At stage \(t\), weights satisfy \(w_{tm}\ge0\) and \(\sum_{m=1}^{M_t}w_{tm}=1\).
Levels satisfy \(0\le\alpha_{tm}<1\), and the child value approximation is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral-risk cut is the same convex combination of valid component-CVaR cuts and is therefore a valid lower cut.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a finite spectral risk measure is a convex combination of CVaR mappings, and positive combinations preserve affine lower bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite mixtures of conditional CVaR mappings in convex SDDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integrable child cost \(Z\), represent the stagewise spectral mapping by \[\rho_t(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)=\sum_{m=1}^{M_t}w_{tm}\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha_{tm}}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t).\] In a backward pass, solve the threshold formulation for every component level \(\alpha_{tm}\) at the same trial state. If \(\ell_{tm}(x)=a_{tm}+b_{tm}^{\mathsf T}x\) is a valid lower supporting cut for the corresponding component value, then the spectral cut is \[\ell_t(x)=\sum_{m=1}^{M_t}w_{tm}\ell_{tm}(x).\] Because all weights are nonnegative and sum to one, \(\ell_t\) lower-bounds the spectral-risk continuation value and can be appended to the SDDP approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite spectral risk mapping combines conditional CVaRs; SDDP combines their component cuts with the same nonnegative weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Risk SDDP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is appropriate under Risk Representations in SDDP, and the finite CVaR mixture is plausible. A specialized source is still required to establish that the separately generated component cuts correspond to the component continuation functions being combined and therefore produce the claimed spectral-risk cut.

children.title: Risk-Envelope SDDP
children.top_down_role: SDDP organized through conditional risk-envelope optimization.

assumptions_latex: The conditional outcome set is finite with probabilities \(p_{tj}>0\).
The envelope \(\mathcal Q_t\) is nonempty, convex, and compact, with \(q_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_jp_{tj}q_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal envelope weight vector combines child subgradients into a valid subgradient of the risk-adjusted continuation value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the support-function representation of a coherent conditional risk measure yields risk-weighted subgradients by convex maximum calculus
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-support coherent conditional risk in SDDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For child values \(z_j\), the conditional coherent risk mapping is represented by \[\rho_t(z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_t}\sum_jp_{tj}q_jz_j.\] At a backward trial state \(\bar x\), let \(q^\star\) maximize the envelope problem for \(z_j=V_{t+1,j}(\bar x)\), and choose \(g_j\in\partial V_{t+1,j}(\bar x)\). Then \[g=\sum_jp_{tj}q_j^\star g_j\] is a subgradient of \(x\mapsto\rho_t((V_{t+1,j}(x))_j)\) at \(\bar x\). Consequently, \(\ell(x)=\rho_t((V_{t+1,j}(\bar x))_j)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) is a valid SDDP lower cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The risk envelope maximizes weighted child values; its optimal weights combine child subgradients into a valid risk-adjusted SDDP cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope SDDP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the leaf, but no citation supports the risk-envelope SDDP construction. The subgradient conclusion also needs the applicable maximum/composition hypotheses, including proper convex child functions and finiteness or continuity at the trial state.

children.title: Single-Cut Risk Variants
children.top_down_role: Aggregated value approximations combining conditional scenario contributions.

assumptions_latex: Each child approximation is a lower bound on its convex child value function.
The stage risk mapping is convex and monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregated affine function \(\ell^k\) is one valid lower cut for the complete risk-adjusted continuation value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a supporting hyperplane of the composite convex risk-adjusted continuation function is a valid single cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One aggregate continuation cut per backward state and stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal V(x)=\rho((V_j(x))_{j=1}^M)\) be the convex risk-adjusted continuation value. At a backward state \(\bar x^k\), obtain child subgradients and a compatible risk subgradient, producing \(g^k\in\partial\mathcal V(\bar x^k)\). The single-cut variant adds only \[\ell^k(x)=\mathcal V(\bar x^k)+(g^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x^k)\] and updates \[\underline{\mathcal V}^{k}(x)=\max\{\underline{\mathcal V}^{k-1}(x),\ell^k(x)\}.\] Outcome-specific affine information is therefore aggregated before storage, and the next forward problem uses one scalar epigraph representation for the risk-adjusted continuation approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-cut variant aggregates all outcome and risk information into one supporting hyperplane per visited state and stage.

children.title: Multicut Risk Variants
children.top_down_role: Disaggregated value approximations retaining separate conditional contributions.

assumptions_latex: Every outcome-specific child value function is convex and admits affine lower cuts.
The risk mapping is monotone in every child value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying the risk mapping to the separate child approximations gives a valid lower approximation of the risk-adjusted continuation value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise lower bounds remain lower bounds after application of a monotone risk mapping
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate child-value cut pools retained inside the stage risk mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each conditional outcome \(j\), retain a cut pool \[\underline V_j^k(x)=\max_{r\le k}\ell_j^r(x),\qquad \ell_j^r(x)\le V_j(x).\] Define the multicut risk approximation by \[\underline{\mathcal V}^k(x)=\rho\bigl((\underline V_j^k(x))_{j=1}^M\bigr).\] In a stage subproblem, introduce epigraph variables \(\theta_j\) satisfying \(\theta_j\ge\ell_j^r(x)\) for all retained cuts and evaluate \(\rho((\theta_j)_j)\). Since \(\underline V_j^k\le V_j\) componentwise and \(\rho\) is monotone, \(\underline{\mathcal V}^k(x)\le\rho((V_j(x))_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multicut variant retains separate lower-cut pools for child outcomes and applies the monotone risk mapping to their individual approximations.

children.title: Aggregation-Level Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Memory, approximation, and coordination consequences of cut aggregation choices.

assumptions_latex: There are \(M\) conditional outcomes at the considered stage.
Both variants process the same visited states and generate one new child cut per processed outcome.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Single-cut storage grows by \(O(K)\), whereas full multicut storage grows by \(O(MK)\) after \(K\) backward visits.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the storage counts follow directly from retaining one aggregate cut versus one cut per outcome at each backward visit
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-storage comparison under full retention and finite conditional support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After \(K\) backward visits to a stage with \(M\) conditional outcomes, a single-cut scheme retains at most \[N_{\mathrm{cut}}^{\mathrm{single}}=K\] newly generated aggregate cuts, while a full multicut scheme retains at most \[N_{\mathrm{cut}}^{\mathrm{multi}}=MK\] newly generated outcome cuts. Thus multicut master descriptions can be larger by a factor of \(M\). For identical child cut pools, preserving outcome-specific epigraphs avoids irreversible pre-aggregation and can yield a tighter state-dependent risk approximation; however, per-iteration solution time and memory increase with the additional variables and inequalities. No universal runtime ordering follows from these counts alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut storage is linear in visits; full multicut storage is linear in visits times outcomes, trading larger subproblems for potentially tighter approximations.

children.title: Regularized Risk-Averse SDDP
children.top_down_role: Stabilized variants for controlling trial-point behavior.

assumptions_latex: Stage problems are convex and the backward risk subproblems generate valid affine lower cuts.
The regularization coefficients satisfy \(\lambda_{tk}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularization controls forward trial states without altering the validity of backward SDDP lower cuts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal forward stabilization for convex risk-averse SDDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During the forward pass, at stage \(t\) compute \[x_t^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_t(x_{t-1}^k,\xi_t^k)}\left\{c_t(x,\xi_t^k)+\underline V_{t+1}^{k-1}(x)+\frac{\lambda_{tk}}{2}\lVert x-\bar x_t^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] During the backward pass, omit the proximal term, solve the ordinary risk-adjusted child problems at \(x_{t-1}^k\), and append the resulting affine lower cut to \(\underline V_t^k\). Update prox-centers according to a fixed incumbent rule. Stop using the underlying SDDP bound or confidence test, and return the policy induced by the unregularized stage objectives and final lower approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized risk-averse SDDP stabilizes forward trial decisions with proximal penalties but generates backward cuts from the original unregularized risk model.

children.title: Cut-Pool Management Calculus

children.title: Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies for retaining influential risk-adjusted value cuts.

assumptions_latex: The current approximation is \(\underline V(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\) for valid affine lower cuts \(\ell_i\).
A finite reference set \(R\) of trial or incumbent states is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected cuts reproduce \(\underline V\) exactly on \(R\) and remain a global lower approximation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: retaining at least one maximizing cut at each reference point preserves the maximum there and deleting valid lower cuts preserves global validity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-point selection from a finite valid cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(r\in R\), compute the active index set \[A(r)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I}\ell_i(r).\] Select a subset \(I_R\subseteq I\) such that \(I_R\cap A(r)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(r\in R\); ties may be resolved by retaining one or several maximizers. Replace the working approximation by \[\underline V_R(x)=\max_{i\in I_R}\ell_i(x).\] Then \(\underline V_R(r)=\underline V(r)\) for all \(r\in R\), while \(\underline V_R(x)\le V(x)\) globally because every retained affine function was already a valid lower cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select at least one maximizing cut at every reference state; the reduced pool stays globally valid and is exact on those states.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cut-selection algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf: retaining a maximizer at each reference point preserves the approximation there. However, the record has no citation or inspectable locator as required for candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Cut Pruning
children.top_down_role: Policies for removing redundant or inactive value cuts.

assumptions_latex: Every stored affine cut is a global lower bound on the true value function \(V\).
The retained index set \(J\) is a subset of the original cut set \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pruning cannot violate lower-bound validity, though it may weaken the approximation away from protected points.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a maximum over any subset of valid lower cuts remains below both the original maximum and the true value function
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and loss mechanism for deleting affine lower cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[\underline V_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\le V(x)\] and prune the pool to any subset \(J\subseteq I\). The pruned approximation satisfies \[\underline V_J(x)=\max_{j\in J}\ell_j(x)\le\underline V_I(x)\le V(x)\quad\text{for every }x.\] Hence deletion preserves the lower-bound certificate. If, for each protected reference point \(r\), the set \(J\) contains an index attaining \(\underline V_I(r)\), then \(\underline V_J(r)=\underline V_I(r)\). Without this active-cut retention condition, pruning can strictly lower the approximation even at previously visited states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting cuts preserves global lower-bound validity; retaining an active cut at each protected point also preserves the old value there.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Pruning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits Cut Pruning, and the subset argument is standard. A source is absent, and the statement should explicitly require a nonempty retained set or define the maximum over an empty pool.

children.title: Approximation-Size Control
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between cut-pool growth, solution quality, and computational burden.

assumptions_latex: All generated cuts are valid global affine lower bounds.
A positive pool cap \(B\) and a finite protected reference set \(R_k\) are specified at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The capped pool remains a valid lower approximation; exactness on every protected state requires that the cap accommodate the selected representatives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard cut-pool caps with optional protection of reference-state values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After adding iteration \(k\)'s cuts, choose \(J_k\subseteq I_k\) with \(|J_k|\le B\). Give priority to indices satisfying \[J_k\cap\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(r)\ne\varnothing\quad\text{for each }r\in R_k.\] If more than \(B\) representatives are required, retain a prescribed priority subset and record the unprotected states. Define \[\underline V^k(x)=\max_{i\in J_k}\ell_i(x).\] Use this capped approximation in subsequent forward and backward subproblems, repeating selection after each update. The pool contains at most \(B\) cuts, always remains a valid lower bound, and preserves the uncapped value at every reference state whose active representative is retained.

children.title: Risk-Adjusted Importance Sampling
children.top_down_role: Tail-focused sampling for policy evaluation and risk estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Adjusted Importance Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Importance sampling for estimating a CVaR objective from tail-enriched trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the nominal trajectory law, \(Q\) a proposal law satisfying \(P\ll Q\), and \(L=dP/dQ\). For loss \(Z\) and level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), draw independent trajectories \(\omega_i\sim Q\), compute \(Z_i=Z(\omega_i)\) and \(L_i=L(\omega_i)\), and minimize \[\widehat F_N(\eta)=\eta+\frac{1}{(1-\alpha)N}\sum_{i=1}^N L_i(Z_i-\eta)_+.\] Return \(\widehat F_N(\widehat\eta)\) as the CVaR estimate. A risk-adjusted proposal assigns increased probability to trajectories with large positive excess loss while retaining nominal support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample trajectories from a tail-enriched proposal, weight them by the nominal-to-proposal likelihood ratio, and minimize the weighted empirical CVaR formula.
assumptions_latex: \(P\ll Q\) and \(L=dP/dQ\) is evaluable.
\(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_N\) are independent under \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat F_N(\widehat\eta)\) is the likelihood-weighted empirical estimator of \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{\alpha}^{P}(Z)\).

notation.meaning: Likelihood ratio of the nominal law with respect to the proposal.
Positive part, equal to the maximum of u and zero.

children.title: Continuous-Support Risk-Averse SDDP

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Support Risk-Averse SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampled backward approximation when stagewise uncertainty has nonfinite support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stages \(t=T,\ldots,1\), let \(P_t(\cdot\mid s_{t-1})\) be a probability kernel on a Borel space and let \(\rho_t\) be a conditional convex risk mapping. Maintain polyhedral approximations \(\underline V_t^k\). At iteration \(k\), sample forward trajectories from the kernels, solve the stage problems using \(\underline V_{t+1}^{k-1}\), and record visited states. In the backward pass, approximate the conditional risk-adjusted expectation at each visited state by sampled or quadrature support, derive affine cuts from subproblem dual solutions, and set \(\underline V_t^k\) to the maximum of retained cuts. Stop under a prescribed statistical or iteration criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk-averse SDDP replaces finite scenario enumeration with sampled or quadrature approximations of continuous conditional distributions during its forward and backward passes.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_t(\cdot\mid s)\) is a measurable probability kernel on a Borel space.
Stage subproblems are convex and admit usable dual solutions.
Each \(\rho_t\) is a well-defined conditional convex risk mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^k\) is the cut model returned at stage \(t\); its deterministic lower-bound status depends on the backward integration rule.

notation.meaning: Stage-t value-function approximation after iteration k.

children.title: Markov Process Variants
children.top_down_role: Risk-averse SDDP architectures indexed by observable Markov regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Markov Process Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-averse dynamic recursion indexed by an observable Markov information state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_t\) be an observable Markov state with transition kernel \(K_t(dm'\mid m)\). If feasible actions and one-stage costs depend only on \((x_t,m_t)\), and the conditional risk mapping \(\rho_t^m\) depends on history only through \(m\), then the risk-averse cost-to-go admits the recursion \[V_t(x,m)=\inf_{u\in U_t(x,m)}\left\{c_t(x,m,u)+\rho_t^m\bigl(V_{t+1}(f_t(x,m,u,M_{t+1}),M_{t+1})\bigr)\right\}.\] Thus SDDP may maintain separate cut collections indexed by \((t,m)\), or parameterized cuts when the Markov state is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficient observable Markov state restores a Bellman recursion; risk-averse SDDP then indexes or parameterizes value-function cuts by that state.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t\sim K_t(\cdot\mid M_t)\).
The controlled dynamics, costs, and feasibility data are Markov in \((x_t,M_t)\).
The conditional risk mapping is Markov-compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t\) depends on past observations only through \((x_t,M_t)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Interstage-Dependent Process Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic recursion using a finite-dimensional statistic for interstage-dependent uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) denote the observation history and suppose there is a measurable statistic \(S_t=\phi_t(H_t)\) with update \(S_{t+1}=g_t(S_t,\xi_{t+1})\). If the conditional law satisfies \(\mathcal L(\xi_{t+1}\mid H_t)=P_t(\cdot\mid S_t)\), and feasibility, costs, and conditional risk mappings depend on history only through \((x_t,S_t)\), then \[V_t(x,s)=\inf_{u\in U_t(x,s)}\left\{c_t(x,s,u)+\rho_t^s\bigl(V_{t+1}(f_t(x,s,u,\xi_{t+1}),g_t(s,\xi_{t+1}))\bigr)\right\}.\] A dependent-process SDDP variant approximates this augmented value function rather than a stagewise-independent one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interstage dependence is handled by adding a sufficient predictive statistic to the optimization state and approximating the resulting augmented value function.
assumptions_latex: \(S_t=\phi_t(H_t)\) is sufficient for the conditional law of \(\xi_{t+1}\).
\(S_{t+1}=g_t(S_t,\xi_{t+1})\) is measurable.
The model data and conditional risk mappings are functions of \((x_t,S_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t\) is a function of \((x_t,S_t)\), and the augmented recursion preserves the specified conditional dependence.

children.title: History-State Expansion

knowledge_statements.title: History-State Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Markovization by treating the observed history as an expanded state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a process \((\xi_t)_{t=1}^T\), define the history state \(H_t=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_t)\) and update it by \(H_{t+1}=(H_t,\xi_{t+1})\). Every regular conditional law \(P_t(d\xi_{t+1}\mid H_t)\) is then a transition kernel on the history space. If decisions are nonanticipative and the one-step conditional risk mapping is conditioned on \(H_t\), the dynamic value may be written as \(V_t(x_t,H_t)\). This representation is exact, but the dimension or cardinality of the information state generally grows with \(t\), making direct cut indexing computationally costly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending the complete observation history to the physical state makes any finite-horizon process Markov, exactly preserving dependence at the cost of state growth.
assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) is finite.
Regular conditional distributions \(P_t(\cdot\mid H_t)\) exist.
Policies are nonanticipative with respect to the history filtration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(\xi_{t+1}\mid H_0,\ldots,H_t)=P_t(\cdot\mid H_t)\), so \((x_t,H_t)\) is a Markov information state.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Risk-Averse SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-memory or tightly coupled parallelization of independent SDDP subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize shared cut models \(\underline V_t^0\). At iteration \(k\), freeze a common snapshot \((\underline V_t^{k-1})_{t=2}^T\), generate a batch of independent forward trajectories, and assign their stage subproblems to parallel workers. In the backward pass, workers independently solve sampled risk-adjusted subproblems and return candidate cut coefficients. A coordinator validates and merges all accepted cuts by taking their pointwise maximum with the current models. The next iteration begins after the selected synchronization barrier. Stop under a common iteration, time, bound-gap, or statistical policy-evaluation criterion and return the shared policy induced by the final cut models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve independent forward and backward subproblems from a shared cut snapshot; a coordinator merges valid cuts into common value-function models.
assumptions_latex: Worker subproblems use a mutually consistent snapshot of the cut models.
Each accepted cut satisfies the serial algorithm's validity requirements.
Parallel random streams follow the prescribed sampling law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^k=\max\{\underline V_t^{k-1},\ell:\ell\in\mathcal C_t^k\}\) is the merged stage-\(t\) approximation.
