knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Risk-Averse SDDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-node SDDP with replicated models and communicated risk-adjusted cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker \(j\) maintain local models \(\underline V_{t,j}\) and a version vector. Each worker repeatedly receives available cuts, samples trajectories using its current model version, solves forward and risk-adjusted backward subproblems, tags generated cuts with their originating version, and transmits them to an aggregation service. The service rejects invalid or duplicate cuts and publishes accepted cuts to all workers. A termination protocol first halts new work, then drains in-flight messages and evaluates the policy represented by a declared global cut version. Under asynchronous operation, bounded communication delay or an explicit staleness rule must be imposed when required by the convergence theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed workers generate risk-adjusted SDDP cuts from versioned local models, while an aggregation service validates, deduplicates, and disseminates them.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted cut is valid independently of the worker's local cut subset.
Messages identify model and cut versions.
The termination protocol accounts for in-flight work and messages.

children.title: Synchronization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordination choices for sharing cuts, bounds, samples, or envelope information.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions for synchronous, bounded-stale, and asynchronous cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A synchronous regime requires every worker in iteration \(k\) to read version \(k-1\), finish its assigned work, and cross a barrier before version \(k\) is published. A bounded-stale regime requires a finite \(D\) such that each cut incorporated at global version \(k\) was generated from a version \(v\) satisfying \(k-D\le v\le k\). A fully asynchronous regime permits unbounded relative timing but must retain cut validity under stale models and guarantee eventual delivery and processing of every accepted cut. The selected predicate is part of the algorithm specification, not merely a hardware setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization is formalized by shared-version barriers, bounded version lag, or eventual processing with stale-model-safe cuts.
assumptions_latex: Global model versions are totally ordered.
Every generated cut carries its source version.
Cut publication is atomic at the level required by readers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v=k-1\) characterizes synchronous generation, while \(k-D\le v\le k\) characterizes bounded staleness.

notation.meaning: Version used to generate a cut.

children.title: Warm-Start Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior value approximations, policies, or solver state.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of still-valid value-function cuts in a shifted rolling-horizon problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a new rolling-horizon problem begins one stage later than a previously solved problem. Initialize each new stage model by mapping retained old cuts through the stage correspondence: if \(\ell_{t+1}^{old}(x)=a^	op x+b\), set \(\ell_t^{0}(x)=a^	op x+b\) only when the state coordinates, units, conditioning information, risk mapping, and downstream model data agree and the cut remains valid for the new value function. Discard or revalidate all other cuts. Run risk-averse SDDP from these initial models and return the updated policy; warm-start reuse changes initialization, not the stopping or validation rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift previously computed cuts into a new rolling-horizon model only when their state meaning and lower-bound validity are preserved.
assumptions_latex: Old and new state coordinates admit an explicit stage correspondence.
Every reused cut is valid for the new downstream value function.
Changed cuts are discarded or revalidated before use.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline V_t^0=\max\{\ell_{t+1}^{old}:\ell_{t+1}^{old}\text{ remains valid after transfer}\}\).

notation.meaning: Affine value-function cut at stage t.
Warm-start cut model for the new problem.

review_flags: rolling-horizon risk-averse SDDP warm-start source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed stage-shift mapping or establishes when old risk-averse SDDP cuts remain valid for the new rolling-horizon value functions.

children.title: Rolling Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Repeated solution as the horizon advances and information changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Rolling Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated risk-averse optimization after observing each rolling-horizon state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At decision epoch \(r\), observe the current physical and information state \(s_r\), construct a horizon-\(H\) risk-averse multistage model conditioned on \(s_r\), and solve or update its SDDP approximation to the prescribed stopping criterion. Apply only the first decision \(u_r\), observe the next information, set \(r\leftarrow r+1\), shift the horizon, update model data and conditional distributions, and repeat. Any transferred cuts must be checked against the shifted downstream problem. The output is the nonanticipative closed-loop sequence of implemented first-stage decisions, rather than the full plan computed at any single epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each epoch, condition on new information, update and solve a finite risk-averse horizon, implement its first decision, and roll forward.
assumptions_latex: The state \(s_r\) contains the information needed to condition the new model.
Each implemented decision is feasible for the current observed state.
Transferred approximations satisfy the new model's validity rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_r\in\arg\min_{u\in U_r(s_r)}\widehat J_{r,H}(s_r,u)\) is implemented before reoptimization at epoch \(r+1\).

notation.meaning: Observed state at rolling decision epoch r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this risk-averse rolling-reoptimization algorithm. The relationship between the conditional risk model, time consistency, stopping rule, and implemented closed-loop policy requires dedicated treatment.

children.title: Approximation Transfer Across Horizons
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of stored approximations with shifted horizons or updated risk inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Transfer Across Horizons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving mapping of affine cuts between overlapping rolling horizons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_{r,t}^{old}\) and \(V_{r+1,t-1}^{new}\) denote value functions for two rolling problems whose downstream stages overlap. A transfer operator \(\mathcal T_{r,t}\) maps an old affine cut \(\ell(x)=a^	op x+b\) to the new state coordinates. The transferred cut is admissible precisely when \[\mathcal T_{r,t}\ell(x)\le V_{r+1,t-1}^{new}(x)\quad\text{for every feasible new state }x.\] Equality of downstream dynamics, costs, conditional laws, and risk mappings on the overlap is a sufficient structural condition when the state mapping preserves feasibility. Otherwise, cuts require correction, revalidation, or deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut may cross rolling horizons only if its mapped form remains a global lower bound for the new downstream value function.
assumptions_latex: The overlapping stages have an explicit state-coordinate map.
Transferred affine functions are defined on every feasible new state.
The new value function uses the stated downstream risk model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal T_{r,t}\ell\le V_{r+1,t-1}^{new}\) on the feasible domain is the transfer-validity condition.
review_flags: sufficient invariance conditions may vary by SDDP formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound admissibility condition is mathematically coherent, but the claimed sufficient invariance conditions and their application to risk-averse SDDP horizon transfer have no supporting source.

children.title: Risk-Averse SDDP Software Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Implementation interfaces for risk mappings, subproblem solvers, and policy simulation.

children.title: Risk-Mapping Software Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing conditional risk mappings to computational routines.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Mapping Software Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contract for evaluating and dualizing one-step conditional risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A risk-mapping software interface for stage \(t\) is a contract that accepts a conditioning state \(s\), successor values \((z_i)_{i=1}^n\), nominal probabilities \((p_i)_{i=1}^n\), and risk parameters \(\theta_t\). It returns a value \(r=\rho_t^s(z)\) and, when required for backward cuts, a risk subgradient or dual weight vector \(q\) satisfying \(q\in\partial\rho_t^s(z)\). The interface must specify probability normalization, parameter domains, treatment of zero-probability outcomes, numerical tolerances, and error behavior. For coherent polyhedral risk mappings, returned dual weights must belong to the declared risk envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface evaluates a conditional risk mapping and supplies validated dual weights or subgradients needed to construct backward-pass cuts.
assumptions_latex: The parameter \(\theta_t\) lies in the declared domain.
The supplied successor values are finite whenever required by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r=\rho_t^s(z)\) and \(q\in\partial\rho_t^s(z)\), with \(q\) satisfying the interface's declared risk-envelope constraints.

notation.meaning: Stage-t conditional risk mapping at state s.
Returned dual weight or risk subgradient vector.

review_flags: risk-envelope requirements depend on the supported risk-mapping family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the software-interface leaf, but no source or inspectable interface specification supports the required inputs, subgradient output, risk-envelope behavior, or error contract.

children.title: Subproblem Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting stage subproblems to optimization backends.

assumptions_latex: Stages are indexed by \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\).
For state \(x_t\) and realization \(\xi_t\), the stage problem is a convex optimization problem with an available continuation approximation \(\widehat V_{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns a primal decision, objective value, feasibility status, and dual information sufficient to construct a valid cut when strong duality holds.

notation.meaning: State supplied to the stage subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contract for a convex risk-averse SDDP stage solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subproblem-solver interface accepts \((t,x_t,\xi_t,\widehat V_{t+1},\rho_t)\), forms the prescribed stage optimization problem, and returns \((s_t,v_t,u_t,\lambda_t)\). Here \(s_t\) is a termination status, \(v_t\) is the certified objective value when available, \(u_t\) is a primal decision, and \(\lambda_t\) contains dual multipliers or subgradients. The contract requires that \(s_t\) distinguish optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, and numerical failure; that reported primal and dual objects refer to the same model instance; and that, under strong duality, \(\lambda_t\) supports a valid affine lower bound for the value function at \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stage-solver interface must return consistent status, value, primal, and dual data, with dual data producing a valid value-function cut when strong duality applies.
knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Solver Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the software-interface leaf, but no citation supports the required statuses, returned dual objects, or cut-validity contract.

children.title: Policy-Simulation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces supporting out-of-sample policy evaluation and risk reporting.

assumptions_latex: A policy \(\pi=(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{T-1})\) is nonanticipative.
The simulator can sample trajectories from the specified exogenous process under a reproducible random-number stream.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an auditable collection of policy trajectories and stagewise quantities from which out-of-sample cost and risk estimates can be computed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Out-of-sample simulation contract for policies produced by risk-averse SDDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A policy-simulation interface accepts \((\pi,N,\nu_0,\mathsf P,\text{seed})\), where \(\nu_0\) is the initial-state law and \(\mathsf P\) specifies the disturbance transition law. For each replication \(i\), it generates an independent admissible trajectory by setting \(u_t^{(i)}=\pi_t(h_t^{(i)})\), advancing the system with sampled disturbances, and recording states, decisions, stage costs, and total cost \(Z^{(i)}\). It returns the trajectories together with metadata identifying the policy, model, sampling law, and random stream. Any reported risk statistic must also identify its estimator and confidence or error convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface reproducibly simulates a nonanticipative policy out of sample and returns auditable trajectories, costs, metadata, and clearly specified risk estimates.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Simulation Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the policy-simulation interface leaf, but its independence, metadata, and risk-estimator requirements have no cited support.

children.title: Risk-Averse Dynamic Programming Methods
children.top_down_role: State-space methods specific to Markov dynamic-risk models.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Risk-Averse Dynamic Programming for Markov Decision Processes

children.title: Risk-Averse Value Iteration
children.top_down_role: Value-iteration families driven by Markov risk operators.

assumptions_latex: The state and action sets are finite, and each feasible-action set \(A(x)\) is nonempty.
The discount factor satisfies \(0<\beta<1\).
Each Markov risk mapping \(\sigma_x\) is monotone, translation equivariant, and nonexpansive in the supremum norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates converge uniformly to the unique fixed point \(V^*\) of \(T\), and every selector attaining the minimum in \(TV^*=V^*\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discounted finite-state value iteration using one-step Markov risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given any bounded \(V_0\), define
\[
(TV)(x)=\min_{a\in A(x)}\left\{c(x,a)+\beta\,\sigma_x\bigl(V(X')\mid x,a\bigr)\right\},\qquad V_{k+1}=TV_k.
\]
Stop when \(\lVert V_{k+1}-V_k\rVert_\infty\leq\varepsilon(1-\beta)/(2\beta)\), and return \(V_{k+1}\) and a greedy selector. Under the assumptions, \(T\) is a \(\beta\)-contraction, so \(V_k\) converges uniformly to its unique fixed point \(V^*\); the returned greedy policy is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal under the stated residual convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply the discounted risk-adjusted Bellman operator. Contraction gives a unique value function, uniform convergence, and an approximately optimal greedy policy at the residual threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Value Iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Powell's cited value-iteration section does not establish the risk-adjusted contraction, residual bound, or policy conclusion. The conclusion concerns exact fixed-point selectors, whereas the algorithm statement also claims epsilon-optimality for the returned approximate selector.

children.title: Risk-Averse Policy Iteration
children.top_down_role: Policy evaluation and improvement under Markov dynamic risk.

assumptions_latex: The state and action sets are finite, with nonempty feasible-action sets.
The discount factor satisfies \(0<\beta<1\).
For every stationary policy, its monotone translation-equivariant Markov risk operator is a supremum-norm contraction after discounting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each strict improvement lowers the value at some state without increasing it elsewhere; hence the procedure terminates at an optimal stationary policy after finitely many improvements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact policy iteration for a discounted finite Markov risk model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize a stationary deterministic policy \(\pi_0\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate it by solving
\[
V^{\pi_k}(x)=c\bigl(x,\pi_k(x)\bigr)+\beta\,\sigma_x\bigl(V^{\pi_k}(X')\mid x,\pi_k(x)\bigr).
\]
Then choose \(\pi_{k+1}(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A(x)}(T_aV^{\pi_k})(x)\), retaining \(\pi_k(x)\) whenever it is already minimizing. Stop if \(\pi_{k+1}=\pi_k\); otherwise repeat. With exact evaluation and improvement, finite action sets imply finite termination, and the terminal policy satisfies the risk-adjusted Bellman optimality equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate exact evaluation of the current policy with risk-adjusted greedy improvement. Finite discounted models terminate at a stationary policy satisfying Bellman optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Policy Iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the risk-sensitive policy-improvement ordering and finite-termination claim require a risk-specific theorem; the cited general ADP section is insufficient.

children.title: Risk-Averse Approximate Value Methods
children.top_down_role: Function-approximation methods for risk-adjusted value functions.

assumptions_latex: The discounted risk-adjusted Bellman operator \(T\) maps bounded value functions to bounded value functions.
The approximation class is \(\mathcal V=\{V_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\).
A specified projection or fitting operator \(\Pi\) maps sampled Bellman targets into \(\mathcal V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method outputs an approximate value function and its greedy policy; its fixed points satisfy \(V_{\widehat\theta}=\Pi T V_{\widehat\theta}\), when the fitting step converges exactly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected or fitted value iteration with risk-adjusted Bellman targets.

source_refs.locator: 4 Introduction to Approximate Dynamic Programming p. 111

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\theta_0\). At iteration \(k\), sample states \(x_k^j\), compute or estimate risk-adjusted targets \(y_k^j=(TV_{\theta_k})(x_k^j)\), and fit
\[
\theta_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta}\sum_j w_k^j\,\ell\bigl(V_\theta(x_k^j),y_k^j\bigr),
\]
equivalently writing \(V_{\theta_{k+1}}=\Pi_kTV_{\theta_k}\). Stop under a declared parameter, value, or Bellman-residual tolerance. Return \(V_{\theta_{k+1}}\) and a policy greedy with respect to it. Sampling, risk estimation, fitting loss, and stopping tolerance are part of the algorithm specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a parameterized value function to sampled risk-adjusted Bellman targets, iterate to a declared tolerance, and return the approximation with its greedy policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Approximate Value Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 4 Introduction to Approximate Dynamic Programming p. 111

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fitted-value algorithm fits the leaf, but the cited general ADP material does not support risk-adjusted targets or the stated projected fixed-point conclusion under the listed assumptions.

children.title: Multistage Risk Decomposition Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Results identifying when multistage risk admits recursive conditional decomposition.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Multistage Stochastic Optimization

children.title: Finite-Tree Decomposition Regime
children.top_down_role: Recursive decomposition on finite scenario trees.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty model is a finite scenario tree of depth \(T\).
At every nonterminal node \(n\), a monotone conditional risk mapping \(\rho_n\) aggregates the values of its children.
The multistage risk functional is recursively time consistent with these nodewise mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value at every node is obtained by backward composition of its local cost with the conditional risk of child values, and the root value equals the multistage risk evaluation.

notation.meaning: Conditional risk mapping at node n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward decomposition of a time-consistent risk functional on a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(V_n=Z_n\) at every leaf \(n\). For each nonterminal node, in reverse depth order, define
\[
V_n=Z_n+\rho_n\bigl((V_m)_{m\in C(n)}\bigr).
\]
Then the root value \(V_{n_0}\) is the nested evaluation
\[
Z_{n_0}+\rho_{n_0}\bigl(Z_{n_1}+\rho_{n_1}(\cdots)\bigr),
\]
with branching interpreted nodewise. Conversely, any finite-tree risk functional specified by this nested composition admits the displayed backward decomposition. If decisions are present, replacing each node recursion by minimization over decisions measurable at that node yields the corresponding dynamic-programming recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite scenario tree, a recursively time-consistent risk evaluation is computed backward by applying each node's conditional risk mapping to its child values.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Tree Decomposition Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the finite-tree regime, but no source supports the equivalence between recursive time consistency and the displayed nodewise decomposition or its optimization extension.

children.title: General-Filtration Decomposition Regime
children.top_down_role: Measurable recursive decomposition beyond finite trees.

assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) is a filtered probability space.
Each \(\rho_{t,t+1}:L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\to L^p(\mathcal F_t)\) is local, monotone, and conditionally translation equivariant.
The dynamic risk family is strongly time consistent and normalized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(0\leq s<t\leq T\), the multistep mapping decomposes as \(\rho_{s,t}=\rho_{s,s+1}\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{t-1,t}\), up to the adopted loss-sign convention.

notation.meaning: Conditional risk mapping from time t to time s
Space of p-integrable random variables measurable at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong time-consistency decomposition on a general discrete-time filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the loss convention, strong time consistency means that for \(X,Y\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), the inequality \(\rho_{r,t}(X)\leq\rho_{r,t}(Y)\) implies \(\rho_{s,t}(X)\leq\rho_{s,t}(Y)\) whenever \(r\leq s<t\). For a normalized, local, monotone, conditionally translation-equivariant family, this property yields
\[
\rho_{s,t}(X)=\rho_{s,s+1}\bigl(\rho_{s+1,s+2}(\cdots\rho_{t-1,t}(X)\cdots)\bigr)
\]
for all \(0\leq s<t\leq T\) and \(X\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), subject to the standard regularity ensuring equality of the conditional versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized strongly time-consistent dynamic risk family on a filtration decomposes into compositions of its one-step conditional risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.title: General-Filtration Decomposition Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the stated implication compares conditional risk values at different information times rather than giving a standard precisely typed formulation of strong time consistency. The unspecified regularity clause also prevents verification of the decomposition theorem.

children.title: Coherent Envelope Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition through stable conditional risk envelopes.

assumptions_latex: Each one-step conditional risk mapping is coherent and has a conditional dual representation.
The representing probability measures are absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mathbb P\).
The family of conditional risk envelopes is stable under admissible pasting across times.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nested coherent risk evaluation equals the essential supremum of conditional expectations over the rectangular family generated by successive envelope selections.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-envelope representation of nested coherent conditional risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Z\in L^p(\mathcal F_{t+1})\), let
\[
\rho_t(Z)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_t}\mathbb E_Q[Z\mid\mathcal F_t].
\]
Stability under pasting permits the choice of a conditional density increment from \(\mathcal Q_t\) after every history. If \(\mathcal Q_{s:t}\) denotes all measures obtained by such successive selections, then for \(X\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\),
\[
(\rho_s\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{t-1})(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_{s:t}}\mathbb E_Q[X\mid\mathcal F_s].
\]
Thus rectangularity of the envelopes supplies the measurewise decomposition corresponding to recursive time consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable conditional risk envelopes combine into a rectangular family, and nested coherent risk equals worst-case conditional expectation over that pasted family.
knowledge_statements.title: Coherent Envelope Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the coherent-envelope leaf, but the conditional dual domains, density-increment compatibility, and rectangular-pasting identity require an authoritative source and more precise hypotheses.

children.title: Convex Penalty Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition through intertemporally compatible penalty functions.

assumptions_latex: Each conditional convex risk mapping admits a robust representation with a minimal conditional penalty.
All expectations and essential suprema are well defined on the chosen \(L^p\) spaces.
The dynamic risk family is strongly time consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimal multistep penalty satisfies a conditional cocycle decomposition, and this decomposition yields the nested robust representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-cocycle form of time-consistent conditional convex risk decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in L^p(\mathcal F_t)\), suppose
\[
\rho_{s,t}(X)=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{Q\in\mathcal Q_{s,t}}\left\{\mathbb E_Q[X\mid\mathcal F_s]-\alpha_{s,t}(Q)\right\}.
\]
Strong time consistency is represented on the dual side by the cocycle relation
\[
\alpha_{r,t}(Q)=\alpha_{r,s}(Q)+\mathbb E_Q[\alpha_{s,t}(Q)\mid\mathcal F_r],\qquad r\leq s\leq t,
\]
for compatible restrictions of \(Q\), together with stability of the finite-penalty dual sets under pasting. Consequently, the robust representation over \([r,t]\) decomposes into the composition of the representations over \([r,s]\) and \([s,t]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-consistent convex risk decomposes when its minimal conditional penalties add through time via a conditional cocycle and its dual measures are stable under pasting.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Penalty Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind fits the penalty-decomposition leaf, but no citation supports the cocycle equivalence, and compatibility and pasting conditions are left too vague to verify the theorem-level conclusion.

children.title: Risk-Averse Dynamic Programming Principle
children.top_down_role: Recursive optimization results for time-consistent dynamic-risk objectives.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: On a Time Consistency Concept in Risk Averse Multi-Stage Stochastic Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: On a Time Consistency Concept in Risk Averse Multi-Stage Stochastic Programming

children.title: Finite-Horizon Risk Recursion
children.top_down_role: Backward recursive optimization over finite horizons.

assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) is finite and the controlled process has measurable state and action spaces.
Feasible policies are nonanticipative, and measurable minimizing selectors exist.
The objective is a nested composition of monotone one-step conditional risk mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal value is obtained by backward risk-adjusted Bellman recursion, and measurable minimizers define an optimal Markov policy.

notation.meaning: Controlled transition from state and action

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon Bellman principle for a nested dynamic risk objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(V_T(x)=g_T(x)\). For \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\), define
\[
V_t(x)=\inf_{a\in A_t(x)}\left\{c_t(x,a)+\rho_t\bigl(V_{t+1}(F_t(x,a,\xi_{t+1}))\bigr)\right\}.
\]
Then \(V_0(x_0)\) equals the infimum of the nested dynamic-risk objective over all admissible policies. If the infimum at every stage is attained by a measurable selector \(a_t^*(x)\), the policy \(\pi^*=(a_0^*,\ldots,a_{T-1}^*)\) is optimal. The recursion relies on the objective's recursive time consistency; a nonnested static risk of total cost need not satisfy it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-horizon nested risk objective is optimized backward: terminal value initializes a risk-adjusted Bellman recursion whose measurable minimizers form an optimal policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Risk Recursion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits finite-horizon recursion, but the cited generic finite-horizon section does not support nested conditional risk. The assumptions also do not explicitly ensure that state alone is sufficient for the displayed state-based recursion and Markov-policy conclusion.

children.title: Markov Risk Recursion
children.top_down_role: State-based recursion for controlled Markov systems.

assumptions_latex: The controlled state process is Markov with transition kernel \(P_t(\cdot\mid x,a)\).
The one-step risk mapping depends on history only through the current state, action, and transition law.
Measurable minimizing selectors exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursively defined value depends only on the current state, and a state-feedback selector attaining each Bellman minimum is optimal for the nested risk objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-based Bellman representation for controlled Markov risk models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X'\sim P_t(\cdot\mid x,a)\). The Markov risk property permits the conditional evaluation of a bounded next-state value \(v\) to be written as \(\sigma_t(v,x,a)\), independent of earlier history. Therefore the finite-horizon value recursion is
\[
V_T(x)=g_T(x),\qquad V_t(x)=\inf_{a\in A_t(x)}\left\{c_t(x,a)+\sigma_t(V_{t+1},x,a)\right\}.
\]
For every admissible history ending at state \(x\), the continuation value equals \(V_t(x)\). Hence any measurable selector attaining the displayed infimum defines an optimal Markov policy for the recursively composed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When transitions and one-step risk depend on history only through the current state and action, the nested problem has a state-based Bellman recursion and Markov optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Markov Risk Recursion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Markov-recursion leaf, but no citation supports reduction from history-dependent admissible policies to state values and optimal measurable Markov selectors under the stated assumptions.

children.title: Stationary Infinite-Horizon Risk Recursion
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point and stationary-policy regimes for long horizons.

children.title: Stationary Risk Recursion
children.top_down_role: Time-homogeneous recursive risk evaluation in Markov settings.

assumptions_latex: The stationary controlled Markov model has bounded one-stage cost \(c\) and nonempty feasible-action sets.
The discount factor satisfies \(0<\beta<1\).
The stationary Markov risk mapping \(\sigma\) is monotone and nonexpansive in the supremum norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stationary Bellman operator has a unique bounded fixed point, value iteration converges to it, and any measurable minimizing selector is an optimal stationary policy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discounted stationary recursion under a nonexpansive Markov risk mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the stationary Bellman operator on bounded functions by
\[
(TV)(x)=\inf_{a\in A(x)}\left\{c(x,a)+\beta\,\sigma(V,x,a)\right\}.
\]
Under the assumptions, \(T\) is a \(\beta\)-contraction in the supremum norm. Consequently, there is a unique bounded function \(V^*\) satisfying \(V^*=TV^*\), and \(T^kV_0\to V^*\) uniformly for every bounded \(V_0\). If a measurable selector \(a^*(x)\) attains the infimum in \((TV^*)(x)\), then the stationary policy \(\pi^*(x)=a^*(x)\) is optimal for the infinite-horizon recursively evaluated discounted-risk criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discounting and a nonexpansive stationary risk mapping make the Bellman operator contractive, yielding a unique value, convergent iteration, and an optimal stationary selector.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Risk Recursion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contraction calculation is plausible, but no source supports identifying its fixed point and minimizing selector with the infinite-horizon recursively evaluated risk criterion. That criterion and the required Markov-risk structure are not defined precisely enough to verify the optimality conclusion.

children.title: Infinite-Horizon Risk Recursion
children.top_down_role: Recursive risk evaluation over unbounded planning horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Horizon Risk Recursion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discounted, stationary Markov recursion with a one-step conditional risk mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the state space be \(S\), let \(A(s)\) be the feasible actions, and let \(P(\cdot\mid s,a)\) be a stationary transition kernel. For discount factor \(\beta\in(0,1)\), bounded cost \(c\), and a monotone, translation-equivariant conditional risk mapping \(\rho_{s,a}\), define \((TV)(s)=\inf_{a\in A(s)}\{c(s,a)+\beta\rho_{s,a}(V(S'))\}\). The infinite-horizon risk recursion is \(V_{n+1}=TV_n\); whenever \(V_n\) converges in the sup norm, its limit \(V\) satisfies \(V=TV\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The infinite-horizon value iterates a stationary risk-sensitive Bellman operator; any uniform limit is a fixed point of that operator.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and all iterates are bounded
\(\rho_{s,a}\) is monotone and translation equivariant
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{n+1}=TV_n\quad\text{and}\quad V=TV\text{ whenever }V_n\to V\text{ uniformly}.\)

notation.meaning: one-step conditional risk mapping after state-action pair
next state distributed according to the transition kernel

review_flags: risk-sensitive extension not directly certified by supplied locator

children.title: Fixed-Point Regimes
children.top_down_role: Long-horizon regimes organized by stationary value relationships.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique fixed point for discounted stationary risk recursion on bounded value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(S)\) be the bounded real functions on \(S\). Suppose each \(\rho_{s,a}\) is monotone and translation equivariant, so that \(|\rho_{s,a}(X)-\rho_{s,a}(Y)|\leq\lVert X-Y\rVert_\infty\). If \(T:B(S)\to B(S)\) is the operator \((TV)(s)=\inf_{a\in A(s)}\{c(s,a)+\beta\rho_{s,a}(V(S'))\}\) with \(0<\beta<1\), then \(\lVert TV-TW\rVert_\infty\leq\beta\lVert V-W\rVert_\infty\). Consequently, \(T\) has a unique fixed point \(V^*\), and \(T^nV_0\to V^*\) for every \(V_0\in B(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discounting makes the stationary risk Bellman operator a contraction, yielding a unique value and convergence of value iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(T:B(S)\to B(S)\)
\(\rho_{s,a}\) is monotone and translation equivariant
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!V^*\in B(S):TV^*=V^*,\qquad \lVert T^nV_0-V^*\rVert_\infty\to0.\)

notation.meaning: bounded real-valued functions on the state space

review_flags: conditional-risk contraction requires direct source confirmation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem and content kind fit the fixed-point leaf, but the cited locator does not directly certify contraction for monotone, translation-equivariant conditional risk mappings.

children.title: Stationary-Policy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Long-horizon settings supporting time-homogeneous policy structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary-Policy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal stationary selectors under attainment of the risk-sensitive Bellman minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V^*\) be the unique bounded fixed point of the discounted stationary operator \(T\). Assume that, for every \(s\in S\), the infimum in \((TV^*)(s)\) is attained by a measurable selector \(\pi^*(s)\in A(s)\). Define \((T_{\pi^*}V)(s)=c(s,\pi^*(s))+\beta\rho_{s,\pi^*(s)}(V(S'))\). Then \(T_{\pi^*}V^*=TV^*=V^*\), and the stationary Markov policy that applies \(\pi^*\) at every time realizes the recursively defined infinite-horizon value \(V^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable action selector attaining the Bellman minimum at every state defines an optimal stationary Markov policy.
assumptions_latex: \(V^*=TV^*\) is the unique bounded fixed point
the Bellman infimum is attained statewise
an attaining selector \(\pi^*\) is measurable
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\pi^*}V^*=V^*\), and \(\pi^*\) is optimal among admissible policies for the recursive criterion.
review_flags: direct source for measurable selection and recursive-risk policy optimality required

children.title: Nonrecursive Objective Boundary
children.top_down_role: The boundary at which the original criterion does not support Bellman decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrecursive Objective Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-inconsistent criteria for which continuation values are insufficient Bellman states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a terminal random cost \(Z\) and \(\lambda>0\), consider the static mean-variance criterion \(J(Z)=\mathbb E[Z]+\lambda\operatorname{Var}(Z)\). At an intermediate information field \(\mathcal F_t\), direct substitution of the conditional criterion omits the dispersion of conditional means because \(\operatorname{Var}(Z)=\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)]+\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t])\). Hence minimizing \(\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F_t]+\lambda\operatorname{Var}(Z\mid\mathcal F_t)\) need not preserve a policy chosen at time zero. Without augmenting the state or adopting an equilibrium formulation, the original objective has no Bellman decomposition based only on the physical state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static mean-variance objectives are generally time inconsistent because conditional optimization drops variation among conditional means.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\)
\(\mathcal F_t\) is a nontrivial intermediate information field
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\) generally cannot be represented by a time-consistent Bellman recursion on the unaugmented physical state.

notation.meaning: information available at the intermediate time

review_flags: time-consistency boundary requires an authoritative dynamic-risk source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mean-variance example fit the node, but the asserted absence of an unaugmented Bellman decomposition requires an authoritative source on dynamic inconsistency.

children.title: Base-Model Recourse Regime Taxonomy

children.title: Polyhedral Finite-Support Regime
children.top_down_role: Classical finite-support linear and polyhedral convergence setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Finite-Support Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical SDDP regime with finite scenarios, linear recourse, and polyhedral risk envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each stage \(t\), let the disturbance have finite support \(\{\xi_t^1,\ldots,\xi_t^{m_t}\}\). Require a nonempty polyhedral feasible correspondence, affine stage cost, relatively complete recourse, and a conditional coherent risk measure with polyhedral envelope \(\mathcal Q_t\subset\{q\geq0:\sum_jq_j=1\}\). Then the stage operator maps convex polyhedral continuation values to convex polyhedral values through finite maximization over \(q\in\mathcal Q_t\) and linear recourse minimization. Consequently, globally valid affine supporting cuts are available, placing the model in the classical polyhedral finite-support SDDP regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite scenarios, linear recourse, and polyhedral risk envelopes preserve polyhedral value functions and permit globally valid SDDP cuts.
assumptions_latex: each disturbance has finite support
stage feasible sets and costs are polyhedral-affine with relatively complete recourse
each conditional risk envelope is a nonempty polytope
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dynamic-programming value functions are convex polyhedral and admit global affine lower supports.
review_flags: supplied locator covers recourse but not risk-averse SDDP convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the regime, but the recourse locator does not support risk-envelope polyhedrality or risk-averse SDDP cut validity. Precise finite-horizon and state-dependence hypotheses also require confirmation.

children.title: Convex Continuous-Support Regime
children.top_down_role: Convex convergence settings requiring continuous-support approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Continuous-Support Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex SDDP regime requiring controlled integration or sampling over continuous disturbances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each stage disturbance have a possibly continuous distribution. Assume convex lower-semicontinuous stage costs, convex feasible correspondences with relatively complete recourse, and finite risk-adjusted continuation values. A continuous-support SDDP approximation is compatible with convergence only when its quadrature or sampling rule consistently approximates both the conditional risk functional and subgradient expectations on the states visited, while generated cuts remain globally valid lower bounds. Suitable domination or uniform-integrability conditions must control interchange of limits, risk evaluation, and conditional integration. Finite-support convergence arguments do not apply merely by replacing the distribution with an arbitrary fixed discretization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous-support convex models require consistent risk integration, valid cuts, and limit-interchange control; arbitrary fixed discretization is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: stage problems are proper, convex, and lower semicontinuous
recourse is relatively complete and risk-adjusted values are finite
sampling or quadrature consistently estimates values and subgradients
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model lies in a convex continuous-support regime only under controlled distributional approximation and globally valid cutting planes.
review_flags: exact convergence topology and integrability hypotheses require a continuous-support risk-averse SDDP source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition belongs in this leaf, but convergence depends on a precise approximation topology, sampling design, integrability assumptions, and cut construction, none of which is sourced sufficiently.

children.title: Discrete-Nonconvex Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary where standard global convex convergence theory no longer applies.

children.title: Integer-Recourse Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of standard global convergence guarantees arising from discrete recourse decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Recourse Convergence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convex cut validity caused by integer recourse decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the scalar recourse value \(Q(x)=\min\{y:y\in\mathbb Z,\ y\geq x\}=\lceil x\rceil\). Although the constraint is linear, \(Q\) is discontinuous at every integer and is not convex. Therefore the convex-subgradient inequality \(Q(x)\geq Q(\bar x)+g(x-\bar x)\) need not admit a supporting slope suitable for classical SDDP. More generally, integer recourse can destroy convexity and continuity of stage value functions, so convergence arguments based on globally valid affine cuts do not extend without integer-specific value-function approximations, enumeration, or valid disjunctive cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even linear integer recourse can produce discontinuous, nonconvex values, invalidating classical subgradient cuts and their convergence theory.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R\)
\(y\in\mathbb Z\)
the classical method requires global affine supporting lower bounds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integer recourse alone can place the value function outside the convex-cut SDDP convergence regime.

notation.meaning: least integer not smaller than x

review_flags: concrete counterexample is standard but an integer-recourse decomposition source is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ceiling-function example correctly demonstrates a nonconvex, discontinuous integer-recourse value and fits a failure boundary, but its claimed consequence for classical SDDP convergence needs a direct decomposition reference.

children.title: Nonconvex-Recourse Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of convex convergence theory arising from nonconvex recourse structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Recourse Convergence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global supporting cuts when continuous recourse is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\min\{(x-1)^2,(x+1)^2\}\) for \(x\in\mathbb R\). This value function can arise by choosing between two nonconvex recourse branches. It is nonconvex: \(Q(-1)=Q(1)=0\), whereas \(Q(0)=1\). Thus no convexity-based affine cut model can converge globally to \(Q\) while remaining a lower representation generated solely from ordinary subgradients. In multistage problems, nonconvex recourse therefore lies beyond classical SDDP convergence unless a global nonconvex relaxation, spatial partition, or other globally valid bounding mechanism replaces convex supporting cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex recourse may yield values violating convexity, so ordinary SDDP supporting cuts cannot globally represent them.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R\)
the approximation uses convex affine lower-cut models
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(0)>\tfrac12Q(-1)+\tfrac12Q(1)\), so classical convex-cut convergence is inapplicable.
review_flags: global nonconvex SDDP boundary requires a directly supporting source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit value function is nonconvex and the content kind fits, but the general boundary asserted for multistage SDDP and the proposed replacement mechanisms need direct source support.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Nonconvex Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined structural effects when discrete decisions occur within nonconvex recourse models.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Nonconvex Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined discrete selection and nonlinear recourse creates separated value-function branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R\), define \(Q(x)=\min_{z\in\{0,1\}}(x-(2z-1))^2=\min\{(x+1)^2,(x-1)^2\}\). The binary variable selects one of two nonlinear recourse branches. The resulting value satisfies \(Q(-1)=Q(1)=0\) and \(Q(0)=1\), hence is nonconvex even though each fixed-\(z\) branch is convex. Integer selection and nonlinear recourse can therefore create switching surfaces, disconnected minimizers, and invalid global subgradient cuts. Classical risk-averse SDDP convergence requires replacement by certified global lower bounds or a restricted formulation restoring convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary selection among convex nonlinear branches can produce a nonconvex value, combining integer and nonconvex convergence failures.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R\)
each fixed-binary branch is convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed-integer value \(Q\) is nonconvex and lacks the global convex-cut structure required by classical SDDP.
review_flags: interaction example is explicit but convergence implications need a mixed-integer decomposition source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary-branch example correctly produces a nonconvex value and fits the interaction leaf, but the broader risk-averse SDDP convergence implications require a mixed-integer decomposition source.

children.title: Local-Certificate Regime
children.top_down_role: Restricted forms of convergence evidence available beyond the global convex setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Certificate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification restricted to a specified neighborhood or fixed discrete configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be a specified nonempty neighborhood, let \(Q:U\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be the objective value, and let \(\bar x\in U\) be an incumbent with an achievable value \(J(\bar x)\). Suppose \(L_U(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in U\). If \(J(\bar x)-\inf_{x\in U}L_U(x)\leq\varepsilon\), then the incumbent is at most \(\varepsilon\) above the optimum represented on \(U\). If \(L_U\) is not valid outside \(U\), this condition does not certify global optimality or classical global SDDP convergence; the certificate must record its neighborhood, discrete assignment, or basin of validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent is locally epsilon-optimal when its value is within epsilon of a valid lower bound on the optimum over the specified neighborhood; no global guarantee follows without a globally valid bound.
assumptions_latex: \(U\neq\varnothing\) and \(\bar x\in U\)
\(L_U(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in U\)
\(J(\bar x)\) is an achievable objective value
\(J(\bar x)-\inf_{x\in U}L_U(x)\leq\varepsilon\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J(\bar x)-\inf_{x\in U}Q(x)\leq\varepsilon\); this is a certificate on \(U\), not a global certificate.

notation.meaning: objective value on the restricted regime
pointwise lower model valid on the restricted regime

children.title: Risk-Sampling Compatibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Compatibility regimes linking conditional risk evaluation with sampling.

children.title: Risk-Envelope Compatibility Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence under decomposable and computationally accessible conditional envelopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope Compatibility Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral conditional risk envelopes compatible with stagewise decomposition and cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stage and conditioning state, require the conditional risk functional to have the dual form \(\rho_t(Z)=\sup_{q\in\mathcal Q_t}\sum_{j=1}^{m_t}q_jZ_j\), where \(\mathcal Q_t\) is nonempty, convex, compact, computationally accessible, and contained in the probability simplex. The envelope description must depend only on information available at stage \(t\) and compose with later conditional mappings. If optimization over \(\mathcal Q_t\) is solved exactly, or with certified vanishing error, risk evaluation and generation of valid risk-adjusted cuts remain decomposable. An inaccessible, nondecomposable, or time-inconsistent envelope falls outside this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact, stagewise, computable risk envelope permits decomposable risk evaluation and valid risk-adjusted cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Q_t\) is a nonempty compact convex subset of the probability simplex
the envelope is measurable using stage-t information
envelope optimization is exact or has certified vanishing error
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditional risk evaluation is compatible with stagewise decomposition and globally valid risk-adjusted cuts.
review_flags: dual conditional-risk representation and SDDP compatibility require a direct authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the risk-envelope compatibility leaf, but conditional dual representation, time consistency, measurability, and validity of risk-adjusted cuts all require a direct authoritative source.

children.title: Risk-Adjusted Sampling Coverage
children.top_down_role: Sampling support for scenarios and tail-relevant events.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Adjusted Sampling Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent sampling of every scenario that can receive positive risk-envelope weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_t=\{j:\sup_{q\in\mathcal Q_t}q_j>0\}\) be the scenarios relevant to stage-t risk evaluation. For every \(j\in I_t\), require the sampling law at iteration \(k\) to satisfy \(p_{t,j}^{(k)}\geq\epsilon_{t,j}>0\), conditionally on the past, or more generally \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}p_{t,j}^{(k)}=\infty\) with an appropriate conditional independence or martingale coverage condition. Then each risk-relevant scenario is sampled infinitely often almost surely. Sampling that excludes a tail scenario with positive admissible envelope weight cannot consistently identify its contribution to risk-adjusted cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every scenario that may receive positive risk weight must be sampled persistently; otherwise tail contributions can remain unidentified.
assumptions_latex: \(I_t=\{j:\sup_{q\in\mathcal Q_t}q_j>0\}\)
\(p_{t,j}^{(k)}\geq\epsilon_{t,j}>0\) for every \(j\in I_t\)
sampling is conditionally independent or satisfies a suitable conditional Borel--Cantelli condition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(j\in I_t\) is sampled infinitely often almost surely.

notation.meaning: iteration-k conditional sampling probability of scenario j

review_flags: risk-envelope coverage condition is more specific than supplied importance-sampling locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Persistent positive conditional sampling probabilities support infinite visitation under an appropriate conditional Borel–Cantelli result, but the importance-sampling locator does not directly establish this risk-envelope coverage condition or its SDDP consequence.

children.title: Dependent-Process Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Changes required beyond stagewise independence or finite-state Markov structure.

assumptions_latex: The disturbance process admits regular conditional laws given histories.
Each stage problem has nonempty compact feasible sets and lower semicontinuous costs.
The conditional risk mappings are monotone and continuous on the relevant integrable-cost space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence requires a sufficient information state and conditionally covering samples; unconditional finite-support sampling alone is insufficient.

notation.meaning: Information state sufficient for conditional transitions and risk evaluation
Conditional risk mapping at stage t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dependent disturbances require conditioning on history or a sufficient information state
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for extending finite-state, stagewise-independent convergence arguments to history-dependent disturbances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dependent disturbance process, a recursion based only on the physical state is generally invalid when either the conditional transition law or \(\rho_t(\cdot\mid H_t)\) depends on information in \(H_t\) omitted from that state. A convergence argument must instead use an information state \(S_t=\phi_t(H_t)\) satisfying conditional sufficiency for both transition and risk evaluation, and its sampling rule must visit every conditionally relevant outcome or risk-envelope extreme point with persistent positive probability. Without these changes, two histories having the same physical state can have different continuation values, so a single statewise approximation may converge to neither correct value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent processes require sufficient information states and conditional sampling coverage; otherwise histories merged into one physical state can have different risk-adjusted continuation values.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependent-Process Convergence Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind and local topic fit are appropriate, but no inspectable source is supplied. In particular, the asserted necessity of persistent coverage of every conditionally relevant outcome or risk-envelope extreme point depends on the precise dependent-process algorithm and cannot be certified from standard-field rationale alone.

children.title: Convergence Objects
children.top_down_role: Distinct objects addressed by risk-averse SDDP convergence results.

children.title: Risk-Adjusted Value-Approximation Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence of recursive lower approximations to risk-adjusted value functions.

assumptions_latex: Every true stage value function is finite and convex on a compact reachable state set.
The generated approximations are valid lower bounds, are monotone by iteration, and use exact risk-compatible Bellman cuts.
Every relevant state and risk-envelope component is sampled persistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every stage \(t\), \(\underline V_t^k(x)\to V_t(x)\) at all accumulation points of sampled reachable states, almost surely.

notation.meaning: True risk-adjusted value function at stage t
Iteration-k lower approximation of the stage-t value function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure pointwise convergence on sampled reachable states, not uniform convergence on the entire state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\underline V_t^0\leq V_t\) for every stage. At iteration \(k\), retain all previous cuts and add a supporting cut obtained from the exact one-step risk-adjusted Bellman problem, so that \(\underline V_t^{k-1}\leq\underline V_t^k\leq V_t\). If sampling persistently exposes every continuation outcome and every risk-envelope component needed at each accumulation point of the trial-state sequence, then, with probability one, \(\underline V_t^k(x)\to V_t(x)\) for every such point \(x\) and every stage \(t\). The claim does not assert uniform convergence away from the sampled reachable set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone valid Bellman lower approximations converge almost surely to each risk-adjusted value function at persistently sampled reachable states.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Adjusted Value-Approximation Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the convergence-object container and appropriately limits the claim to sampled reachable states, but the almost-sure convergence result requires an authoritative risk-averse SDDP theorem with precise sampling, cut-generation, measurability, and regularity hypotheses.

children.title: Policy-Decision Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence properties of generated decisions and policies.

children.title: Trial-Policy Sequence Convergence
children.top_down_role: Limit behavior of trial policies generated across decomposition iterations.

assumptions_latex: For each stage \(t\) and visited state \(x\), the feasible action set \(A_t(x)\) is nonempty and compact.
The functions \(Q_t^k(x,\cdot)\) converge uniformly to the continuous function \(Q_t(x,\cdot)\) on \(A_t(x)\).
The limiting problem has the unique minimizer \(\pi_t^*(x)\) at every state covered by the claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every stage \(t\) and visited state \(x\) covered by the assumptions, \(\pi_t^k(x)\to\pi_t^*(x)\); without uniqueness, every accumulation point is optimal.

notation.meaning: Trial policy constructed at iteration k
Feasible action set at stage t and state x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform objective convergence on a compact feasible set and a unique limiting minimizer imply argmin convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise convergence of trial policies at visited states; no convergence on unvisited states or measurable global-policy convergence is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stage \(t\) and a visited state \(x\), choose \(\pi_t^k(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A_t(x)}Q_t^k(x,a)\). If \(Q_t^k(x,\cdot)\to Q_t(x,\cdot)\) uniformly on the nonempty compact set \(A_t(x)\), then every accumulation point of \(\{\pi_t^k(x)\}\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A_t(x)}Q_t(x,a)\). If this argmin is the singleton \(\{\pi_t^*(x)\}\), then \(\pi_t^k(x)\to\pi_t^*(x)\). Applying the statement separately at each stage and visited state gives pointwise convergence there; without uniqueness, only optimality of accumulation points is guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each visited state, uniform convergence of approximate stage objectives makes every trial-decision accumulation point optimal, and a unique limiting minimizer forces pointwise convergence of the trial policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Policy Sequence Convergence

children.title: Decision-Sequence Convergence
children.top_down_role: Limit behavior of stagewise decisions produced by successive approximations.

assumptions_latex: The state and action spaces are metric spaces, and \(x^k\to x^*\).
The feasible-action correspondence \(A\) is nonempty compact-valued and both upper and lower hemicontinuous at \(x^*\).
The functions \(Q^k\) converge uniformly to the continuous function \(Q\) on a compact neighborhood containing the relevant feasible pairs.
The set \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A(x^*)}Q(x^*,a)\) is the singleton \(\{a^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sequence satisfying \(a^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A(x^k)}Q^k(x^k,a)\) converges to \(a^*\).

notation.meaning: Trial state and selected decision at iteration k
Limiting state and its unique optimal decision

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compact argmin stability under uniform objective convergence and continuity of the feasible correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Argmin convergence along a convergent trial-state sequence when the limiting decision is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x^k\to x^*\) and \(a^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A(x^k)}Q^k(x^k,a)\). If \(A\) is nonempty compact-valued and both upper and lower hemicontinuous at \(x^*\), while \(Q^k\to Q\) uniformly on a compact neighborhood containing the relevant feasible pairs and \(Q\) is continuous, then every accumulation point of \(\{a^k\}\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A(x^*)}Q(x^*,a)\). Consequently, if this argmin is \(\{a^*\}\), then \(a^k\to a^*\). Without uniqueness, the theorem guarantees only optimality of accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along convergent states, uniform objective convergence and continuity of the compact feasible-action correspondence make every decision accumulation point optimal; uniqueness forces convergence of the full decision sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Sequence Convergence

children.title: Policy-Limit Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Feasibility status of accumulation points associated with generated policies.

assumptions_latex: Every trial decision is feasible for its corresponding trial history or state.
The trial histories and decisions converge componentwise.
Each stage feasible-action correspondence has a closed graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting policy is feasible at every history where the componentwise limit is defined.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility is preserved under limits by closed-graph correspondences
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-graph preservation of feasibility; global measurability requires a separate argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stage \(t\), let \(a_t^k\in A_t(h_t^k)\), and suppose \((h_t^k,a_t^k)\to(h_t,a_t)\). If the graph \(\{(h,a):a\in A_t(h)\}\) is closed, then \(a_t\in A_t(h_t)\). Hence any pointwise policy limit satisfying \(\pi_t(h_t)=a_t\) is feasible at every history covered by the convergence. This statement certifies feasibility of pointwise limits only; to obtain an admissible policy on the entire history space, the limiting selectors must additionally be measurable and nonanticipative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed feasible-action graphs preserve feasibility under convergent trial histories and decisions, though global policy admissibility still requires measurable nonanticipative selectors.
knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Limit Feasibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the policy-limit-feasibility leaf and correctly restricts the closed-graph conclusion to histories covered by pointwise convergence while separating measurability and nonanticipativity. No citation is supplied, so it remains source-dependent candidate knowledge.

children.title: Decision-Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing whether approximate value convergence yields stable decisions.

assumptions_latex: The action set \(A\) is nonempty and compact, and the true objective \(Q:A\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
The approximate objectives satisfy \(\sup_{a\in A}|Q^k(a)-Q(a)|\leq\varepsilon_k\), where \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).
Each \(a^k\) is an exact minimizer of \(Q^k\) on \(A\).
For the quantitative regime, \(Q(a)\geq\min_{b\in A}Q(b)+(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(a,A^*)^2\) for all \(a\in A\), with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(A^*\) is a singleton, then \(a^k\) converges to its unique element; under quadratic growth, \(\operatorname{dist}(a^k,A^*)\leq\sqrt{4\varepsilon_k/\mu}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform objective error and quadratic growth control distance to the argmin set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two sufficient decision-stability regimes: a unique minimizer for convergence and quadratic growth for a quantitative distance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}Q(a)\), suppose \(\sup_{a\in A}|Q^k(a)-Q(a)|\leq\varepsilon_k\), and choose \(a^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in A}Q^k(a)\). If \(A^*\) is a singleton and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), compactness and continuity imply convergence of \(a^k\) to its unique element. More quantitatively, if \(Q(a)\geq\min_{b\in A}Q(b)+(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(a,A^*)^2\) for every \(a\in A\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(a^k,A^*)\leq\sqrt{4\varepsilon_k/\mu}\). Thus uniform objective convergence controls decisions only when an isolation or growth condition is also available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique true minimizer converts uniform objective convergence into decision convergence; quadratic growth yields the distance bound equal to the square root of four times the uniform error divided by the growth modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Stability Regimes

children.title: Bound-Estimator Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence properties of lower and policy-evaluation estimators.

assumptions_latex: The lower estimator is measurable, valid at every iteration, and converges almost surely to the optimal value.
Policy-evaluation replications are conditionally independent given the evaluated policy.
Evaluated risk-adjusted costs are integrable, and the evaluated policies converge to an optimal policy with continuous value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower estimates and consistent policy-evaluation estimates converge almost surely to the optimal risk-adjusted value.

notation.meaning: Risk-aware evaluation estimator for policy k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure convergence of lower estimates and separately replicated policy evaluations under consistent nested-risk estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(L_k\leq v^*\) almost surely and \(L_k	o v^*\) almost surely. For each fixed \(k\), suppose \(U_{k,m}\to v(\pi^k)\) almost surely as the replication count \(m\to\infty\), where the estimator respects the nesting of the conditional risk mappings. If \(v(\pi^k)\to v^*\), then any diagonal sequence \(m(k)\to\infty\) chosen sufficiently rapidly for consistency satisfies \(U_{k,m(k)}	o v^*\) almost surely. Thus the lower and policy-evaluation estimators converge to the same value, although finite-sample ordering \(L_k\leq U_{k,m}\) need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid lower estimates and consistent nested-risk policy evaluations converge to the same optimal value when evaluated policies become optimal and sample sizes grow sufficiently.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Estimator Convergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem belongs in the bound-estimator convergence container, but fixed-policy almost-sure consistency does not by itself justify almost-sure convergence along an unspecified diagonal sample-size sequence. Rates, summable error probabilities, uniform consistency, or an explicit diagonal-selection result are needed, together with a source for nested dynamic-risk estimation.

children.title: Dynamic-Risk Stability Approximation Theory
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity and approximation results linking stochastic-process models to risk-adjusted values and policies.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Multistage Stochastic Optimization

children.title: Nested-Distance Stability
children.top_down_role: Stability under approximations preserving multistage information structure.

assumptions_latex: Two filtered process laws have finite first moments and are compared by a nested distance compatible with their filtrations.
The admissible policies are nonanticipative under both models.
The total cost is uniformly Lipschitz along coupled process paths, and each conditional risk mapping is monotone and nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal values satisfy \(|v(P)-v(Q)|\leq Ld_{\mathrm{nest}}(P,Q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz value stability under filtration-preserving, bicausal perturbations of the process law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(P)\) and \(v(Q)\) be optimal values of the same multistage nonanticipative model under filtered laws \(P\) and \(Q\). Suppose every admissible policy has a nested risk-adjusted cost functional whose difference under any bicausal coupling \(\gamma\) is bounded by \(L\int d(\xi,\tilde\xi)\,d\gamma\). Taking the infimum over bicausal couplings and then comparing optimal policies in both directions yields \(|v(P)-v(Q)|\leq Ld_{\mathrm{nest}}(P,Q)\). Ordinary Wasserstein distance cannot replace the nested distance here because it need not preserve the multistage information structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When risk-adjusted policy costs are uniformly pathwise Lipschitz, optimal values are Lipschitz in nested distance, which preserves multistage information.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Distance Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is well matched to nested-distance stability, but no source establishes that the nested risk-adjusted policy cost satisfies the required coupling bound or that the same admissible-policy comparison is valid in both directions. The stated Lipschitz constant is therefore not independently supported.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Approximation for Dynamic Risk
children.top_down_role: Approximation effects from tree construction, reduction, and probability adjustment.

assumptions_latex: The original filtered process law and each scenario-tree law have finite first moments.
Tree policies are nonanticipative with respect to tree nodes.
The dynamic-risk objective satisfies a nested-distance stability bound with modulus \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(d_{\mathrm{nest}}(P,P_N)\to0\), then \(v(P_N)\to v(P)\), with \(|v(P_N)-v(P)|\leq Ld_{\mathrm{nest}}(P,P_N)\).

notation.meaning: Law represented by the N-th scenario tree
Optimal value under a process law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value consistency for tree construction, reduction, or probability adjustment measured in nested distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the original filtered law by \(P\) and a constructed, reduced, or probability-adjusted scenario tree by \(P_N\). If the dynamic-risk model has the stability property \(|v(P)-v(Q)|\leq Ld_{\mathrm{nest}}(P,Q)\), then \(|v(P_N)-v(P)|\leq Ld_{\mathrm{nest}}(P_N,P)\). Consequently, any sequence of trees converging to \(P\) in nested distance has convergent optimal values. Weak convergence of path distributions alone is not sufficient, because tree modification may alter conditional distributions and the information available at intermediate stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario-tree values converge when construction, reduction, and probability changes drive nested distance to zero; ordinary weak convergence need not preserve information structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Approximation for Dynamic Risk

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional implication from a nested-distance stability bound is mathematically plausible and fits the scenario-tree approximation container. However, the cited scenario-tree section does not support the asserted nested-distance convergence criterion or its dynamic-risk extension, so an authoritative stability or scenario-process approximation source is required.

children.title: Filtration Approximation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds associated with changing the available information structure.

assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) is finite and \(\mathcal G_t\subseteq\mathcal F_t\) for every stage \(t\).
The projected disturbance is \(\widehat\xi_t=\mathbb E[\xi_t\mid\mathcal G_t]\), and \(\xi_t\) is integrable.
For a fixed policy class \(\Pi\) admissible in both compared models, the nested risk-adjusted objective is stagewise Lipschitz with propagated constants \(L_t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection component of the value perturbation satisfies \(|v^{\Pi}(\xi)-v^{\Pi}(\widehat\xi)|\leq\sum_{t=1}^T L_t\mathbb E[\|\xi_t-\widehat\xi_t\|]\); a policy-class restriction caused by filtration coarsening requires a separate value-of-information term.

notation.meaning: Stage-t disturbance and its conditional projection
Policy class held fixed in the projection comparison
Optimal value over the fixed policy class for a specified disturbance process

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-error bound with a common policy class; the effect of changing admissible information is explicitly excluded from the displayed bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G_t\subseteq\mathcal F_t\) and define \(\widehat\xi_t=\mathbb E[\xi_t\mid\mathcal G_t]\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\). Fix a policy class \(\Pi\) that is admissible in both models. If backward propagation through the conditional risk mappings makes the objective uniformly stagewise Lipschitz with constants \(L_t\), then the projection component of the perturbation satisfies \(|v^{\Pi}(\xi)-v^{\Pi}(\widehat\xi)|\leq\sum_{t=1}^T L_t\mathbb E[\|\xi_t-\widehat\xi_t\|]\). If replacing \((\mathcal F_t)\) by \((\mathcal G_t)\) also restricts the admissible policy class, the resulting value-of-information term is separate and is not bounded by projection error alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a common admissible policy class, propagated Lipschitz constants bound the value effect of conditional projection errors. Any additional loss from restricting decisions to a coarser filtration must be analyzed separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Filtration Approximation Bounds

children.title: Risk-Parameter Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of values and policies to dynamic-risk parameters.

assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) is finite, and the stage costs and feasible sets do not depend on the risk parameter vector.

For every stage \(t\), the conditional risk mapping is finite on the relevant continuation-cost space and satisfies \(|\rho_t^{\theta_t}(Z)-\rho_t^{\theta_t'}(Z)|\leq K_t\|\theta_t-\theta_t'\|\) uniformly over continuation costs generated by admissible policies.
For every stage \(t\), the conditional risk mapping is nonexpansive in its cost argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal value satisfies \(|v(\theta)-v(\theta')|\leq\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}K_t\|\theta_t-\theta_t'\|\); policy sensitivity requires additional argmin regularity.

notation.meaning: Optimal value under a risk-parameter vector
Stage-t conditional risk mapping with parameter theta_t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: backward induction propagates uniform parameter-Lipschitz bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon value sensitivity only; continuity or quantitative stability of optimal policies is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that, for each \(t=1,\ldots,T-1\), the conditional risk mapping satisfies \(|\rho_t^{\theta_t}(Z)-\rho_t^{\theta_t'}(Z)|\leq K_t\|\theta_t-\theta_t'\|\) uniformly over continuation costs generated by admissible policies, and satisfies \(|\rho_t^{\theta_t}(Z)-\rho_t^{\theta_t}(Z')|\leq\|Z-Z'\|\). If costs and feasible sets are parameter-independent, backward propagation gives \(|v(\theta)-v(\theta')|\leq\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}K_t\|\theta_t-\theta_t'\|\). This value estimate does not imply continuity of optimal policies; policy sensitivity additionally requires regularity of the stagewise argmin mappings, such as uniqueness together with a suitable growth condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform parameter sensitivity and cost nonexpansiveness of the conditional risk mappings propagate to a finite-horizon Lipschitz bound for the optimal value. Policy stability needs additional argmin regularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Parameter Sensitivity
