children.title: Risk-Averse Lower-Bound Families
children.top_down_role: Lower estimators from value approximations, relaxations, or altered probability models.

assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes a finite-horizon nested monotone dynamic-risk functional.
The exact Bellman operators are well defined, and each conditional risk mapping \(\rho_t\) is monotone.
The approximate terminal value satisfies \(\underline V_T\leq V_T\), and each earlier approximation is a Bellman subsolution.
For the restricted-envelope construction, each coherent conditional risk mapping has the stated dual representation and \(\underline{\mathcal Q}_t\subseteq\mathcal Q_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The approximate initial value satisfies \(\underline V_1(x_1)\leq v^*\); restricting a coherent dual risk envelope also produces a lower conditional risk value and hence a valid lower-bound construction when used consistently in the recursion.

notation.meaning: Exact and approximate stage value functions
Exact and restricted dual risk envelopes
Stage-t feasible action set at state x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bellman-subsolution and restricted coherent-risk-envelope certificates for minimization lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Require \(\underline V_T\leq V_T\) and, for \(t=T-1,\ldots,1\), require \(\underline V_t(x)\leq\inf_{a\in A_t(x)}\{c_t(x,a)+\rho_t(\underline V_{t+1}(X_{t+1}))\}\). Monotonicity of each \(\rho_t\) then makes \((\underline V_t)\) a Bellman subsolution and certifies \(\underline V_t\leq V_t\), in particular \(\underline V_1(x_1)\leq v^*\). For a coherent conditional risk mapping with a dual supremum over \(\mathcal Q_t\), replacing that envelope by \(\underline{\mathcal Q}_t\subseteq\mathcal Q_t\) lowers the conditional risk value. Used consistently in the backward recursion, this restricted-envelope construction therefore also yields a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bellman subsolution gives a valid lower bound for a minimization problem with monotone conditional risk mappings. In a coherent dual representation, consistently restricting each risk envelope also lowers the recursive value.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Lower-Bound Families

children.title: Feasible-Policy Upper Bounds
children.top_down_role: Upper estimators based on implementable risk-averse policies.

assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\neq\varnothing\) is a class of implementable nonanticipative policies for a finite-horizon cost-minimization problem.
\(\rho_{0:T}\) is a monotone nested conditional risk functional, and every \(J(\pi)=\rho_{0:T}(C^\pi)\) is finite.

notation.meaning: certified upper bound supplied by a feasible policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-minimization convention; feasibility and exact nested-risk evaluation produce the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\pi\in\Pi\), evaluate its adapted cost stream \(C^\pi=(C_0^\pi,\ldots,C_T^\pi)\) by the prescribed nested conditional-risk recursion and set \(U(\pi)=J(\pi)=\rho_{0:T}(C^\pi)\). Since \(V^*=\inf_{\pi'\in\Pi}J(\pi')\), the pair \((\pi,U(\pi))\) is a feasible-policy upper-bound certificate satisfying \(V^*\le U(\pi)\). If evaluation only establishes \(J(\pi)\le\widehat U\), then \((\pi,\widehat U)\) remains a valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implementable policy evaluated under the same nested risk model gives an upper bound on the optimal risk-adjusted cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Policy Upper Bounds

children.title: Risk-Aware Policy Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Evaluation mechanisms accounting for nonlinear conditional risk and tail sampling.

assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\), \(\pi\) is nonanticipative, and sampled trajectories follow the policy-induced law.
Each one-step conditional risk mapping \(\rho_t\) can be evaluated exactly or by a specified consistent estimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat J_N(\pi)=\widehat V_0\) is the recursively evaluated policy value.

notation.meaning: sampled continuation value at stage t

review_flags: tail-sampling treatment needs an authoritative locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward evaluation of a fixed policy under nested conditional risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a policy \(\pi\), horizon \(T\), and \(N\) policy-induced trajectories. Set each terminal sample value to \(\widehat V_T^{(i)}=C_T^{\pi,(i)}\). For \(t=T-1,\ldots,0\), group samples by the information available at stage \(t\) and compute \(\widehat V_t=C_t^\pi+\widehat\rho_{t,N}(\widehat V_{t+1})\), using conditional samples and any required tail weights. Output \(\widehat J_N(\pi)=\widehat V_0\), together with the sample groups, estimator parameters, and random seed; stop after completing stage \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a fixed policy backward through the nested risk recursion, estimating each conditional risk from appropriately conditioned trajectory samples.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Aware Policy Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the evaluation leaf, but the backward estimator is not mathematically reliable without a specified conditional-risk estimator, conditioning scheme, and assumptions ensuring consistency. The recursion also switches from sample-indexed terminal values to an unindexed stage value without defining how history-dependent sample groups produce values for each information state.

children.title: Statistical Risk Certificates
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based confidence evidence for risk values and policy performance.

assumptions_latex: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) are independent copies of a policy loss \(Z\).
A data-dependent interval \([L_N,U_N]\) has coverage at least \(1-\delta\) for the selected risk functional \(R(Z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr\{L_N\le R(Z)\le U_N\}\ge 1-\delta\)
review_flags: finite-sample construction depends on the selected risk measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite-sample certificate; its interval construction must match the chosen risk measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A statistical risk certificate is the tuple \((Z_{1:N},L_N,U_N,\delta)\), where \([L_N,U_N]\) is measurable with respect to the sample and satisfies \(\Pr\{L_N\le R(Z)\le U_N\}\ge 1-\delta\) under the stated sampling law. For a policy \(\pi\), replacing \(Z\) by its policy-induced loss gives confidence evidence for \(J(\pi)=R(Z^\pi)\). The certificate must record the sampling law, confidence level, risk parameters, and assumptions used to obtain coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A statistical certificate is a reproducible sample-based interval that covers the specified policy risk value with a declared probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Risk Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and coverage formulation fit the leaf, but coverage is assumed rather than supported by a risk-specific finite-sample construction. An authoritative result must identify the admissible risk functional, sampling assumptions, and interval construction.

children.title: Dynamic-Risk Duality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual evidence derived from envelopes and multistage decompositions.

assumptions_latex: Each conditional coherent risk mapping admits an attained envelope representation \(\rho_t(X)=\sup_{q_t\in\mathcal Q_t}\mathbb E[q_tX\mid\mathcal F_t]\).
The policy \(\pi\) is feasible, and the adapted envelope selection \(q=(q_0,\ldots,q_{T-1})\) is feasible for the rectangular multistage envelope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(q)\le V^*\le U(\pi)\)

notation.meaning: primal value of a feasible policy
dual lower value induced by feasible envelope selections and stagewise dual variables

review_flags: exact dual objective depends on the primal dynamic program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract certificate for coherent rectangular dynamic risk; model-specific dual constraints remain necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V^*\) be the minimum nested-risk cost. A dynamic-risk duality certificate consists of a feasible primal policy \(\pi\), adapted envelope densities \(q_t\in\mathcal Q_t\), and any model-specific stagewise dual variables producing a dual-feasible value \(L(q)\). Weak duality and primal feasibility give \(L(q)\le V^*\le U(\pi)=J(\pi)\). Consequently, \(U(\pi)-L(q)\) is a verifiable primal-dual gap; equality certifies optimality when the applicable strong-duality conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible primal and envelope-based dual objects bracket the optimum; a zero certified gap establishes optimality under strong duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Risk Duality Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf, but envelope feasibility alone does not define the claimed dual lower value. The primal model, dual constraints, objective defining L(q), rectangularity assumptions, and applicable weak- and strong-duality result are model-dependent and require an authoritative source.

children.title: Risk-Averse Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Termination diagnostics adapted to risk-adjusted bounds and policy evaluation.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), certified quantities satisfy \(L_k\le V^*\le U_k\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge0\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), and \(s>0\) is a fixed scaling floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{s,|U_k|,|L_k|\}\)

notation.meaning: certified risk-adjusted lower and upper bounds

review_flags: statistical bounds require simultaneous coverage adjustment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic gap test; confidence-qualified bounds require a declared joint coverage event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Terminate at iteration \(k\) when both bounds are valid for the same dynamic-risk objective and \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{s,|U_k|,|L_k|\}\). The returned policy then has certified suboptimality at most the right-hand side. If either bound is statistical, termination is certified only on the stated simultaneous-coverage event; repeated testing must be covered by the confidence construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when compatible risk-adjusted bounds have a sufficiently small absolute-relative gap, with simultaneous coverage when bounds are statistical.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Averse Stopping Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic absolute-relative gap condition is mathematically sound and its condition kind fits the leaf. However, the cited upper-bound section does not specifically support this stopping rule or the claims about simultaneous coverage and repeated testing; those statistical claims require a sequentially valid confidence source.

children.title: Dynamic-Risk Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural sources of computational growth and tractability.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in paths, nodes, and conditional-risk variables.

assumptions_latex: A rooted scenario tree has horizon \(T\) and uniform branching factor \(b\ge2\).
Every nonterminal node carries one local conditional-risk block of fixed size \(r\ge1\).

notation.meaning: number of tree nodes through stage T

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform full tree; recombination, pruning, or stage-dependent branching changes the count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), a full uniformly branching tree contains \(b^t\) nodes and represents \(b^T\) root-to-leaf paths. Hence the total node count is \(N_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T}b^t=(b^{T+1}-1)/(b-1)=\Theta(b^T)\). If each nonterminal node contributes \(r\) scalar variables for its conditional-risk representation, their total is \(R_T=r\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}b^t=r(b^T-1)/(b-1)=\Theta(rb^T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full tree with fixed branching has exponentially many nodes and paths, and nodewise conditional-risk variables inherit that growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Tree Growth

children.title: Risk-Envelope Extreme-Point Growth
children.top_down_role: Computational growth induced by envelope geometry.

assumptions_latex: At a tree node, a polyhedral risk envelope is \(\mathcal Q=\{q\in\mathbb R^m:Aq\le a,\ Bq=b,\ q\ge0\}\).
The envelope is bounded and has affine dimension \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal Q)|\le {p\choose d}\), where \(p\) counts its facet-defining inequalities.
review_flags: degeneracy may make the combinatorial bound loose
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crude combinatorial bound for bounded polyhedral envelopes at one conditional-risk node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every vertex of the bounded \(d\)-dimensional polyhedron \(\mathcal Q\) is determined by at least \(d\) active, linearly independent facet inequalities. Therefore \(|\operatorname{ext}(\mathcal Q)|\le {p\choose d}\). An explicit extreme-point formulation of the nodewise risk mapping may consequently require up to \({p\choose d}\) affine pieces. Across a scenario tree, multiplying this per-node count by the number of nonterminal nodes gives the corresponding storage bound when envelopes are stored independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral risk envelope can have combinatorially many vertices, so explicit extreme-point risk formulations may be large at every tree node.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Envelope Extreme-Point Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, and the combinatorial vertex bound is plausible for a bounded polyhedron considered in its affine hull when p counts actual facets. No source is supplied for the polyhedral bound or for its translation into an extreme-point risk formulation, so candidate acceptance requires authoritative support.

children.title: Tail-Event Sampling Complexity
children.top_down_role: Rare-event and high-variance difficulties in estimating dynamic tail risk.

assumptions_latex: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent Bernoulli indicators of a tail event with probability \(p\in(0,1)\).
The estimator is the empirical frequency \(\widehat p_N=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N X_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: To have \(\Pr\{|\widehat p_N-p|\ge\varepsilon p\}\le\delta\), it suffices that \(N\ge 3\log(2/\delta)/(\varepsilon^2p)\) for \(0<\varepsilon\le1\).
review_flags: extension from event probability to nested tail-risk values needs additional assumptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rare-event baseline; nested risk estimation may compound this burden across stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), a multiplicative concentration bound gives \(\Pr\{|\widehat p_N-p|\ge\varepsilon p\}\le2\exp(-N\varepsilon^2p/3)\). Thus \(N\ge3\log(2/\delta)/(\varepsilon^2p)\) suffices for relative error at most \(\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\). Consequently, plain Monte Carlo requires order \(1/p\) samples merely to resolve an event of probability \(p\); dynamic tail-risk evaluation repeats this difficulty at relevant conditional nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolving a rare tail event to relative accuracy by plain Monte Carlo requires sample size proportional to the inverse event probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Event Sampling Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bernoulli multiplicative concentration calculation is stated precisely and the complexity-bound kind fits the leaf. An authoritative concentration locator is absent, and the extension from estimating one event probability to dynamic conditional tail-risk evaluation needs additional assumptions and support.

children.title: Cut-State Growth Coupling
children.top_down_role: Growth of value approximations under long horizons, dependence, or state augmentation.

children.title: Cut-Pool Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of stored value-function approximations across stages and iterations.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), each of \(M_k\) visited post-decision states may retain at most one newly generated affine cut.
No cut deletion or aggregation is performed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_K\le C_0+\sum_{k=1}^{K}M_k\), and if \(M_k\le M\), then \(C_K=O(KM)\).

notation.meaning: number of stored cuts after K iterations
states producing cuts at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage count for an unpruned multicut scheme generating at most one cut per visited state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If iteration \(k\) adds no more than \(M_k\) cuts, then the unpruned pool satisfies \(C_K\le C_0+\sum_{k=1}^{K}M_k\). Under the uniform bound \(M_k\le M\), storage is \(O(KM)\). Evaluating every stored affine cut once at every currently visited state costs \(O(C_KM)\) scalar affine evaluations per sweep, excluding the cost of solving stage subproblems and optimizing over risk envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without pruning, a multicut pool grows with iterations times cut-generating states, and scanning it can become quadratic in those counts.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Pool Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counting bound is correct under the stated one-cut-per-visited-state and no-pruning assumptions, and the complexity-bound kind fits Cut-Pool Growth. The cut-generation and exhaustive-evaluation model is algorithm-specific, however, and no authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: State-Space Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of the effective state representation over long horizons or dependent processes.

assumptions_latex: A discretized Markov state has \(d\) coordinates, with coordinate \(j\) represented by \(n_j\) grid values.
The dynamic program stores one value or policy entry for every joint grid state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal S|=\prod_{j=1}^{d}n_j\); if \(n_j=n\), storage is \(\Theta(n^d)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tensor-product discretization; sparse, adaptive, or reachable-state representations can reduce storage.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Markov Processes with Arbitrary State Space p. 101

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The tensor-product grid is \(\mathcal S=\prod_{j=1}^{d}\{1,\ldots,n_j\}\), so \(|\mathcal S|=\prod_{j=1}^{d}n_j\). A table storing one scalar at each state therefore requires \(\Theta(\prod_{j=1}^{d}n_j)\) memory. When all coordinates use \(n\) values, the requirement is \(\Theta(n^d)\), exponential in the state dimension \(d\). A full action table multiplies this count by the number of represented actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tensor grid multiplies coordinate resolutions, producing storage exponential in state dimension when each coordinate has the same resolution.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Growth

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Markov Processes with Arbitrary State Space p. 101

children.title: State-Augmentation Burden
children.top_down_role: Computational growth attributable to additional state variables used to recover recursive structure.

assumptions_latex: A Markov representation is augmented by \(r\) risk-memory coordinates.
Augmented coordinate \(\ell\) is discretized with \(m_\ell\) values independently of the original state grid \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\widetilde{\mathcal S}|=|\mathcal S|\prod_{\ell=1}^{r}m_\ell\).

notation.meaning: grid size of risk-memory coordinate ell

review_flags: dynamic-risk augmentation mechanism needs a model-specific source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact count for tensor-product augmentation by discretized risk-memory variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The augmented grid is \(\widetilde{\mathcal S}=\mathcal S\times\prod_{\ell=1}^{r}\{1,\ldots,m_\ell\}\), whence \(|\widetilde{\mathcal S}|=|\mathcal S|\prod_{\ell=1}^{r}m_\ell\). Thus any table-based Bellman representation, state-indexed cut family, or exhaustive state sweep incurs the same multiplicative factor. If \(m_\ell=m\) for every added coordinate, augmentation multiplies the original state count by \(m^r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding discretized risk-memory coordinates multiplies the original state count by the product of their grid sizes.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Augmentation Burden

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product count is correct for the explicitly assumed independent tensor-product augmentation, and the complexity-bound kind fits the leaf. No source establishes when a dynamic-risk model requires these risk-memory coordinates or supports the broader claims about Bellman tables and state-indexed cut families.

children.title: Cut-State Growth Interaction
children.top_down_role: Mutual amplification between enlarged state representations and value-approximation storage.

assumptions_latex: After \(K\) iterations, \(C_K\) affine cuts are stored and evaluated at \(M_K\) represented states.
Evaluating one cut at one state costs \(\Theta(d)\) arithmetic operations in state dimension \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_K=\Theta(dC_KM_K)\) for an exhaustive cut-state sweep.

notation.meaning: arithmetic work of one exhaustive sweep

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense exhaustive evaluation; indexing, pruning, and sampling can avoid the full product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exhaustive sweep evaluates each of \(C_K\) affine cuts at each of \(M_K\) states. With \(\Theta(d)\) arithmetic per cut-state pair, its work is \(W_K=\Theta(dC_KM_K)\), while storing all scalar evaluations requires \(\Theta(C_KM_K)\) memory. Therefore simultaneous growth of the cut pool and represented state set is multiplicative rather than additive for dense evaluation, even when each count separately grows only linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense evaluation couples cut and state growth multiplicatively: every stored cut is tested at every represented state.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-State Growth Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dense exhaustive-sweep count is correct under the stated cost model, and the complexity-bound kind fits the interaction leaf. Because the exact Theta claim depends on representation and implementation choices, an authoritative algorithmic or complexity source is required.

children.title: Nonconvex Dynamic-Risk Complexity
children.top_down_role: Hardness arising from nonconvex risk, integer recourse, or endogenous information.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Dynamic-Risk Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case computational hardness inherited from nonconvex terminal decisions or integer recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider finite-horizon dynamic-risk minimization with explicitly encoded rational data. If the model class permits a deterministic terminal objective that is an arbitrary nonconvex quadratic over a polytope, then the class contains nonconvex quadratic programming as the special case with one stage and identity risk mapping. Likewise, binary recourse contains binary linear feasibility. Consequently, computing a global optimum, or deciding whether the optimal risk-adjusted value is at most a rational threshold, is NP-hard. Nested risk evaluation does not remove this inherited hardness; endogenous information decisions may additionally make the filtration decision-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic-risk optimization is NP-hard whenever its admissible subclasses include nonconvex quadratic optimization or binary recourse; nesting the risk mappings does not eliminate that hardness.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge 1\) is finite and all numerical input is rationally encoded.
The admissible model class contains either nonconvex quadratic terminal optimization or binary linear recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Global dynamic-risk optimization is NP-hard.}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hardness claim fits the terminal container and complexity_bound role, and the special-case reduction is plausible. No citation supports the NP-hardness assertions or the encoding assumptions, so promotion beyond needs_source is not justified.

children.title: Dynamic-Risk Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failures affecting interpretation, statistical reliability, recursive validity, or computational evidence.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Risk Aversion in Multistage Stochastic Programming: A Modeling and Algorithmic Perspective

children.title: Preference-Specification Failures
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between selected dynamic risk families and intended intertemporal preferences.

children.title: Compounding Conservatism
children.top_down_role: Excessive conservatism produced by repeated nesting over long horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Compounding Conservatism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-tree example where repeated worst-case conditioning creates a horizon-growing risk premium.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_1,\ldots,L_T\) be independent Bernoulli losses with \(\mathbb P(L_t=1)=p\in(0,1)\). Use the conditional essential-supremum mapping at every stage and evaluate total loss by nesting these mappings. Every history has a continuation on which all remaining losses equal one, so the nested value is \(T\). The risk-neutral value is \(Tp\); hence the conservatism gap is \(T(1-p)\), which grows linearly with the horizon even though the one-stage loss distribution remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated conditional worst-case evaluation values Bernoulli losses at the all-loss path, producing a conservatism gap that grows linearly with the horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb N\) and \(p\in(0,1)\).
\(L_1,\ldots,L_T\) are independent with \(\mathbb P(L_t=1)=p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{0:T}(\sum_{t=1}^T L_t)-\mathbb E[\sum_{t=1}^T L_t]=T(1-p).\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bernoulli example is mathematically consistent and fits the compounding-conservatism failure boundary. No inspectable source is cited for the nested conditional essential-supremum interpretation or its use as a dynamic-risk failure example.

children.title: Risk-Parameter Instability
children.top_down_role: Abrupt policy variation under small changes in dynamic-risk parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Parameter Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-action threshold example exhibiting discontinuous optimal-policy dependence on a risk-aversion parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let action \(a\) incur loss \(Z_a=M\) with probability \(p\) and zero otherwise, while action \(b\) incurs constant loss \(c\). For \(p\le 1-\beta\), define \(\rho_\lambda(Z)=(1-\lambda)\mathbb E[Z]+\lambda\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z)\). Then \(\rho_\lambda(Z_a)=M[(1-\lambda)p+\lambda p/(1-\beta)]\) and \(\rho_\lambda(Z_b)=c\). Choosing \(c\) equal to the first expression at an interior \(\lambda_*\) makes the unique minimizing action switch across \(\lambda_*\). Thus arbitrarily small parameter changes can produce a discrete policy change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a two-action mean–AVaR model, crossing a single parameter threshold switches the unique optimal action, despite an arbitrarily small parameter perturbation.
assumptions_latex: \(M>0\), \(0<p\le 1-\beta\), and \(\beta,\lambda_*\in(0,1)\).
\(c=M[(1-\lambda_*)p+\lambda_*p/(1-\beta)]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\min_{u\in\{a,b\}}\rho_\lambda(Z_u)=\{a\}\) for \(\lambda<\lambda_*\), while it equals \(\{b\}\) for \(\lambda>\lambda_*\).

notation.meaning: average value-at-risk at confidence level beta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mean-AVaR calculation and threshold switch are correct under the stated assumptions, and countervailing unique optimizers occur on either side of lambda_*. The record nevertheless has no source supporting its characterization as risk-parameter instability.

children.title: Stage-Preference Misalignment
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between local conditional choices and horizon-wide preferences.

knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Preference Misalignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Bellman-optimal local choices when the horizon preference lacks a recursive conditional representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) rank bounded terminal losses on a filtered probability space. A Bellman recursion using conditional mappings \(\rho_t\) represents the horizon preference only if, for every bounded terminal loss \(Z\), \(\mathcal R(Z)=\rho_0(\rho_1(\cdots\rho_{T-1}(Z)\cdots))\), with the mappings satisfying the corresponding time-consistency ordering. If this identity fails, local minimization of the proposed conditional continuation risks optimizes a different functional. Therefore a policy assembled from locally preferred actions need not minimize \(\mathcal R\), and a later self may reject the continuation selected initially.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bellman-local choices match a horizon-wide preference only when that preference has the stated time-consistent recursive representation; otherwise policy disagreement can occur.
assumptions_latex: \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\) is a filtered probability space.
\(\mathcal R\) and each \(\rho_t\) are defined on the required bounded-loss spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R\ne\rho_0\circ\cdots\circ\rho_{T-1}\) implies that local conditional optimality does not generally imply \(\mathcal R\)-optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content fits the stage-preference-misalignment boundary, but the claimed relationship between recursive representation, time-consistency ordering, local optimality, and later rejection depends on precise axioms and domain conditions that are not stated or sourced. A direct time-consistency representation source is required.

children.title: Statistical Tail-Estimation Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by limited tail data or misspecified dynamic dependence.

children.title: Tail-Data Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Instability of conditional-risk estimates under limited tail observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Data Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rare-loss example quantifying catastrophic empirical AVaR underestimation when no tail observation appears.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=M\) with probability \(p\) and \(Z=0\) otherwise, where \(0<p\le 1-\beta\). Its population average value-at-risk is \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z)=pM/(1-\beta)\). From \(N\) independent observations, the event that every observation is zero has probability \((1-p)^N\). On that event the empirical distribution is concentrated at zero, so its empirical average value-at-risk is zero. Thus limited tail data cause an error of \(pM/(1-\beta)\) with probability at least \((1-p)^N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rare Bernoulli loss, observing no tail loss makes empirical AVaR zero although population AVaR is positive; this occurs with probability `(1-p)^N`.
assumptions_latex: \(M>0\), \(0<p\le 1-\beta\), and \(N\in\mathbb N\).
The \(N\) observations are independent copies of \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P\!\left(\widehat{\operatorname{AVaR}}_{\beta,N}=0\right)\ge(1-p)^N\), while \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z)=pM/(1-\beta)>0\).

notation.meaning: AVaR of the empirical distribution from N observations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The population AVaR, no-tail-observation probability, and resulting empirical error are correct for the stated two-point distribution. The failure example has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Dynamic Dependence Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Incorrect risk evaluation caused by misspecified interstage dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Dependence Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equal stagewise marginals can yield different tail risk under different interstage dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_1,L_2\) each have Bernoulli marginal \(\mathbb P(L_t=1)=p\), where \(0<p\le 1/2\). Under the comonotone model set \(L_1=L_2\); under the mutually exclusive model impose \(L_1L_2=0\) and \(\mathbb P(L_1+L_2=1)=2p\). Both models have identical stagewise marginals. For \(\beta>1-p\), however, \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(L_1+L_2)=2\) in the comonotone model and equals \(1\) in the mutually exclusive model. Marginal calibration alone therefore cannot identify dynamic tail risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two loss processes with identical stagewise Bernoulli marginals have AVaR values two and one because their interstage dependence differs.
assumptions_latex: Both dependence models preserve \(\mathbb P(L_t=1)=p\) for \(t=1,2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta^{\mathrm{com}}(L_1+L_2)=2\ne1=\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta^{\mathrm{excl}}(L_1+L_2).\)

notation.meaning: average value-at-risk at confidence level beta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both dependence constructions preserve the Bernoulli marginals, and the stated AVaR values follow when beta>1-p. The counterexample fits the container, but no source supports the dependence-misspecification claim.

children.title: Tail Distortion under Scenario Reduction
children.top_down_role: Loss of risk-relevant paths or conditional tail structure during scenario compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail Distortion under Scenario Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deleting a small-probability extreme scenario can erase the entire upper-tail risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original loss distribution assign probability \(p\) to \(M>0\) and probability \(1-p\) to zero, with \(p\ge1-\beta\). A scenario-reduction rule that deletes the loss scenario and transfers its mass to zero produces the reduced distribution \(\delta_0\). The original and reduced distributions differ by total-variation distance \(p\), yet their average value-at-risk values are \(M\) and \(0\), respectively. Hence when \(\beta\) is close to one, removing arbitrarily small probability mass can cause maximal relative distortion of the relevant tail risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a rare extreme scenario can change AVaR from the full loss magnitude to zero, even when the deleted probability mass is arbitrarily small.
assumptions_latex: The removed mass \(p\) is reassigned to the zero-loss scenario.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(P)=M\), whereas \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(\delta_0)=0\) and \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,\delta_0)=p\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-point counterexample, total-variation distance, and AVaR distortion are correct under p>=1-beta. No scenario-reduction or tail-risk source is attached.

children.title: Computational Validation Failures
children.top_down_role: Situations in which familiar risk-neutral diagnostics do not provide valid evidence.

children.title: Biased Risk Upper Estimators
children.top_down_role: Bias arising from nonlinear risk evaluation of sampled policy costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Biased Risk Upper Estimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A plug-in nonlinear risk estimate need not be unbiased or constitute an upper estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=M\) with probability \(p\) and zero otherwise, with \(p\ge1-\beta\). Then \(\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z)=M\). For a one-observation empirical distribution, the plug-in estimator is \(\widehat R_1=Z_1\), because the empirical distribution is a point mass. Consequently \(\mathbb E[\widehat R_1]=pM<M\), and \(\widehat R_1=0<M\) with probability \(1-p\). Thus nonlinear risk evaluation of sampled policy costs can be downward biased and cannot be treated as a valid risk upper bound without a separate finite-sample correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sample empirical AVaR of a rare-loss policy has expectation `pM`, below the true value `M`, and is not a valid upper estimator.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_1\) is one independent observation from the law of \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widehat R_1]=pM<\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z)=M\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sample plug-in AVaR calculation correctly demonstrates downward bias and failure of an uncorrected upper-estimator interpretation. The counterexample fits the terminal container but lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Rare-Tail Coverage Failure
children.top_down_role: Failure to sample scenarios dominating the risk-adjusted objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Rare-Tail Coverage Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sample-size condition for observing at least one risk-dominating rare event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each independently sampled validation path enters a risk-dominating tail event \(A\) with probability \(p\in(0,1)\). The probability that \(N\) paths provide no coverage of \(A\) is \((1-p)^N\). Therefore coverage with probability at least \(1-\delta\) is equivalent to \((1-p)^N\le\delta\), or \(N\ge\log(\delta)/\log(1-p)\). If this condition fails, the validation sample misses every path in \(A\) with probability exceeding \(\delta\), irrespective of the magnitude of losses on that event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At least `log(delta)/log(1-p)` independent paths are necessary and sufficient to observe a probability-`p` tail event with confidence `1-delta`.
assumptions_latex: \(0<p<1\), \(0<\delta<1\), and \(N\in\mathbb N\).
Validation paths are independent and each intersects \(A\) with probability \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\text{at least one sampled path lies in }A)\ge1-\delta\iff N\ge\lceil\log(\delta)/\log(1-p)\rceil.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The independent-path coverage probability and exact integer sample-size condition are correct, and condition is an appropriate content kind. No cited source supports the sampling condition in the dynamic-risk validation context.

children.title: Invalid Transfer of Risk-Neutral Bounds
children.top_down_role: Use of estimators or bounds whose validity does not survive nonlinear dynamic risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Transfer of Risk-Neutral Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A mean-confidence bound can severely understate AVaR on a rare-loss distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in[0,M]\) equal \(M\) with probability \(p\) and zero otherwise, where \(p\ge1-\beta\). On an all-zero sample of size \(N\), a one-sided Hoeffding upper bound for the mean is \(U_N=M\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)/(2N)}\). If \(N>\log(1/\delta)/2\), then \(U_N<M=\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z)\). The all-zero event has probability \((1-p)^N\); whenever this exceeds \(\delta\), the transferred risk-neutral bound fails to cover AVaR at its advertised confidence level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid concentration bound for the mean can fall below true AVaR with probability above its nominal error level, so it cannot be transferred unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(N>\log(1/\delta)/2\) and \((1-p)^N>\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(U_N<\operatorname{AVaR}_\beta(Z))\ge(1-p)^N>\delta.\)

notation.meaning: one-sided Hoeffding upper confidence bound for the mean on an all-zero sample

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The all-zero-sample argument plausibly shows that a mean confidence bound need not cover AVaR, and the counterexample fits the container. A source is required both for the precise one-sided Hoeffding construction and for the claimed invalidity of transferring it to nonlinear risk.

children.title: Structural Decomposition Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of separability or recursive tractability caused by model structure.

children.title: Nondecomposable Risk Envelopes
children.top_down_role: Cross-stage model coupling preventing local envelope recursion.

knowledge_statements.title: Nondecomposable Risk Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonrectangular joint ambiguity prevents exact construction from independent conditional envelope choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a finite scenario tree, let \(\mathcal Q\) be a convex set of joint probability measures and define \(R(Z)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_Q[Z]\). A nested conditional-envelope recursion represents \(R\) for every bounded terminal loss only when the envelope is rectangular: admissible conditional kernels can be selected independently at each history and pasted into an admissible joint measure. If \(\mathcal Q\) is not closed under such pasting, there exists a bounded terminal loss for which the nested supremum over local conditional envelopes differs from \(R(Z)\); stagewise decomposition is then invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint risk envelope supports exact nested recursion only under rectangularity; failure of closure under conditional pasting yields some loss with a different recursive value.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and horizon are finite.
\(\mathcal Q\) is a nonempty convex set of joint probability measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal Q\text{ nonrectangular}\implies\exists Z\in L^\infty:\ R(Z)\ne R_{\mathrm{nested}}(Z).\)

notation.meaning: value obtained by nested local envelope maximization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted rectangularity-pasting principle matches the nondecomposable-envelope container, but its necessity statement depends on how local conditional envelopes are derived and on the exact representation theorem. Those details are not fully specified, and no authoritative source is cited.

children.title: Nonconvex Risk-Mapping Failure
children.top_down_role: Loss of convex value geometry and standard cutting-plane validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Risk-Mapping Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A lower-envelope risk mapping destroys convexity and invalidates tangent cuts as global lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two probability measures evaluate a decision-dependent loss as \(\mathbb E_{Q_1}[Z(x)]=x\) and \(\mathbb E_{Q_2}[Z(x)]=-x\) for \(x\in[-1,1]\). Define the nonconvex risk mapping \(\rho(Z)=\min\{\mathbb E_{Q_1}[Z],\mathbb E_{Q_2}[Z]\}\). The resulting value function is \(V(x)=\min\{x,-x\}=-|x|\), which is not convex. At any \(x_0>0\), the active affine branch gives the tangent \(\ell(x)=-x\), but \(\ell(x)>V(x)\) for every \(x<0\). Hence the standard convex cutting-plane construction does not produce a valid global lower approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum of two expected-loss mappings yields `-|x|`; its active affine tangent exceeds the value elsewhere, invalidating convex lower cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E_{Q_1}[Z(x)]=x\) and \(\mathbb E_{Q_2}[Z(x)]=-x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=-|x|\) is nonconvex, and for \(x_0>0\), \(\ell(x)=-x>V(x)\) whenever \(x<0\).

notation.meaning: affine cut from the active branch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-envelope construction yields V(x)=-|x|, and the active affine branch fails as a global lower cut exactly as stated. The counterexample fits the structural failure container but has no supporting citation.

children.title: Hidden History Dependence
children.top_down_role: Apparent Markov recursion omitting risk-relevant information from the state.

assumptions_latex: A finite-horizon filtered control model is defined on \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T,\mathbb P)\).
The proposed state satisfies \(S_t=\phi_t(H_t)\), where \(H_t\) is the observable history.
The conditional risk mapping \(\rho_t\) evaluates bounded continuation losses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No exact value function depending only on \(S_t\) exists unless the state is augmented or the discrepancy vanishes for every admissible continuation.

notation.meaning: compressed state used by the proposed recursion
conditional risk mapping at time t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon failure criterion for a state compression that is insufficient for conditional risk evaluation.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 A Simple Modeling Framework for Dynamic Programs p. 50

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Hidden history dependence occurs at time \(t\) if there exist reachable histories \(h_t\) and \(h'_t\) with \(\phi_t(h_t)=\phi_t(h'_t)\), together with an admissible continuation policy \(\pi\) and its bounded continuation loss \(Z^\pi\), such that \[\rho_t(Z^\pi\mid H_t=h_t)\ne \rho_t(Z^\pi\mid H_t=h'_t).\] Consequently, there is no function \(V_t\) of the compressed state alone satisfying \(V_t(\phi_t(h))=\rho_t(Z^\pi\mid H_t=h)\) for both histories. A Bellman recursion indexed only by \(S_t\) therefore fails to represent the conditional risk evaluation exactly; validity requires state augmentation or risk-sufficiency of \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressed state is inadequate when two histories mapped to it produce different conditional risks for the same continuation, preventing an exact state-only Bellman recursion.
knowledge_statements.title: Hidden History Dependence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 A Simple Modeling Framework for Dynamic Programs p. 50

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Powell §2.4 supports state modeling in dynamic programs but does not specifically support conditional risk sufficiency or the stated failure criterion. Moreover, differing risk evaluations for one fixed continuation loss rule out a state-only representation of that evaluation, but do not by themselves rule out coincidence of optimized value functions. Evaluation conditional on H_t=h_t also requires a well-defined historywise conditional-risk kernel, especially for null histories. A risk-specific source and corrected conclusion are required.

children.title: Risk-Adjusted Recourse Failure
children.top_down_role: Loss of feasible continuation under risk constraints or conditional model distortions.

assumptions_latex: At a reachable history \(h_t\), the physically feasible continuation set \(\mathcal U_t(h_t)\) is nonempty.
Each continuation \(u\in\mathcal U_t(h_t)\) induces bounded constraint losses \(G_{t+1}^j(u)\).
Conditional risk constraints have thresholds \(b_t^j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Risk-adjusted recourse fails precisely when \(\mathcal U_t(h_t)\ne\varnothing\) but \(\mathcal U_t^{\rho}(h_t)=\varnothing\); the risk-constrained continuation value is then \(+\infty\).

notation.meaning: physically feasible continuations after history h_t
continuations satisfying all conditional risk constraints
j-th future constraint loss induced by continuation u

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of relatively complete recourse after imposing conditional risk constraints at a reachable history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the risk-feasible continuation set at a reachable history \(h_t\) by \[\mathcal U_t^{\rho}(h_t)=\left\{u\in\mathcal U_t(h_t):\rho_t\bigl(G_{t+1}^j(u)\bigr)\le b_t^j\ \text{for every }j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\] Risk-adjusted recourse fails at \(h_t\) when \(\mathcal U_t(h_t)\ne\varnothing\) but \(\mathcal U_t^{\rho}(h_t)=\varnothing\). Thus physical recourse exists, yet every continuation is rejected by at least one conditional risk constraint. With the extended-value convention, minimization over \(\mathcal U_t^{\rho}(h_t)\) has value \(+\infty\), and any policy reaching \(h_t\) cannot remain risk feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Risk-adjusted recourse fails when physical continuations exist at a reachable history but every one violates at least one conditional risk constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Adjusted Recourse Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and empty risk-feasible-set criterion fit the terminal container, but Pflug §1.1.1 is cited only for recourse problems and does not establish this conditional-risk formulation. The definition also needs explicit historywise evaluation of the F_t-measurable conditional risk quantity, or a stated convention that rho_t(G)(h_t) is meant. A source specifically covering dynamic conditional risk constraints and recourse failure is required.
